contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFSPREAD settles YES if the named team wins the game by more than the half-point strike (for example Florida Atlantic by more than 41.5 versus UTSA) on the official final result (the sampled SPREAD text never says whether overtime counts; including overtime is assumed because FBS games cannot end tied, unverified); KXNCAAFGAME and KXNCAAFCSGAME have no sampled rules, and their winner/no-tie treatment is inferred from the absence of ties in FBS play, not read. KXNCAAFWINMARGIN settles on bucketed final point differential including overtime. A postponed game that starts within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official result; if not started within 48 hours the market resolves to a fair price. The archetype also holds season-level count markets (conference teams reaching 10 wins, any Division I game above a total) whose settlement is regular-season-only.

rules_evidence.quote: If Florida Atlantic wins by more than 41.5 points in the UTSA vs Florida Atlantic college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: Spread rung is a strict greater-than on a .5 strike, so no push exists and the question is P(margin >= 42).

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponement under 48 hours does not void; after 48 hours the same rules text resolves to a fair price, so weather and scheduling delays matter only if they cross that line.

rules_evidence.quote: Between 7 to 14 points against Miami (FL) in the Full game (including overtime)
rules_evidence.establishes: Margin buckets use the full game including overtime, so an overtime game caps the winner margin through the extra period score.

rules_evidence.quote: Only wins recorded in the 2026 college football regular season count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Conference win-count markets are regular-season only and exclude title game, bowl and CFP wins.

rules_evidence.quote: If there is a Division I game (including overtime) with over 144.5 total points scored
rules_evidence.establishes: Season-extreme market over all Division I games including FCS and overtime, an extreme-value event not a single-game side.

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNCAAFGAME and KXNCAAFCSGAME (FBS and FCS winner markets) have no sampled rules text: whether the winner market is full-game including overtime is assumed from the absence of ties, not read.
KXNCAAFWINMARGIN buckets are custom strike_type (Notre Dame by 7 to 14); inclusive boundaries at 7 and 14 are inferred from the title, not from stated rounding text.

Conference-win markets (KXNCAAFSECWINS, BIGTENWINS, BIG12WINS, ACCWINS) resolve on a count of teams with 10+ wins, so they depend on every conference game and schedule, not on one matchup; these are season-futures in nature but filed under this archetype.
KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE is an extreme-value contract over every Division I game (FBS vs FCS mismatches included) and counts overtime points; it is not a single-game side.
A postponed game that starts after 48 hours resolves to a fair price rather than void, so exposure to weather postponements is capped but non-zero.

KXNCAAFSPREAD rules text says only 'wins by more than 41.5 points' and resolution 'based on the official final result' after a postponement; overtime inclusion is not stated (contrast KXNCAAFWINMARGIN 'Full game (including overtime)'). Treated as unverified.
contract.settlement_data_source: Kalshi text cites the official final result of the game; the specific Source Agency or stats provider is not named in the sampled rules for the game markets. NCAA and conference box scores are the likely truth, but the exact provider is unresolved.

mechanism.summary: Final margin = true strength difference (opponent-adjusted offense and defense, each uncertain) + site effect + situational and availability shifts, plus a game-level noise term whose size grows with fewer possessions, high variance styles and weather. College football has thin connectivity, a very wide spread of team strength (spreads above 30 are common), and no reliable injury feed, so the prior and its uncertainty matter as much as the mean. The realized margin is then truncated and reshaped by script: favourites with big leads pull starters and run clock, trailing teams chase, and scoring comes in lumps of 3, 6, 7 and 8, so probabilities at adjacent half-point rungs differ by key-number mass. Moneyline settles on the winner after overtime (no ties), spread rungs on margin including overtime.

stages.name: Team-strength prior and its uncertainty
stages.description: Each team's true strength is a latent opponent-adjusted offensive and defensive efficiency, estimated from last season (shrunk by returning production, portal net gains and recruiting talent) and updated through the year. Connectivity across the 130-plus FBS teams is thin, so a Group-of-Five team's rating relative to a Power team is calibrated by few cross-conference games. The width of the estimate, not just its centre, matters for P(cover).
stages.distribution: Latent Gaussian rating with prior SD roughly 5-6 points in week 0 shrinking toward 2-3 by midseason; mean-reverting, heavy-tailed for teams with massive roster churn.

stages.name: Availability and personnel substitution
stages.description: Starting quarterback, offensive line and a handful of high-snap defenders determine the actual units on the field. Information is released late and partially (there is no mandatory injury report in most conferences), so what matters is both the expected points value of each loss and the vintage at which it became knowable. A quarterback swap is a discrete shift with a wide posterior on the replacement.
stages.distribution: Discrete shocks (zero most weeks, 3-10 point magnitude for a QB) with a mixture of confirmed and doubtful states; replacement quality is itself uncertain.

stages.name: Site, travel, weather and motivation adjustments
stages.description: A home-field term that differs by team (crowd, altitude, visiting travel and body clock), neutral-site games where it vanishes, short-week or bye effects, and games with unusual stakes such as rivalry, bowl eligibility or opt-outs. Weather mostly changes the variance and the run-pass balance of the game rather than the mean margin.
stages.distribution: Mostly small additive shifts (0.5-3 points) with a few large conditional ones (altitude visitors, bowl opt-outs); weather widens variance.

stages.name: Matchup-specific scoring process and variance
stages.description: Two teams of equal rating can produce different margin distributions: a pressure defence against a thin line, an explosive passing attack against a poor secondary, a run-heavy slow offence that shortens the game. Possession count and play style set how many independent scoring trials there are, which controls margin variance and thus underdog cover frequency, and head-coach aggression bends the tail of late scoring.
stages.distribution: Margin variance scales roughly with the number of possessions; style pairings create heteroscedastic, skewed margin errors rather than mean shifts.

stages.name: Game-script truncation and score lattice
stages.description: Once a lead exceeds roughly three scores, college coaches substitute starters, run the ball and burn clock, and trailing teams score late garbage points, so realized margins compress at high spreads relative to a Gaussian. Football scoring is lumpy (3, 6, 7, 8), producing mass on margins of 3, 7, 10 and 14 and differences between rungs such as 6.5 and 7.5. The final result includes overtime, which cannot end tied.
stages.distribution: Truncated, key-number-lumpy margin distribution with a right tail that depends on opponent class (FBS vs FCS) and on coach behaviour.

stages.name: Contract mechanics and aggregate-contract variants
stages.description: The rung is a strict greater-than on a .5 strike, a postponement of under 48 hours keeps the market open, and over 48 hours produces a fair-price resolution. Conference win-count and highest-score contracts in this archetype are not single-game sides; they aggregate over a full schedule or over every Division I game and need the game-level distribution run many times. Inputs for the aggregate series are cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence (correlated schedule simulation) and cfb.season_max_total_tail (extreme-value fit); the series are mis-filed here and listed in contract.series_mapping_issues, so any claim about them is conditional on the future split.
stages.distribution: Binary payoff for sides; for season counts, a Poisson-binomial over game win probabilities; for the highest-score contract, a maximum over roughly 850 game totals.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted efficiency, talent and returning production feed the latent rating; rating_posterior_sd adds the uncertainty term the existing set lacked.

opponent_matchup.note: Unit-on-unit matchups; value is in crosses (rush rate vs protection) not levels.

role_personnel.note: Replacement quality at quarterback and snap-weighted loss across positions.

availability_news.note: Coverage rests on timestamped quarterback status, snap-weighted availability loss and eligibility news; cfb.injuries is WEAK (no official feed in most conferences) and removed, the feed gap is listed as injury_feed_gap.

coaching_scheme.note: Aggression and clock management plus scheme identity; coach-change resets are an open definition issue.

environment.note: Home field, altitude, neutral site and weather; kickoff body-clock effects are not separately defined.

game_context_script.note: Starter-removal and clock behaviour truncate large margins.

pace_volume.note: Possession count and tempo are measured by cfb.pace (seconds per play, plays per game, no-huddle rate) and cfb.drives (drives per game, plays per drive), crossed with offense_style and clock behaviour; the combined possession count sets margin variance.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-play efficiency with a luck adjustment for fumble recoveries.

distribution_variance.note: Margin SD, truncation and key-number mass.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry, bowl eligibility and opt-outs.

officiating_rules.note: Crew penalty tendencies move a game by about one or two penalties and under a point of margin; the one rule-driven item that matters (targeting ejection) is carried by cfb.suspension_eligibility, so no separate officiating input is justified for sides.

settlement_contract.note: Strict greater-than rungs, overtime inclusion and 48-hour postponement rule read from the sampled rules; ML and FCS series text is missing.

cfb.qb_replacement_value.label: Quarterback replacement value in points
cfb.qb_replacement_value.mechanism: Converts a confirmed or doubtful quarterback change into an expected-margin shift in points per game.
cfb.qb_replacement_value.rationale: Identity of the starter (cfb.qb_status_pit) is a vintage, not a number. A backup with 40 career dropbacks has a very wide EPA/play posterior, so the swap cost is both a mean shift and a variance increase; the market tends to over- or under-react depending on prior-year snaps.
cfb.qb_replacement_value.measurement: For each team-season, starter value = EPA per dropback (incl. designed rushes) over the last 2 seasons, opponent-adjusted, weighted by dropbacks with a 1-season half-life, shrunk to the recruiting-class prior (247/On3 composite rating mapped to expected EPA/play from historical FBS QBs) with k = 150 dropbacks. Swap value = (starter - replacement) EPA/dropback x team dropbacks per game (about 35 to 45) x 0.75 points per EPA-equivalent play; report mean and posterior SD. As-of timestamp = last confirmed depth-chart or beat-report vintage before kickoff.
free_sources: CFBD plays and PPA endpoints (free key)
raw_data: play-by-play with passer id, EPA, dropbacks
cfb.qb_replacement_value.why: Quarterback change is the biggest discrete news item in a college spread, and the replacement pool is thin and unevenly observed, so a point value with uncertainty is required, not just a flag.

cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.label: Snap-weighted availability loss
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.mechanism: Aggregates all known absences (any position) into a single points-per-game value using snap share times player value over replacement.
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.rationale: College injury information is sparse, so the model needs a way to price a partial list (two starting linemen out, a corner doubtful) consistently; counting injuries is wrong because snap load and positional value differ by factors of five or more.
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.measurement: For each missing or doubtful player i: loss_i = P(out_i) x snap_share_i(prior season or current season to date) x (grade_i - grade_replacement_pos) x positional_points_per_grade, with positional weights fitted from historical snap-weighted ratings (QB >> OT/CB > WR/DL > RB/TE/S). Sum over players, subtract nothing for the opponent. P(out) = 1.0 for confirmed out, 0.5 for doubtful or questionable, 0.15 for unreported-but-flagged. Grades from PFF where available, otherwise PPA-on-field proxy. Timestamp each source report.
free_sources: CFBD player usage and season stats (free key)
raw_data: player snaps by game (PFF or proxy)
cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss.why: Turns an unstructured injury list into the same unit as the spread, so a +/- 1.5 point late shift can be compared with the quote move rather than judged qualitatively.

cfb.rating_posterior_sd.label: Team-rating posterior standard deviation
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.mechanism: Per-team uncertainty about true strength given games played, connectivity and roster churn; sets the width of the margin distribution.
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.rationale: A rating gap of 7 with SDs of 2.0 and 2.0 gives a different win probability than the same gap with SDs of 5.0 and 5.0 early in the season; ignoring estimation error makes September favourites look too safe and moves cover probabilities at every rung.
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.measurement: Bayesian state-space rating per team: prior mean from last season rating x returning-production shrinkage, prior SD 6 points at week 0 falling toward 2.5 by week 10 per the observed rating update; implement as posterior variance = 1 / (1/prior_var + n_eff / game_sd^2) with game_sd = 13 points and n_eff = sum of connectivity-weighted game weights. Add portal-churn variance inflation proportional to 1 - returning production. Use margin-difference SD sqrt(sd_home^2 + sd_away^2 + 13^2 x (1 + 0.3 x pace_variance_term)).
free_sources: CFBD games and returning production (free key)
cfb.rating_posterior_sd.why: Margin SD and the shape of P(cover) across rungs depend on rating uncertainty, which no existing input supplies.

cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.label: Large-spread cover curve from non-market rating gap
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.mechanism: Empirical probability that the favourite's margin exceeds k, as a function of pre-game rating gap and opponent class (FBS vs FCS, G5 vs P4).
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.rationale: Rungs such as FAU by more than 41.5 sit in a regime where starters are removed, the clock runs and margin growth is truncated; a Gaussian around the rating gap overstates the tail, and the truncation point differs for FCS opponents and for coaches who keep scoring.
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.measurement: From historical FBS games (2014 onward), bin pre-game rating gap (non-market, SP+ or own rating) in 3-point buckets; for each bucket compute the empirical survival function P(margin >= k) for k in {1..60} with isotonic smoothing and a beta prior of strength 30 games on the pooled curve. Estimate separate curves for FCS opponents, neutral site, and for coaches in the top and bottom tercile of historical starter-pull time. Output is a vector of probabilities per rung, evaluated as-of kickoff.
cfb.mismatch_cover_curve.why: The sampled KXNCAAFSPREAD and KXNCAAFWINMARGIN rungs reach 41.5 and 7-14 buckets; probabilities across 40 rungs must come from a calibrated truncated distribution, not a normal.

cfb.fourth_down_aggression.label: Fourth-down aggression and clock-management index
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.mechanism: Coach tendency to go for it, onside, and to run or save clock, which changes margin variance and end-of-game scoring.
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.rationale: Aggressive coaches convert field goals into possible touchdowns or turnovers on downs, widening the margin distribution; conservative leaders reduce late scoring. Two teams of equal rating but different aggression produce different cover rates for a rung.
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.measurement: For each head coach, 4th-down go-for-it rate over expected from a fitted model (yard line, distance, score diff, time) = observed go rate - model go rate for the same situations, computed over last 2 seasons with k = 40 situations shrinkage; add mean seconds of clock burned per play when leading by 8-24 in Q4 versus the conference median. Coach change resets to a coach-career prior; compute as-of week.
raw_data: play-by-play down, distance, yard line, score, time
cfb.fourth_down_aggression.why: Coaching_scheme was uncovered for sides; aggression and clock management bend the margin distribution without changing its mean.

cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.label: Conference schedule grid and correlated win-count simulation inputs
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.mechanism: For the count-of-teams-with-10+-wins contracts: the conference game grid (who plays whom, home/away, byes) plus non-conference opponents define each team win probability vector, and shared rating uncertainty plus intra-conference head-to-head games make team outcomes dependent.
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.rationale: The count is not a Poisson-binomial of independent teams: every intra-conference game gives one team a win and another a loss, so wins are negatively dependent within the conference, while a shared conference-strength error (cross-conference calibration) makes them positively dependent. The two forces change the variance of the count and therefore the tail rung (5+ Big 12, 7+ Big Ten, 8+ SEC). Regular season only, so championship games and bowls are excluded from the count.
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.measurement: For each conference, take the 2026 schedule as of the as-of date: for every game g compute P(home win) from a non-market rating difference (cfb.sp_plus or own rating) plus venue term, with each team rating drawn once per simulation from N(rating, cfb.rating_posterior_sd^2) and a conference-level shift drawn from N(0, tau_c^2) with tau_c estimated from the historical dispersion of cross-conference results (start tau_c=1.5 points, to be fitted). Simulate 20,000 seasons, count teams with >=10 regular-season wins (FCS opponents count as wins) and read P(count>=K). Re-run weekly using results to date as fixed; report the simulated count variance against the independent-Poisson-binomial variance as a diagnostic.
free_sources: CFBD games and schedule endpoints (free key)
raw_data: conference schedule grid by season (team, opponent, site, week)
team rating and rating SD as-of date
cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence.why: KXNCAAFSECWINS, BIGTENWINS, BIG12WINS and ACCWINS (sampled rungs 8+, 7+, 5+ teams with 10+ wins, regular season only per the rules text) need a joint schedule simulation, not a single-game margin model.

cfb.season_max_total_tail.label: Season maximum-total tail model across all Division I games
cfb.season_max_total_tail.mechanism: KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE settles on the single largest combined score over every Division I regular-season game including overtime, so it is an extreme-value quantity of roughly 850 game totals, driven by FBS-vs-FCS mismatches, multi-overtime games and pace-and-defence-poor matchups.
cfb.season_max_total_tail.rationale: The rung 144.5 sits far in the tail; the maximum total is governed by rare pairings (two fast, weak defences, or a long overtime game where each overtime adds up to 8 points) rather than the mean total. A Gaussian game-total model badly understates it, so the tail needs an empirical or Poisson-compound fit with a separate overtime-length component.
cfb.season_max_total_tail.measurement: Collect the maximum regular-season Division I total per season 2005-2025 (FBS and FCS games, including overtime) and the full set of per-game totals above 100. Fit a generalised Pareto tail to game totals above 95 points with a threshold chosen by mean-excess plot; scale the exceedance rate by the number of games (about 850 FBS-involved and more with FCS-FCS games) and add a multi-overtime component: P(k overtimes) from cfb.ot_model, with 2-point-only possessions after the second overtime. Output P(max total > K) for K in 120..160 and the number of games expected above 100. As-of date uses only completed seasons plus current-season games already played.
free_sources: CFBD games (FBS and some FCS, free key)
raw_data: final scores with overtime periods by game 2005 onward
scheduled pairings of the current season
cfb.season_max_total_tail.why: The sampled KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE rule is a Division I maximum including overtime, regular season only; one favourite game cannot price it.

cfb.market_ratings.reason: A rating backed out of sportsbook or Kalshi prices already contains QB, weather and injury news; feeding it into a model that is then compared with the same price removes any chance of finding incremental information. Keep only as the comparator for edge measurement.

cfb.sp_plus.reason: SP+ is an opponent-adjusted, tempo-free rating with a preseason prior built partly from recruiting and returning production, so it is correlated with cfb.talent and cfb.roster_continuity; useful as a second independent strength estimate but must be lagged to the pre-kickoff publication date, not the season-end value.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Opponent-adjusted offensive PPA is the structural scoring component of the margin, but the label bundles PPA, success rate and explosiveness; needs pass/rush splits, garbage-time filtering and a decay window, otherwise blowout-inflated plays overstate teams that beat weak opponents badly.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Defensive counterpart of off_ppa with the same caveats (garbage time, FCS and low-connectivity opponents); also double counts part of pass_rush, secondary_coverage and run_defense, so those matchup rows should be modelled as deviations from this baseline, not added to it.

cfb.cross_conf_calibration.reason: Needed because 12-game schedules inside 10 conferences give thin connectivity; matters most for Group-of-Five vs Power-conference games and early-season Week 1-4 ratings, nearly irrelevant by November within a conference.

cfb.talent.reason: Recruiting composite gives a prior on depth and ceiling that is informative in September and decays as in-season efficiency accumulates; its weight should be a declining function of games played, which the label does not state.

cfb.roster_continuity.reason: Returning production regresses last year's rating toward the mean and drives the early-season prior width; overlaps with cfb.transfer_roster which is its portal-adjusted extension, so the two should be merged into one net-production measure.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Starting QB identity with vintage is the single largest discrete late-news term in college spreads; however it supplies only identity, not the points value of the swap, which is why cfb.qb_replacement_value is added.

cfb.injuries.reason: No official injury report exists in most conferences, so as defined this input is a wish rather than a feed; it only becomes usable with a self-captured, timestamped news archive, and even then coverage is partial.

cfb.ol.reason: Offensive-line continuity (starts together, games missed) is a real driver of sack rate and rush efficiency; the label also lumps in the defensive line, which duplicates pass_rush and run_defense and should be split out.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Fumble recovery is close to a coin flip (about 50 percent) so results-based ratings over-credit lucky teams; a regression-to-expected adjustment to rating is valid but only matters for teams with extreme turnover margin.

cfb.venue.reason: Home-field value is team-specific (altitude, crowd, travel for the visitor) and absent at neutral sites; keep, but split neutral-site flag, altitude and visiting-team time-zone shift into separate fields.

cfb.rest_travel.reason: Bye-week and short-week effects are real but small, around a point at most, and are partly priced; keep as a context adjustment, not a primary driver.

cfb.motivation.reason: Rivalry, bowl eligibility and clinched or eliminated status shift effort and lineup choices in specific games; partial knowability and a thin sample of comparable situations mean the coefficient will be noisy.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Matters for large-spread rungs, where starters are pulled and clock is run, compressing the favourite's margin below what ratings imply; the effect is coach-specific and needs a measured pull-point, not an assumption.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind and precipitation mostly move totals; for the margin it changes variance and slightly favours the run-heavy side, so it is context for sides rather than a primary driver.

cfb.score_resid.reason: Defined as residuals around lines, so it is market-derived; the non-market content (mass at margins 3, 7, 10, 14) is carried by cfb.mismatch_cover_curve and rating_posterior_sd, so score_resid is removed from stage and coverage wiring.

m.external_lines.reason: De-vigged sportsbook sides are the reference price to beat, not an input; use them to measure whether a fundamentals estimate adds information and to detect Kalshi staleness after news.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung consistency of the spread ladder (KXNCAAFSPREAD rungs) is an arbitrage and staleness diagnostic derived from prices; it says nothing about game outcome.

cfb.transfer_roster.reason: Portal arrivals reshape starters before the season and eligibility rulings can land mid-year; mostly a preseason prior input and effectively merged with roster_continuity once week 4 has passed.

cfb.opt_out_departures.reason: Only relevant for bowl and CFP games and for four-game redshirt decisions; regular-season sides rungs are unaffected, so keep as a conditional input for postseason games.

cfb.suspension_eligibility.reason: Suspensions and targeting first-half ejections remove players for part of a game; low frequency and partial knowability, but when known pregame (named suspension) it is a clean availability shock.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is the market's own output; it measures when information was absorbed (useful for timing studies and closing-line value) but is not a cause of the game side outcome and must not enter a fundamentals model.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread govern whether a game side edge is tradable, not whether the event occurs; keep for execution and sizing, not as an outcome input.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule changes net edge on game side contracts (largest near 50c) but has no causal link to the result; an execution parameter, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe liquidity and price reliability for game side quotes; useful to weight benchmark trust, irrelevant to the outcome process.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades show informed flow and fill realism for game side contracts; it is market microstructure used to validate fills, not a determinant of the outcome.

m.lifecycle.reason: Open/close/halt/postponement events matter here because the 48-hour postponement clause converts a delayed game side market to a fair-price settlement; needed to define the information set and void handling.

cfb.pass_rush.reason: Pressure rate for and against interacts with OL health; as an additive term it duplicates def_ppa pass splits, so its value is the matchup product (rush rate vs protection rate), not the level.

cfb.secondary_coverage.reason: Explosive-pass-allowed rate is a component of def_ppa and success_explosiveness; keep as the matchup partner of the opponent's deep-pass rate, not as a standalone strength term.

cfb.run_defense.reason: Front-seven run defence is a component of def_ppa rushing; adds information only when crossed with the opponent's rushing share and quarterback mobility.

cfb.offense_style.reason: Option, tempo and RPO identity changes possession count and therefore margin variance more than margin mean; valuable mainly for the underdog-cover shape at constant rating gap.

interactions.mechanism: A backup quarterback behind a depleted offensive line loses more than the sum of the two separate effects because inexperienced passers rely on protection and play-action tied to a functioning run game; the penalty is largest when the replacement is a first-year player with fewer than 50 dropbacks.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit margin residual on replacement value, OL games-missed index and their product; compare slope on the product term in games with both vs one shock.

interactions.mechanism: Past a lead of about 21 points in the second half the favourite's marginal scoring rate drops sharply for conservative coaches, while aggressive coaches keep scoring; this makes the cover rate for 30+ point rungs a coach-dependent step, not a smooth function of rating gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised P(margin >= 30) for games with gap > 28 split by aggression tercile; test a step at pre-game gap 21-24.

interactions.mechanism: In weeks 1-4 the prior dominates, so talent and returning production explain more of the margin than in-season efficiency and the posterior SD is wide; from about week 8 the weights flip and the same variables become nearly redundant.
interactions.how_to_test: Rolling regression of margin on prior vs in-season rating by week; identify the crossing week and test stability across seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Wind or rain compresses passing, which helps a run-heavy option team against a weak front and hurts an air-raid favourite; the weather effect on margin depends on which side is pass-reliant and on opposing run defence.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact style (pass share), wind speed above 15 mph and opponent run-defence rank in a margin residual model; check sign by pass-reliant favourite vs underdog.

interactions.mechanism: Home-field value is not constant: it grows with altitude and crowd for visitors on a short week and shrinks in rivalry games where both teams are fully motivated; opt-outs at neutral-site bowls remove it altogether.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate home-edge by team and test interactions with days of rest and rivalry flag; neutral-site bowls as a control group.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave in rating gap beyond ~21 points, with a floor from garbage-time scores
nonlinearities.why: Expected margin does not grow one-for-one with rating gap once starters sit, so P(margin >= 42) rises far more slowly than a Gaussian predicts and differs by opponent class.

nonlinearities.shape: Inverse-square-root decay in games played, with a jump after portal-heavy offseasons
nonlinearities.why: Rating uncertainty shrinks with sample size but resets with roster churn; it changes win probability by several points at constant rating gap.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in dropbacks of the replacement: very wide posterior below ~50 career dropbacks
nonlinearities.why: Swap cost for an unknown backup is a fat-tailed mixture, not a normal shift; the mean is little changed but the downside tail is heavy.

required_data.dataset: FBS and FCS game results with team-level play-by-play advanced stats
required_data.timestamp_requirement: Only games finished before kickoff; ratings recomputed as-of each Sunday and carried to the next game, never end-of-season values.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFTEAMRECYDS settles YES if the named team records at least the stated number of receiving yards (for example Notre Dame 325 or more, strike 324.5) in the game; receiving yards recorded in the first or second overtime period count towards the team total, while successful 2-point conversions, including those in overtime, do not. A game postponed but started within 48 hours remains open and settles on the official final result; if not started within 48 hours the market resolves to a fair price. The settlement source is the official stat result, with no provider named in the sampled text.

rules_evidence.quote: Any receiving yards recorded in the first or second overtime periods count toward a team's total.
rules_evidence.establishes: Overtime periods 1 and 2 add yards to the total, so overtime probability is a (small) positive contribution to the distribution.

rules_evidence.quote: Successful 2-point conversions, including those in overtime, do not count for this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Yards gained on 2-point attempts are excluded, which matters for third-overtime-and-later periods that consist only of 2-point tries.

rules_evidence.quote: If Notre Dame records 325+ receiving yards in the Miami (FL) vs Notre Dame college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: The strike is stated as 325+ (floor_strike 324.5), a greater-than-or-equal threshold on the sum of the team's receiving yards.

variants_and_edge_cases: Only one series (KXNCAAFTEAMRECYDS) is registered in this archetype in the ledger, but the contract_types include team stat props across other stats (rushing, passing, turnovers, first downs); only receiving yards rules text was sampled, so other stat definitions are unverified.
Overtime period 1 and 2 yards count; from the third overtime the format is alternating 2-point attempts whose yards are excluded, so the rule has an effect only for very long games.

Receiving yards can be negative on a catch behind the line; whether negative receiving yards net against the total, whether sacks or laterals affect it, and whether team receiving yards equal completions' yards under official NCAA statistics are NOT stated in the sampled text; this is domain knowledge only and the definition is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED.
Threshold rungs are .5 strikes written as N+ (for example 325+), so there is no push; the ladder of rungs for one team and game is a monotone survival curve.
Postponement of more than 48 hours or cancellation resolves to a fair price rather than void.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game statistics per the Kalshi wording (official final result); the specific provider (NCAA stats, conference, ESPN or Sportradar) is not named in the sampled rules, so reconciliation against CFBD box scores is required before using it for labels.

mechanism.summary: A team's receiving yards equal its passing-game completions' yardage (excluding 2-point tries), so the outcome is dropbacks x completion rate x yards per completion, truncated by what the game looks like. Dropbacks come from plays in regulation (tempo and possessions) times the pass share, which swings 15 to 20 percentage points with score state; efficiency per attempt depends on the quarterback, receiver depth and opposing pass defence and pressure; the distribution is right-skewed because explosive completions are rare and large. Overtime adds a small right tail (periods 1 and 2 count). Settlement depends on which statistics provider is the source of truth.

stages.name: Snap budget from tempo and possessions
stages.description: The number of offensive snaps a team gets in 60 minutes comes from drives and seconds per snap; both vary with score state and the season's clock rule regime (running clock after first downs since 2023). The budget sets the ceiling for dropbacks, and overtime adds one or two extra possessions with probability under ten percent.
stages.distribution: Roughly Gaussian per-game plays (SD around 9) with heavier right tail in shootouts; overtime adds a discrete lump.

stages.name: Pass share conditional on game script and scheme
stages.description: Out of the snap budget, dropbacks equal plays times the pass rate, which depends on the offence's scheme, quarterback strength, weather and above all expected score state: trailing teams drop back much more, leading ones run. Quarterback scrambles and sacks are dropbacks that do not produce receiving yards, so the relevant count is attempts, not dropbacks.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative binomial) conditional on expected margin; pass share piecewise in lead size.

stages.name: Completion rate and yardage per completion
stages.description: Each attempt becomes a completion with probability set by the quarterback, protection against the opposing pressure rate, receiver quality and coverage; the yards per completion are air yards plus yards after catch, with a long tail for explosive plays. The opposing secondary's explosive-allowed rate acts multiplicatively on a deep-passing offence.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli completions with heavy-tailed positive yards per completion; team receiving yards skew right (median below mean).

stages.name: Pass-catcher and quarterback availability
stages.description: The effective passing unit depends on who plays quarterback and which receivers are available; with sparse college injury reporting these shocks arrive late. A missing receiver shifts targets to replacements, lowering yards per target more than the number of targets; a quarterback change lowers both completion rate and yards per attempt and widens uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Discrete availability states with replacement-quality uncertainty; effect size is a mixture, not a smooth shift.

stages.name: Dispersion and joint script correlation
stages.description: The final yardage is a sum of a correlated set of components (plays, pass share, yards per attempt) that move together with the game script: a shootout lifts all three. The tail above a high rung such as 325 is dominated by those correlated high-script games, so independent marginals understate it.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed, correlated mixture; the threshold probability is a tail quantity sensitive to variance and covariance.

stages.name: Settlement and stat-source reconciliation
stages.description: Yards in overtime periods 1 and 2 count and 2-point yards do not; the official provider may differ from public box scores, so labels and live checks must use the same definition. A postponement beyond 48 hours resolves to a fair price rather than a win or loss.
stages.distribution: Deterministic given the provider; risk comes from definitional mismatches of a few yards near the strike.

cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.label: Script-adjusted team dropbacks
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.mechanism: Expected team pass attempts plus sacks given the expected game flow, rather than the season-average pass rate.
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.rationale: Pass volume is the largest driver of receiving-yards variance: a team that trails by two scores throws 50-plus times, a team leading by 21 throws 20. Using season-average attempts mixes games of both kinds and understates the spread in the mean.
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.measurement: Fit dropbacks per game on team neutral-situation pass rate (first and second down, score within 7, first three quarters), opponent neutral pass-rate allowed, expected margin from non-market ratings (not a quote), and plays; then predict at the pre-game expected margin with a piecewise term at +/-14 and +/-21. Window: current season with 6-game half-life, shrunk to previous season with k = 4 games; as-of the Saturday preceding kickoff. Output: mean attempts and a negative-binomial dispersion.
free_sources: CFBD plays with down, distance, score and play type (free key)
raw_data: play-by-play with play_type, down, distance, score diff, period, clock
cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts.why: Receiving yards = completions x yards per completion, and completions scale with dropbacks that depend on score state, so the mean and its spread must be conditioned on expected flow.

cfb.state_dependent_pace.label: State-dependent tempo (seconds per play by score state)
cfb.state_dependent_pace.mechanism: Plays per minute differ when leading, tied or trailing, and by clock situation; determines total plays inside 60 minutes plus any overtime.
cfb.state_dependent_pace.rationale: A hurry-up team trailing can add 8 to 12 plays versus its average; a ball-control team leading runs the clock. The season mean hides this, and the rule set since 2023 (clock running after first downs outside the last two minutes) changed the baseline.
cfb.state_dependent_pace.measurement: For each offence compute seconds per snap in four buckets (trailing by 9+, within 8, leading 9-16, leading 17+) in Q1-Q4, excluding two-minute drills, over the last 12 games with 0.5 shrink toward conference mean (k = 200 snaps). Combine with the opponent's pace allowed and expected state mix from the script input to produce expected snaps; flag the season's clock-rule regime. As-of last completed game.
raw_data: play-by-play with period, clock, score, offense, play_type
cfb.state_dependent_pace.why: The yardage threshold is crossed mostly in games with high snap counts; state-dependent tempo is the mechanism linking expected margin to those counts.

cfb.completion_yardage_profile.label: Completion yardage profile (depth of target and yards after catch)
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.mechanism: Splits yards per completion into air yards and yards after catch and records the explosive-completion rate.
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.rationale: Two offences with the same yards per attempt can have very different variance: one dinks and runs screens, the other throws deep. Threshold probabilities depend on the tail of long completions and on the opponent's tackling and safety depth.
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.measurement: Per team: average depth of target, YAC per completion, share of completions of 20+ and 40+ yards, all opponent-adjusted by the opponent's allowed values; 10-game window with 0.7 per-game decay and shrinkage k = 60 completions to conference mean. Where air-yards data is missing (CFBD has limited coverage), approximate with yards per completion and 20+ rate. Report mean and SD of yards per completion.
free_sources: CFBD plays (yards, play text parse, free key)
PFF/SIS charting for air yards (paid, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for CFB depth)
raw_data: pass plays with yards gained, receiver, air yards where available
cfb.completion_yardage_profile.why: Sets the dispersion of per-completion yards, and so P(325+) relative to the mean.

cfb.wr_personnel_rate.label: Receiver personnel-grouping rate
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.mechanism: Share of snaps with 3 or more receivers (11 personnel, 10 personnel, empty sets) versus heavy sets.
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.rationale: Receiving-yards volume depends on how many pass-catchers are deployed: spread offences convert dropbacks into more targets to receivers and fewer to backs and tight ends, and the loss of a receiver matters more when the team lives in 4-wide sets.
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.measurement: For each offence, share of snaps by personnel group (RB/TE/WR counts) over the last 8 games, opponent-weighted; compute the 3+ WR snap share and empty-set rate with k = 150 snap shrinkage to conference average. Combine with receiver snap shares and starters out as of the pregame vintage.
free_sources: No free CFB personnel feed confirmed (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
cfb.wr_personnel_rate.why: Links availability of specific pass-catchers to team yardage via formation, instead of treating every receiver as interchangeable.

cfb.pace.reason: Plays per game bound every counting stat, but the single season average hides that tempo changes with score state; the state-dependent version (cfb.state_dependent_pace) is what actually sets how many dropbacks a team gets.

cfb.pass_rate.reason: Pass share is the direct multiplier between plays and receiving yards; keep, but as the script-adjusted pass attempts, since a raw season pass rate is dominated by games that were blowouts one way or the other.

cfb.rush_efficiency.reason: For a team receiving-yards threshold, rushing efficiency matters only indirectly through play-calling balance, which pass_rate already carries; line yards and stuff rate have no path into receiving yardage.

cfb.pass_efficiency.reason: Opponent-adjusted yards per attempt and PPA per dropback directly generate receiving yards; sack rate in the label is a different outcome (sack yards count against rushing under NCAA rules and do not subtract from receiving yards).

cfb.run_defense.reason: Opposing run defence affects receiving yards only by pushing the opponent toward passing, a small second-order effect; included as primary matchup input for rushing props but misplaced here.

cfb.secondary_coverage.reason: Opposing explosive-pass-allowed and yards per attempt allowed set yards per completion; strongest for deep-passing offences, so it should be used in a product with the team's average depth of target.

cfb.pass_rush.reason: Pressure converts attempts into incompletions and throwaways (lower completions) but sacks do not count as negative receiving yards; effect runs through completion rate and yards per attempt, not through a sack term.

cfb.havoc.reason: Havoc rate combines tackles for loss, forced fumbles and pass breakups; only the pass-breakup component touches receiving yards, and it is already carried by opposing secondary_coverage.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Interceptions end drives and cut dropbacks modestly, but the regression-to-expected adjustment changes expected team receiving yards by well under one reception; negligible for a 325-yard threshold.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Defined as the split of the game total and spread, i.e. a price-derived expected score; it is a benchmark for the expected game script, to be replaced here by a rating-based expected margin that is not a function of any quote.

cfb.script.reason: Expected score state drives pass attempts (trailing teams throw and snap faster); needs to be built from rating gap and coach tendencies, and label's 'garbage-time behaviour' mixes two different effects.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind above roughly 15 mph and precipitation cut deep passing and completion rate; forecast vintage is correct, but the effect depends on the team's average depth of target.

cfb.player_stat_variance.reason: Label says player stat shape but this contract is a team aggregate; the useful content is the team-level dispersion of receiving yards (right-skewed, explosive-play driven), which the threshold probability depends on.

m.rules_text.reason: Settlement wording is decisive here: overtime periods 1 and 2 count, successful 2-point conversions do not, and the 48-hour postponement clause applies; versioning matters because stat definitions can change by season.

m.stat_source_mismatch.reason: Not pregame-knowable but needed to build labels: the official provider can differ from CFBD or ESPN box scores by a few yards on lateral and review plays, which matters near the strike.

cfb.corr.reason: Correlation of passing volume, game total and period script is needed for joint use with other ladders, but for a single team yardage rung it only matters through shared expected plays.

cfb.skill_avail.reason: A missing WR1 or tight end moves yards per target more than volume (targets redistribute); labelled primary but for a team aggregate the quarterback matters more than any one receiver.

cfb.injuries.reason: No official college injury feed; as an untimestamped concept it adds nothing beyond skill_avail and qb status, which are the specific absence terms.

cfb.player_usage.reason: Target and carry share allocate yards among players, but this contract sums the whole team; usage only matters as the replacement-receiver quality term, which skill_avail already approximates.

interactions.mechanism: A team's dropback response to being a big underdog depends on its own pass-rate slope and tempo: an air-raid, up-tempo offence converts a deficit into many extra pass snaps, while a run-first or slow team under the same deficit still burns clock; so extra receiving yards from the trailing script appear only where pass_rate slope and pace are high.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress dropbacks on the SP+ expected-margin gap interacted with the team neutral pass-rate-over-expected slope and seconds per play; compare the gap coefficient across pass-rate-slope terciles.

interactions.mechanism: An offence that lives on deep completions has yards per completion multiplied by the opposing safeties' explosive-allowed rate, while a short-pass offence is almost insensitive to it; the product, not the sum, determines the right tail above a high strike.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit yards per completion on depth-of-target x opponent explosive rate and compare to an additive model on held-out games.

interactions.mechanism: Sustained wind above about 15 mph reduces deep-ball completion and shifts calls to the run, but the cut-in only appears past the threshold and is largest for vertical offences; mild weather has no effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team receiving yards in games with forecast wind above 15 mph against calm games, split by depth-of-target tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Loss of a top receiver costs more yards in a four-wide scheme (where he is on the field for 90 percent of snaps and targets concentrate) than in a heavy-set scheme where targets spread across tight ends and backs; a backup quarterback shrinks the yards per target of every remaining receiver at once.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the yards-per-attempt drop when a top-2 receiver or the starting quarterback is absent, split by 3+ WR snap-share tercile.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: pass share rises about 10 points when trailing by two scores and falls sharply when leading by 21+
nonlinearities.why: Dropback volume is the main driver of the right tail and responds non-linearly to lead size, so a linear score-state term understates both extremes.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail in yards per completion
nonlinearities.why: A few 50+ yard completions can add 100 yards; threshold probabilities near the mean are sensitive to the tail share of explosive plays rather than the mean yards per attempt.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: extra snaps convert into pass attempts at a falling rate as clock-burning kicks in
nonlinearities.why: Beyond about 75 snaps the added plays are disproportionately runs in clock-killing situations, so yards do not scale with tempo one-for-one.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise-convex in expected margin with hinges near -10 and +14 to +21
nonlinearities.why: Dropbacks rise faster than linearly as the expected deficit grows (trailing teams pass and hurry), and flatten or fall for large favourites that run the clock; the hinge sits in the SP+ margin, not in a second input, so it is a single-input response shape.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFTOTAL settles YES if the two teams collectively score more than the half-point strike (for example over 25.5 for Nebraska vs Illinois) in the game; the title says Full Game but the sampled rules text does not state whether overtime points are included. A postponed game that begins within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result; if it does not start within 48 hours the market resolves to a fair price. Rungs are strict greater-than on .5 strikes, so there is no push.

rules_evidence.quote: If the teams collectively score more than 25.5 points in the Nebraska vs Illinois college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike is strictly greater than a half-point number on combined points, so settlement requires 26 or more total points.

rules_evidence.quote: Full Game: Over 25.5 points scored
rules_evidence.establishes: This is the market title, not rules text: it labels the market a full-game total but establishes nothing about overtime, which the rules text is silent on.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: Short postponements keep the market open; beyond 48 hours the same text says fair price.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime treatment is unstated in the sampled KXNCAAFTOTAL text (compare KXNCAAFHIGHSCORE which says including overtime and KXNCAAF4QTOTAL which says excluding overtime); the Full Game title suggests inclusion but this is not verified.
The sampled rung of 25.5 for a Power-conference game is an extreme low rung of a ladder; the ladder runs from low to high strikes and each rung is a nested event.
Cancelled or non-started games after 48 hours resolve to a fair price, not to NO, so weather cancellations do not pay the under.
Totals have mass at certain sums (3, 6, 7, 10, 13, 14...) so the distance between consecutive .5 rungs carries very different probability.
FBS vs FCS games are included in the series with very high totals possible when a large mismatch occurs.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final result per the Kalshi wording; the stats provider is not named in the sampled text, so the final score as published by the NCAA or the schools is assumed.

mechanism.summary: Total points = number of possessions x expected points per possession summed over both offences, plus non-offensive scores, with overtime as an optional extra if the contract counts it. Possessions come from tempo (seconds per play), run-pass mix and clock management, and are shared between the two teams so the slower side dominates; points per possession come from opponent-adjusted efficiency, finishing (touchdown versus field goal), field position and special teams. Late information (quarterback, weather) and game script (blowouts compress the favourite, garbage time adds underdog points) shape the distribution, which is right-skewed with key-number lumps.

stages.name: Possession count from joint tempo
stages.description: A game contains roughly 22 to 26 combined possessions in modern FBS. The count is set by both offences' seconds per play, plays per drive, run share and the clock regime (running clock after first downs since 2023), and by the lead size late; a slow ball-control team pulls a fast team's possessions down, so tempo combines harmonically rather than additively.
stages.distribution: Near-Gaussian count with SD of about 2 possessions; right tail in shootouts with turnovers and quick scores.

stages.name: Points per possession for each offence
stages.description: For each side, expected points per drive combine ability to move the ball (opponent-adjusted success and explosive plays), the quality of the opposing defence, starting field position and the finishing rate inside the 40. Finishing includes the touchdown versus field-goal choice and kicker range, and so the same yardage yields different points.
stages.distribution: Per-drive points are a 0/3/7 mixture; the sum over ~12 drives gives a total with SD of roughly 13 points, right-skewed by explosive drives.

stages.name: Late information on personnel and conditions
stages.description: Quarterback identity, kicker status and weather are confirmed late and move the total more than any rating. Wind and rain reduce passing and field-goal range but only at open stadiums; temperature and dome status matter at the margins. Officials contribute a small amount through penalty rate.
stages.distribution: Discrete shocks (QB change) plus continuous weather effects; weather impact is threshold-like in wind speed.

stages.name: Script compression and non-offensive scores
stages.description: When a favourite builds a large lead, starters leave and the clock runs, trimming its late scoring, while the underdog gets garbage-time possessions; the net depends on the coach. Defensive and special-teams touchdowns add points without an offensive drive and add dispersion; they are mostly luck with a small skill component.
stages.distribution: Mixture: the central mass is truncated by script compression, while rare 6-8 point lumps (return touchdowns) fatten the right tail.

stages.name: Overtime and contract definition
stages.description: If regulation ends tied (about 5 to 8 percent of games) overtime adds points: a two-possession period starting at the 25-yard line with about 4 to 5 expected points per side; whether those count is not stated in the sampled rules, which changes the probability of crossing a rung near the median by a few percentage points. Conditional input set: if overtime counts in KXNCAAFTOTAL, the total needs cfb.ot_model (P(tie after 60 minutes) from the margin and total distribution, overtime possession scoring, number of overtimes; the same inputs are defined in the overtime archetype as cfb.regulation_tie_curve and cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate); if it does not, the series is regulation-only and cfb.ot_model drops out.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli tie event with discrete additive points in 3/6/7/8 lattice.

talent_strength.note: Opponent-adjusted efficiency of both offences and defences; talent composite is in the catalog but not attached.

opponent_matchup.note: Style pairing and defensive havoc against the opposing line and protection.

availability_news.note: Late quarterback confirmation and bowl opt-outs; other injuries rely on catalog inputs not attached here.

coaching_scheme.note: Scheme and lead-management tendencies; fourth-down aggression is untested for totals.

efficiency_conversion.note: Moving the ball versus finishing; field-goal conversion.

distribution_variance.note: Right-skewed total with lumps at 3/7 and a return-touchdown tail.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, lookahead, rivalry and conference-championship stakes shift effort and tempo but nothing in this archetype's inputs captures them for totals; their effect size on totals is unmeasured.

officiating_rules.note: Crew penalty tendency and the season clock regime.

settlement_contract.note: Strict greater-than, overtime inclusion unresolved, 48-hour postponement clause.

cfb.expected_possessions.label: Expected combined possessions per game
cfb.expected_possessions.mechanism: Number of drives in the game computed from both teams' seconds per drive rather than from averaged plays.
cfb.expected_possessions.rationale: Total points scale with the number of possessions, roughly 22-26 combined in modern FBS games. Seconds per play, plays per drive and run/pass mix interact: two slow teams produce fewer possessions than the average of their individual paces implies, because clock-killing drives are shared.
cfb.expected_possessions.measurement: For each team compute average drive duration (seconds) on non-garbage-time drives over last 10 games with 0.8 per-game decay, excluding drives ending a half; expected possessions per team = (3600 - stoppage-adjusted halftime-neutral time) / (0.5*(d_own + d_opp_allowed)) with a clock-regime constant fitted by season; add 1 when either team has no-huddle rate above 40 percent. Report mean and SD (about 2 possessions). As-of the last completed game.
free_sources: CFBD drives (start time, duration, plays; free key)
raw_data: drive table with start/end clock, plays, yards, result
cfb.expected_possessions.why: Replaces the average-of-paces approach with the structural number of scoring trials, the strongest single driver of a game total.

cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.label: Points per scoring opportunity (drives crossing opponent 40)
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.mechanism: Average points on drives that reach the opponent 40 or closer, opponent-adjusted, separating finishing from moving the ball.
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.rationale: A team can have strong PPA and still score few points if it settles for field goals; conversely, strong finishers outperform yardage. Scoring-trip efficiency regresses less than red-zone TD rate because it pools more drives and includes field-goal-range situations.
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.measurement: Per team: sum of points on drives with first down inside the opponent 40 divided by number of such drives (over 10 games, 0.85 per-game decay), adjusted by opponent allowed value and by kicker field-goal value; shrink with k = 25 drives toward conference mean. Output mean and SE; combine own offence and opposing defence by an additive deviation model.
raw_data: drive start/end yard line, result, points scored
cfb.scoring_trip_efficiency.why: Splits efficiency into moving and finishing, important because totals depend on 3-versus-7 outcomes rather than yardage.

cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.label: Defensive and special-teams touchdown rate
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.mechanism: Rate at which a team scores on interception returns, fumble returns, kickoff and punt returns, and blocked kicks, and allows them.
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.rationale: These touchdowns add 6-8 points without using an offensive possession, are partly skill (returners, ball-hawks) and mostly luck, and fatten the right tail of the total. The market's total rarely prices them separately.
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.measurement: For each team: defensive plus special-teams touchdowns scored and allowed per game over 2 seasons with 0.5 season decay, shrunk with k = 12 games toward the FBS mean per team-game (to be measured, plausibly 0.1 to 0.2); add a return-specialist indicator from kick returner yards over expected. Output expected points = 7 x rate (own) + 7 x rate allowed by opponent minus offence replaced.
raw_data: plays with type: interception TD, fumble TD, kickoff/punt return TD, blocked kick
cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate.why: Fat-tail component of the total not captured by drive-based efficiency.

cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.label: Stadium wind exposure and forecast bias
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.mechanism: Translates a forecast wind speed into expected on-field wind by stadium (open bowl, enclosed, dome, orientation).
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.rationale: A 20 mph forecast at a closed or dome stadium is irrelevant while the same forecast at an open lakeside stadium cuts passing and field-goal range materially; the forecast vintage alone is not predictive without the exposure factor.
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.measurement: Per stadium: roof type (open, retractable, dome), historical ratio of observed on-field wind (from nearest airport station via NOAA ISD or Meteostat) to forecast at issue 6 hours out, fitted by month over 8 seasons; exposure = ratio x forecast. Outputs adjusted wind in mph and an indicator of >15 mph. Apply only at kickoff plus 3 hours.
raw_data: venue table with roof, orientation, lat/long
cfb.stadium_wind_exposure.why: Makes the weather vintage input usable for totals by linking forecast to actual game conditions in the specific building.

cfb.pace.reason: Plays per game from both teams is the volume term of the total, but a season average ignores that the slower team and the score state control the clock; it should feed an expected-possessions computation rather than be added to the opponent's value.

cfb.drives.reason: Drives per game is the unit of scoring trials and is more direct than plays; the label mixes drives, explosiveness and finishing drives into one, which should be separated (possessions, points per drive, drive success).

cfb.pass_rate.reason: Pass share affects clock use and variance (incompletions stop the clock) but is already inside pace and offense_style; marginal value is small once drive duration is modelled.

cfb.clock_rules.reason: The clock-rule regime changes only between seasons (running clock after first downs, 2023 onwards), so within a season it is constant; it is a training-set stratifier and a level shift, not a game-level predictor, and was mislabelled secondary.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Points per drive for each side flows from opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency; PPA is a model-based quantity, so it should be paired with a direct points-per-drive from actual scoring to keep a non-modelled check.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Opposing defensive efficiency suppresses points per drive; conference connectivity makes G5 defence values noisy, so a shrinkage prior (cross_conf_calibration) should be applied before use.

cfb.success_explosiveness.reason: Success rate versus explosiveness changes drive length and the variance of the total at the same mean PPA; useful mostly for the width of the distribution.

cfb.redzone.reason: Red-zone TD-versus-FG rate shifts points per trip but regresses heavily on 30 or so trips per season; use shrunk expected points per scoring opportunity instead of a raw rate.

cfb.havoc.reason: Havoc creates negative plays and short fields, hitting both teams' drive outcomes; partly duplicate with def_ppa success rate, retained for turnover/short-field effect.

cfb.field_pos.reason: Average starting field position and special-teams quality shift points per drive; punt and kickoff-return strength are stable enough to carry weight.

cfb.kicker.reason: Kicker range and accuracy decide how many stalled drives become 3 points and shape key-number mass in the total; kicker change is a late news item.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Quarterback identity affects both efficiency and tempo; for totals the change in pace and in explosive-play rate is as important as the efficiency shift.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind, precipitation and temperature are the best-known late-information drivers of totals; the forecast vintage is correct but the stadium-specific wind exposure (open bowl, closed, dome) is missing.

cfb.offense_style.reason: Option, air-raid and RPO labels overlap with pace and pass_rate; keep as a categorical regime to catch atypical plays-per-game that rating-based models mispredict.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Starter removal lowers favourite late scoring while the underdog gets garbage-time points; net effect on totals is ambiguous and coach-specific, so it is secondary to the pregame mismatch regime.

cfb.officials.reason: Penalty-heavy crews lengthen drives and add replays, worth a fraction of a point to the total; weak but real, and crew assignments are announced late in the week for most conferences.

cfb.score_resid.reason: Residuals of totals around lines are market-derived by construction; they calibrate the benchmark's error shape but cannot serve as a fundamentals input.

m.external_lines.reason: Sharp sportsbook totals embed weather, lineup and sharp money; use as the comparator after de-vig, never as an input to a model claiming independent information.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Monotonicity and kinks across total rungs (the quotes at 25.5, 45.5, 55.5...) are a diagnostic of stale quotes and of the market's implied distribution, not a cause of the total.

cfb.opt_out_departures.reason: Relevant to bowl and CFP totals where opt-outs lower scoring versus regular-season ratings; absent for regular-season games.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is the market's own output; it measures when information was absorbed (useful for timing studies and closing-line value) but is not a cause of the game total outcome and must not enter a fundamentals model.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread govern whether a game total edge is tradable, not whether the event occurs; keep for execution and sizing, not as an outcome input.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule changes net edge on game total contracts (largest near 50c) but has no causal link to the result; an execution parameter, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe liquidity and price reliability for game total quotes; useful to weight benchmark trust, irrelevant to the outcome process.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades show informed flow and fill realism for game total contracts; it is market microstructure used to validate fills, not a determinant of the outcome.

m.lifecycle.reason: Open/close/halt/postponement events matter here because the 48-hour postponement clause converts a delayed game total market to a fair-price settlement; needed to define the information set and void handling.

m.settlement_truth.reason: Labels must use the official settled total and the contract's overtime treatment; not available pregame but essential to build correct training targets.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Turnovers create short fields and drive-ending events; regression-to-expected recovers true offensive efficiency, but the effect on totals is smaller than on sides because both teams' luck partially offsets.

interactions.mechanism: Possession count depends on run share through the clock rules: a run-heavy team that keeps the clock moving after first downs shortens the game for both sides, and a pass-heavy opponent cannot restore the possessions because incompletions stop the clock only for its own snaps; so tempo of the faster team matters less when the slower team has a high run share.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress realised total possessions on each team seconds per play interacted with the combined run share and season clock regime; check whether the tempo coefficient shrinks as combined run share rises.

interactions.mechanism: Wind above roughly 15 mph at an open stadium reduces both deep passing and field-goal range beyond 40 yards; the cut in total is minimal below the threshold and then steep, and is amplified when the kicker is already marginal.
interactions.how_to_test: Bucket games by adjusted on-field wind and kicker long-range accuracy; compare average total versus ratings-implied total.

interactions.mechanism: In a one-sided game the total follows a different regime: the leader's scoring drops but the trailing team's garbage-time possessions and return touchdowns add points; whether the total goes up or down depends on the coach's pull point and on trailing-team passing.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the total residual for games with pre-game rating gap above 21 split by coach pull-point tercile and by trailing offence pass rate.

interactions.mechanism: A high-explosiveness offence facing a high-havoc defence produces many failed drives but occasional long scores; the mean total changes little while its variance and right tail increase, which matters for high rungs.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the variance of totals by explosiveness x havoc bucket; test with quantile regression at the 80th and 90th percentiles.

interactions.mechanism: A quarterback change lowers both efficiency and tempo (backups run a simpler script), so the effect on the total is the product of a smaller points-per-drive and fewer possessions, and it is bigger for up-tempo offences.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast pre/post-change totals for teams by tempo tercile, controlling for opponent and weather.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold near 15 mph on-field wind, steep beyond 20 mph
nonlinearities.why: Passing and kicking degrade slowly until wind affects the ball's flight, then drop steeply; a linear wind term misprices both calm and gale games.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in count but with SD that grows with tempo; total points concave in possessions at high counts
nonlinearities.why: Extra possessions are not equal: late extra possessions occur in blowouts or garbage time with lower scoring rates, so marginal points per added possession declines.

nonlinearities.shape: Lumpy 0/3/7 per trip with convex value of touchdown conversion near the goal line
nonlinearities.why: Moving a trip from field goal to touchdown adds 4 points, and the probability gain is concentrated near the 10-yard line; small efficiency shifts have large point effects when concentrated there.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFOT settles YES if at least one overtime period is played in the named game (strike 1); an overtime period counts as played once it commences, via a legal snap in the first two overtimes or a first two-point attempt from the third overtime onward, and once started counts in full whether or not both teams get a possession. KXNCAAFMOSTOT settles YES if any Division I game in the 2026 regular season goes to at least 9 overtime periods. A game postponed but started within 48 hours stays open and uses the official final result; outside that window the markets resolve to a fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: An overtime period counts as played once it commences, via a legal snap (in the first two overtimes) or a first two-point attempt (in the third overtime and onward).
rules_evidence.establishes: Period counting is event-based: a started period counts even if the game ends on the first possession, and OT 3+ periods are two-point attempts.

rules_evidence.quote: If there is a Division I game that goes to 9+ overtime periods in the 2026 college football regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: The season-extreme contract covers every Division I game (FBS and FCS) in the regular season, strike 9 with greater-or-equal construction.

rules_evidence.quote: If at least 1 overtime period is played in the Illinois vs UCLA college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: Per-game contract is the indicator that the game was tied after regulation (overtime period one commenced).

variants_and_edge_cases: KXNCAAFOT is equivalent to regulation tie; KXNCAAFMOSTOT is an aggregate over all Division I games with a rule-regime change at the third overtime (alternating two-point attempts), so the per-period survival is not constant.
A period counts as played once started even if the game ends on the first snap of that period, so a sudden-death result in period k still counts k periods.
Overtime periods scheduled but never started do not count, which matters only for weather suspensions or ties after curfew; the rules do not say how a suspended overtime is treated.

KXNCAAFMOSTOT primary text scopes the market to 'the 2026 college football regular season', and the sibling HIGHSCORE rules state conference championship, bowl and CFP games are not part of the regular season, so conference championship games are reasonably excluded; the sampled MOSTOT text is truncated and how a game halted by weather during overtime counts is still not addressed.
The 9+ strike is greater-or-equal on count of periods; a 9-overtime game with the ninth period commenced counts, even if the ninth ends the game on the first snap.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game records (final box score with periods) as reported by the NCAA or the participating schools; Kalshi text does not name a provider for these two series.

mechanism.summary: Overtime happens if and only if the game is tied after four quarters, so P(OT) is the point mass of the regulation margin distribution at exactly zero: roughly the margin density at zero (large when teams are evenly matched and the total is low) adjusted for the scoring lattice, plus an excess created by late-game decisions to tie rather than win. How many periods follow is a separate renewal process: each period from the 25-yard line ends tied only if both teams score the same, with a rule change at the third overtime to alternating two-point attempts, so the count of periods is nearly geometric and the 9+ strike is a long-tail event across hundreds of games in the season.

stages.name: Regulation margin distribution near zero
stages.description: The final regulation margin has centre equal to the expected rating gap and spread equal to the sum of game-level noise and rating uncertainty; the tie probability is the mass at exactly zero, which falls roughly Gaussianly with the absolute gap and is highest when the gap is within three points. Fewer possessions or lower totals reduce the margin SD and therefore raise the mass at zero for close matchups.
stages.distribution: Point mass of a discrete lattice, approximately density at 0 times lattice factor; peaks at zero gap and decays like exp(-gap^2/(2 sigma^2)).

stages.name: Scoring lattice and low-scoring conditions
stages.description: Points arrive as 3, 6, 7 and 8 (and occasionally 2), so some margins are far more reachable than others; field-goal-heavy games produce ties more easily because both teams accumulate multiples of three. Wind and rain make scoring lower and lumpier, and kickers with limited range convert drives to threes.
stages.distribution: Lumpy discrete distribution with elevated mass on margins reachable by equal numbers of three-point scores; weather lowers the total and raises lumpiness.

stages.name: End-of-regulation decisions that create or avoid ties
stages.description: In the last two minutes the team trailing by three can kick the tying field goal, a team trailing by eight needs a touchdown and a two-point conversion, and a team with the ball in a tie may kneel into overtime. These choices put extra mass at zero relative to a smooth margin density and differ by coach.
stages.distribution: Binary decisions at specific score and clock states; excess mass at tie created by coach-specific decision rules.

stages.name: Overtime period renewal process
stages.description: Once in overtime, each period gives each team a possession from the 25-yard line; the period is tied if both score the same number of points (both touchdown with equal conversion, both field goal, both none). Scoring probabilities per possession are far higher than ordinary drives, so a tie after period one is the exception, giving a decay by period with a modest per-period continuation probability.
stages.distribution: Geometric-like renewal with continuation probability depending on team scoring rates, roughly a quarter to a third per period in early periods (to be fitted).

stages.name: Rule regime change and season-extreme aggregation
stages.description: From the third overtime periods are single alternating two-point attempts, so each period ends tied only if both succeed or both fail, near one half; reaching nine periods requires six consecutive such ties after two ordinary overtimes. Across several hundred games the contract is a rare-event union, so exposure (games remaining, maximum already seen) matters as much as per-game probability.
stages.distribution: Piecewise geometric survival with a regime break at period 3; season-level union probability 1-(1-q)^N for a very small q.
