cfb.regulation_tie_curve.label: Regulation tie probability curve from non-market expected margin and total
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.mechanism: Empirical P(margin = 0 after four quarters) as a function of absolute expected margin and expected total points.
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.rationale: A tie is a point mass on a lumpy lattice: the probability is roughly the margin density at zero adjusted for the fact that football scores come in 3, 6, 7, 8 and so ties occur preferentially at combined patterns that are reachable by both sides. The curve is peaked at zero gap and decays quickly, and the expected total changes the margin SD.
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.measurement: From all FBS games since 2005 (about 15,000 games: roughly 750 per season over 21 seasons), fit logistic/GAM of tie indicator on |expected margin| (from SP+ or own rating, not market) and expected total with monotone smoothing; bucket |gap| in 2-point bins (0-2, 2-4, ... 14+) and expected total in 8-point bins; shrink bins to pooled curve with prior strength 200 games. Evaluate as-of kickoff. Output P(tie) with 95 percent interval; for FCS fit separately.
free_sources: CFBD games with period line scores (free key)
cfb.regulation_tie_curve.why: Tie incidence is the entire target of KXNCAAFOT and the entry condition for KXNCAAFMOSTOT; direct estimation from non-market axes avoids circularity with the price.

cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.label: End-of-regulation decision profile
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.mechanism: How often a coach settles for a tie (kneel, kick the tying field goal) versus plays for the win in the last two minutes.
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.rationale: Tied games are created or avoided in the final minutes: a trailing team that kicks a field goal to tie creates overtime, and a team with the ball tied with 40 seconds left may kneel. Coaches differ systematically, so two matchups with equal margin distributions can differ in tie incidence.
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.measurement: From plays with clock under 2:00 in Q4 and score diff in {-3..-1, -8..-1 requiring TD+2, 0}: for each head coach compute the rate of choosing kneel/tying FG versus aggressive play over expected from a fitted decision model, over 3 seasons with shrinkage k = 15 situations to the conference mean. Output coach-level tie-propensity z-score; coach change resets to prior of coordinators plus career data.
free_sources: CFBD plays with clock and play_type (free key)
raw_data: play-by-play final 2:00 with down, distance, score, timeouts
cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile.why: The existing coaching input measures tenure and scheme but not the one decision that converts a close game into overtime.

cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.label: Overtime possession scoring rates (touchdown, field goal, none)
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.mechanism: Per-team probabilities of touchdown, field goal or no score from the 25-yard line, offence and defence, opponent-adjusted.
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.rationale: Overtime ends when one team outscores the other in a period; probability a period ends tied depends on the pair of scoring outcome distributions, and overtime offence differs from ordinary offence (short field, no clock, kicker at 42 yards).
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.measurement: Per team: P(TD), P(FG), P(none) on first-and-10 from the 25 with no clock pressure, estimated from non-OT drives starting inside the opponent 30 with shrinkage k = 20 drives plus actual OT possessions with weight 3; opponent-adjust by the same quantity for defences. Period tie probability = sum over outcomes of own x opponent matched scores (TD-TD with equal conversion, FG-FG, none-none). Compute as-of date.
cfb.ot_possession_scoring_rate.why: Sets the conditional probability of a second and later overtime period, which compounds geometrically into the 9+ period contract.

cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.label: Two-point conversion success rate for the alternating-attempt overtimes
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.mechanism: Team probability of converting a two-point attempt from the 3-yard line, offence and defence, used from the third overtime.
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.rationale: From the third overtime onward periods are single two-point attempts; a period ends tied whenever both teams convert or both fail, so the per-period tie chance is p_a p_b + (1 - p_a)(1 - p_b), close to one half for any plausible p, which keeps the process nearly memoryless and makes 9+ periods a power of about one half.
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.measurement: Per team: successful two-point attempts divided by attempts, offence and defence, over 3 seasons with beta prior at league mean of roughly 0.47-0.50 (to be estimated) and prior strength 25 attempts; use goal-to-go 3-yard plays with 2 or fewer yards to go as proxy where attempts are few. Combine as p_a = (off_a + (1 - def_b)) / 2. As-of date.
free_sources: CFBD plays: two-point conversion play types (free key)
raw_data: two-point attempts with result and play type
cfb.two_point_shootout_rate.why: Only the rule regime of OT 3+ makes 9+ periods possible, and its per-period tie probability depends on exactly this quantity.

cfb.season_ot_exposure.label: Season overtime exposure (games remaining and current maximum)
cfb.season_ot_exposure.mechanism: Number of remaining Division I games in the regular season and the maximum overtime periods already seen.
cfb.season_ot_exposure.rationale: KXNCAAFMOSTOT is a season-extreme event: if a nine-overtime game has already occurred the market is decided, otherwise the number of remaining games times the per-game probability of reaching 9+ periods determines the price. The decay of exposure through the season is a deterministic input.
cfb.season_ot_exposure.measurement: Count remaining Division I regular-season games as of query date (FBS plus FCS, per the contract's scope) by week; current season maximum number of overtime periods across all D-I games; P(YES) = 1 - (1 - q)^N with q from the tie curve x period-length geometric (with regime change at OT 3), unless max already >= 9 (then 1.0). Update weekly.
raw_data: season schedule with game dates and divisions
cfb.season_ot_exposure.why: Turns a per-game tail probability into the season contract and handles the monotone state variable (record already set).

cfb.score_resid.reason: Defined as residuals around lines, so it is a market-conditioned table; the tie mass it is meant to deliver is better estimated directly as the historical frequency of regulation ties in non-market expected-margin and expected-total buckets (cfb.regulation_tie_curve).

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Implied team points derived from the game total and spread are price outputs; they are useful as a cross-check for tie-probability buckets but cannot be an input without circularity.

cfb.market_ratings.reason: A rating backed out of lines is a price-derived quantity; only the absolute value of the rating gap matters for tie probability and a non-market SP+ or own rating gives the same information independent of the quote.

cfb.ot_model.reason: Overtime procedure (alternating possessions from the 25, 2-point alternation from the third period) is deterministic and defines length; the label conflates rules with a tie-probability model, which should be split into tie incidence and period-length parts.

cfb.kicker.reason: Kicker quality affects regulation scoring lumps, tying-field-goal success at the end and overtime period scoring; needs separate definitions for each use (regulation range, 42-yard OT kick).

cfb.coaching.reason: End-of-regulation decisions (kneel to go to overtime, kick the tying field goal, go for two) are the coaching lever; the generic coaching-change label does not measure them, so replace with a late-game decision profile.

cfb.pace.reason: Original claim that fewer possessions raises tie variance is imprecise: fewer possessions shrinks margin SD, which raises P(margin = 0) only when expected margin is near zero; keep as a driver of margin SD, not as a standalone tie predictor.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind and rain reduce scoring and increase lumpiness of 3-point scores, which slightly raises tie incidence; small and indirect through expected total.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: A large expected margin already makes tie probability near zero; blowout management adds nothing for the 1-in-20 games that stay close, where it is irrelevant by definition.

m.rules_text.reason: The rules text defines when an overtime period counts as played (legal snap in OT 1-2, first two-point attempt from OT 3), which is the core of both series and of period counting for the most-overtimes strike.

m.strike_hit_rates.reason: Base rate of overtime games per season (roughly 5 to 8 percent of games) and of long overtimes is the prior; sample is small (dozens of games a year), so it should be pooled across 10+ seasons and not applied by rung.

interactions.mechanism: Tie probability depends jointly on the absolute rating gap and the margin SD, which in turn depends on possessions and weather; at a gap of zero the probability rises as SD falls, but at a gap of seven it rises with SD, so the sign of the SD effect flips with the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit tie probability on gap, SD proxy and their product; contrast the SD slope in gap<3 versus gap>7 games.

interactions.mechanism: A coach who habitually kicks the tying field goal creates overtime only if his kicker is accurate from 35-45 yards; a poor kicker makes the decision pointless, so incidence of created ties depends on the product of intent and capability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare tie rates in games where the trailing team had a late tying-FG opportunity by decision-profile tercile x kicker accuracy tercile.

interactions.mechanism: The probability that a period ends tied switches regime at the third overtime from a score-matching process (0.25-0.35) to a two-point match (about 0.5), so survival to 9 periods multiplies a small early factor by a roughly 0.5^6 tail; both the regime and the number of games enter the season probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate period-tie rates separately for OT1-2 and OT3+ from historical long games; compare the geometric prediction with the observed count of 6+ OT games.

interactions.mechanism: Overtime ties are more likely when both offences are poor from the 25 or both kickers are reliable (both score a field goal), and wind lowers touchdown probability while leaving short field goals reachable; the period tie probability is a product-sum of both teams' scoring distributions.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute predicted period tie probability from team distributions and evaluate calibration against realised OT1 outcomes by weather bucket.

nonlinearities.shape: Gaussian-like decay in absolute rating gap with a long thin tail; flat near zero gap
nonlinearities.why: A gap of 10 points has about one third of the tie probability of a gap of 3, but not zero because of volatile late scoring, so a linear gap term misprices both ends.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise with regime break at overtime period 3; period tie probability bounded near 0.5
nonlinearities.why: Because p_a p_b + (1 - p_a)(1 - p_b) stays between about 0.45 and 0.55 for all realistic rates, the probability of long overtimes is insensitive to team quality but very sensitive to the number of periods.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in games remaining: 1-(1-q)^N is nearly linear for tiny q and saturating only at very large N
nonlinearities.why: The market price should decay almost linearly as games complete, then jump to 1 if a qualifying game happens; a smooth hazard model misrepresents the step.

contract.settlement_definition: Period winner markets (KXNCAAF1H, 1Q, 2Q, 3Q, 4Q, 2H) are titled 'wins the <period>' and are read here as settling YES if the named team outscores the opponent in that period (inferred; the sampled rules never state tie handling and the secondary text is truncated near 930 characters, so a tie sentence may sit beyond the sample); only points in the stated period count. The 2nd half includes overtime (KXNCAAF2H, KXNCAAF2HSPREAD, KXNCAAF2HTOTAL), while the 4th quarter excludes it. Spread markets settle YES if the team wins the period by more than the half-point strike (for example 7.5). Short postponements under 48 hours stay open; longer ones resolve to a fair price. The sampled winner text is silent on what a tied period pays, which is a significant open item.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 4th quarter (excluding overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Fourth-quarter markets exclude overtime points, so a game tied after regulation does not add to the 4Q margin.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 2nd half (including overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Second-half markets include overtime points, making them depend on regulation tie probability.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 1st quarter of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: First-quarter spread uses only Q1 points; the strike 7.5 means a margin of 8 or more in 15 minutes.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple quarters are tied for the most points scored
rules_evidence.establishes: Highest scoring quarter splits payout across tied quarters at $1/N, so ties are paid pro rata rather than lost.

rules_evidence.quote: If either the first half or full game result is incorrect, the market resolves to No
rules_evidence.establishes: Half-time/full-time combos require both legs, so settlement is a joint event including a tied half and a full game including overtime.

variants_and_edge_cases: Tied period: the sampled KXNCAAF1H, 1Q, 2Q, 3Q, 4Q text says wins the period but does not state the payout on a tie; ties in single quarters are very frequent (a quarter can end 0-0 or with equal scores) so this is a first-order ambiguity, partly mitigated by the existence of the 1HFT market which uses a Tie leg.
Overtime scope differs across series within the archetype: 2H includes it, 4Q excludes it, 1H and Q1-Q3 cannot include it.
KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS and 3QBTTS (both teams to score in a quarter) are title-only: no rules text sampled, so settlement for ties and overtime is not read.
KXNCAAFQF (College Football Playoff Quarterfinals qualifiers) is an outright futures contract mislabelled into this archetype by the period-style key; it belongs with season futures.
KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE pays 1/N (rounded down) among N tied quarters, so a payout can be fractional and ties are not binary.
The sampled secondary rules text for the period winner series is cut off at about 930 characters, so any tie or suspension sentence after the 48-hour clause is unseen.

mechanism.summary: A quarter or half margin is the difference between two short compound-Poisson scoring processes: the number of possessions each team gets in the period (set by tempo, who received the opening kick, and end-of-half clock behaviour) times the probability that a possession ends in a 3-, 6-, 7- or 8-point score. Period mean margin is a fraction of the game margin, but variance relative to mean is very large and there is a big point mass at zero, so winner markets are trinomial (win, tie, lose) and spreads sit in a thin lumpy tail. Second-half and fourth-quarter periods are distorted by blowout management and by the contract's overtime scope.

stages.name: Possession order and tempo within the period
stages.description: Each period contains only two or three possessions per team. The opening kickoff recipient takes the first and (usually) the third quarter's opening drive, deferral is a coach habit, and the second quarter ends with the team that kicked off in the first half often holding the ball with the last chance to score. Possession counts differ by period and drive times differ by tempo.
stages.distribution: Small-integer counts (about 2 to 3 per team per quarter) with a deterministic order effect; variance relative to the mean is high.

stages.name: Scoring rate per possession by period
stages.description: Per-possession scoring probability equals the team's opponent-adjusted offence against the opposing defence, but with period-specific modifiers: scripted openers in Q1, end-of-half two-minute drills in Q2, halftime adjustments in Q3, and clock-driven decisions in Q4. Quarter scoring history is mostly noise around the game-level rate.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcomes per possession with 3/7 payoff; period-level differences mostly random; real structural effects are a fraction of a point.

stages.name: Availability and the game-level margin prior
stages.description: The game-level expected margin from team ratings and the late quarterback decision supplies the mean from which period means are derived; the translation from game margin to period margin is roughly proportional to the period's share of scoring, but not exactly because favourites score disproportionately in first halves and clock-burn late.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like prior on game margin scaled by period fraction; period mean about 1/4 (quarter) or 1/2 (half) of game margin, with period noise far exceeding the mean shift.

stages.name: Script effects: blowout management and correlation across periods
stages.description: Second-half and fourth-quarter margins depend on halftime lead: favourites with large leads pull starters and run the ball, compressing their margin, while the first half is played at full strength. Period margins are positively correlated with the game margin and with each other through script and team strength.
stages.distribution: Conditional distribution given halftime lead; correlated joint distribution across periods with sign-flipping mean reversion in blowouts.

stages.name: Period margin lattice and settlement scope
stages.description: The distribution of period margin is lumpy: large mass at zero, then 3, 6, 7, with spread rungs at 7.5 requiring a touchdown-plus-conversion margin; winner markets lose on ties unless the rules say otherwise. The second half includes overtime, the fourth quarter does not, and highest-scoring-quarter pays 1/N on ties.
stages.distribution: Discrete lattice with point mass at 0 (roughly a quarter of quarters for even teams) and a thin right tail; series-specific overtime scope.

cfb.period_possession_allocation.label: Period possession allocation (opening kick, deferral and end-of-half order)
cfb.period_possession_allocation.mechanism: Expected possessions per team in each quarter given who receives the opening kickoff, deferral habits and tempo.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.rationale: A quarter has only about 2-3 possessions per team, and receiving the opening kickoff gives one extra drive in Q1 (and typically ends Q2 with the other team holding the ball); the share swings expected quarter margin by 0.3 to 0.8 points between the two possession orders. The toss itself is only known at kickoff, so the input must be probabilistic.
cfb.period_possession_allocation.measurement: Per head coach: P(defer | win toss) over last 3 seasons (shrink k = 10 tosses to the conference mean) and P(win toss) = 0.5; P(team receives first) = 0.5 x P(receive | win) + 0.5 x (1 - opponent P(defer)). Expected drives per quarter per team = season drives per team x quarter share (0.24-0.26 each) with Q1 and Q3 adjusted by the receive-first indicator times 0.5 drive. Store the realised toss only after kickoff.
free_sources: CFBD games and plays (kickoff and coin toss from play text, free key)
cfb.period_possession_allocation.why: Possession count in a quarter is the dominant source of difference between a quarter spread and a share of the game spread.

cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.label: Two-minute and end-of-half drive efficiency
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.mechanism: Points per drive in the final two minutes of the first half and of the game, plus the share of drives where the leader runs out the clock.
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.rationale: Quarters 2 and 4 end with clock-driven scoring chances that are not representative of normal drives; a good two-minute offence with a reliable kicker produces points at a much higher rate, and teams differ in whether they play to score or hold the ball at the end of the half.
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.measurement: For each team: points per drive in the last 2:00 of Q2 and Q4 when score within 14 and at least one timeout, over 2 seasons, with 0.5 decay per season and shrinkage k = 20 drives to the conference mean; include kneel-down rate (drives ending in kneels when leading) and no-timeout slot. Compute opponent-adjusted by the opponent's allowed value.
free_sources: CFBD plays and drives with clock (free key)
raw_data: drive records with start time, clock at start, timeouts, result
cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency.why: Q2 and Q4 spreads and highest-scoring-quarter markets depend on these abnormal drives, which are not in a season efficiency rating.

cfb.period_margin_lattice.label: Period margin lattice and tie mass by expected margin and total
cfb.period_margin_lattice.mechanism: Empirical probabilities of period margin = 0, positive margins up to 8+, by period and by pre-game expected margin and total.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.rationale: In a single quarter the most likely outcome for evenly matched teams is a tie (0-0 or equal scores) and the winner market loses on ties; spread rungs at 7.5 correspond to a touchdown-plus-two margin or more, so they live in the thin right tail of a lumpy distribution. A Gaussian misprices both the mass at zero and the key numbers.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.measurement: From FBS games since 2014 take the line scores by period; for each period and for each of expected-margin bins (-14 to +14 in 3-point bins, from non-market ratings) and expected-total bins (3 bins) estimate P(margin = k) for k in {-14..14} with Dirichlet smoothing (prior strength 100 games, centred on a compound-Poisson model). Evaluate as of kickoff and output joint probabilities of tie, win and cover at each rung.
cfb.period_margin_lattice.why: Direct empirical shape for period winner and period spread contracts, whose ties and rung settlement (>7.5) hinge on lattice probabilities.

cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.label: Second-half overtime spillover
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.mechanism: Expected effect of overtime on the second-half margin, which includes overtime points by contract.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.rationale: For second-half sides, overtime points are added to each team's second-half total; a game that is tied after regulation is decided by overtime, so the second-half margin equals the overtime result plus second-half regulation margin; ignoring this biases second-half winner probabilities for the close games where it matters.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.measurement: P(OT) from a tie curve (bucketed by non-market expected margin and total) x distribution of OT margin (home/away first possession, points scored by period one: roughly 7 versus 3 versus 0); output expected spillover to the second-half margin = P(OT) x E[OT margin | team] and a variance increment. For 4Q and Q1-Q3 contracts set to zero because they exclude overtime.
cfb.second_half_ot_spillover.why: The same rules text contrast (2H includes OT, 4Q excludes it) changes the target distribution by series; a series-specific spillover makes the difference explicit.

cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.label: Joint four-quarter scoring pmf with per-team scoreless mass and highest-quarter argmax
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.mechanism: Distribution of each quarter combined points and each team points jointly across Q1-Q4, with quarter-to-quarter correlation, used to price both-teams-to-score in a quarter and the highest-scoring-quarter contract with its 1/N tie split.
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.rationale: KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE pays 1/N (rounded down to a cent) when N quarters tie for the most combined points and excludes overtime from Q4; the BTTS series (1Q, 2Q, 3Q) need the per-team probability of scoring at least once in that quarter. Neither is a margin event, so a margin lattice cannot price them: they need the pmf of period totals, the probability each team is held scoreless in the quarter, and the negative dependence between a heavy first half and a compressed second half.
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.measurement: From FBS games 2014 onward (CFBD line scores and drives), for each team and quarter fit scoring drives N ~ negative binomial with mean from cfb.q_scoring times expected possessions, dispersion fitted pooled; points per scoring drive from a 3/6/7/8 mixture with team touchdown share shrunk k=25 drives; combine the four quarters with a Gaussian copula whose Spearman correlations are estimated by bins of expected total (3 bins) and absolute expected margin (3 bins), shrunk to the pooled matrix with prior strength 200 games. Simulate 50,000 games: output P(team scores >=1 in quarter k) for each team, the pmf of combined points per quarter, and for QHIGHSCORE the expected payout sum over quarters of P(k is the argmax with N-way tie)/N, Q4 regulation points only. As-of last completed game before kickoff.
free_sources: CFBD games line scores and drives (free key)
raw_data: line scores by period for both teams
scoring drives by quarter with points
cfb.quarter_joint_scoring_pmf.why: KXNCAAFQHIGHSCORE and KXNCAAF1QBTTS, 2QBTTS, 3QBTTS are live series of this archetype that need the four-quarter joint pmf, per-team scoreless mass and argmax-with-ties payout rather than period margins.

cfb.half_tie_conditional_win.label: Conditional full-game win probability given a tied first half
cfb.half_tie_conditional_win.mechanism: For KXNCAAF1HFT (first-half tie AND named team wins the full game including overtime) the joint probability is P(first half tied) times P(team wins | first half tied), and the second factor depends on second-half scoring rates, possession order and overtime.
cfb.half_tie_conditional_win.rationale: A tied half carries information about the teams: ties happen more in low-scoring, evenly matched games, where the conditional winner probability is near 50 percent plus a home and strength tilt that is not the unconditional win probability. Overtime makes the full game always decisive, so the conditional is a proper win probability with no tie leg.
cfb.half_tie_conditional_win.measurement: From FBS games 2014 onward, estimate P(half tied) as a logistic/GAM function of absolute expected margin and expected total (non-market, SP+ or own rating) with prior strength 150 games, and estimate P(team wins | half tied) by logistic regression on the pre-game rating gap, home/neutral and second-half receiving team, fitted only on games tied at halftime (about 4-5 percent of games, pooled across seasons, shrunk to 0.5 with prior strength 40 games). Multiply the two. Include overtime in the full-game result. As-of last completed game before kickoff.
raw_data: line scores by half with overtime
cfb.half_tie_conditional_win.why: KXNCAAF1HFT settles on a first-half tie plus the full-game (including overtime) winner; the joint needs this conditional, which cfb.corr alone does not measure.

cfb.market_ratings.reason: A full-game strength backed out of quotes is a benchmark; period markets are priced off it by sportsbooks, so using it as an input makes any period edge a statement about the sportsbook's period conversion, not about football.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Full-season opponent-adjusted offence is the right mean for the game but not for a single quarter; needs period-specific splits and scripted-opening effects, and its signal is diluted in a 15-minute window with 2-4 possessions.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Same limitation as off_ppa: defensive quality drives the scoring rate in every period but period-level noise dominates, so it enters only as the mean of a per-period rate.

cfb.half_split.reason: First-versus-second-half scoring share is the sum of quarter shares already in q_scoring; keeping both double-counts the same sample, and the half split has even fewer games per team than needed to be reliable.

cfb.q_scoring.reason: Team quarter scoring history is the direct target proxy, but a 12-game sample per quarter is mostly noise, so it must be shrunk heavily toward the game-level rate and used only for the structural (not random) component of quarter differences.

cfb.opening_poss.reason: Who receives the opening kickoff (and thus the second-half kickoff) decides the possession order in Q1 and Q3; the toss happens just before kickoff so this is not pregame-knowable, only forecastable from each coach's deferral tendency.

cfb.first_drive.reason: Opening-drive tendency matters for Q1 but the sample is one drive per game (about 12 per team-season), so its reliability is low; use only as a minor shrunk adjustment to Q1 scoring.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Relevant to third and fourth quarters and second-half sides, not to the first half where starters play; the label presents it as primary for all periods, which overstates its role.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Quarterback change shifts expected period margin proportionally to the game effect, but is also a late-news driver for the quote; no period-specific effect has been shown, so secondary.

cfb.talent.reason: The claim that depth wins second halves is a plausible hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect; keep as a context variable to test whether depth shifts H2 share, not as an assumed driver.

cfb.coaching.reason: Halftime adjustment and tempo claims have no supporting measure in the label; define through measurable items (two-minute management, second-half pace change) before treating as informative.

cfb.score_resid.reason: Residuals around lines are tied to the quote; the period margin lattice with mass at zero must be built from historical period scores by expected margin, not from market residuals.

m.rules_text.reason: The rules text decides ties and overtime scope by series: the 2nd half includes overtime, the 4th quarter excludes it, and QHIGHSCORE pays 1/N on tied quarters; every series needs its own parameterisation.

cfb.corr.reason: Needed to price joint outcomes such as 1HFT (tie at the half and a game winner) and to keep Q1, 1H, 2H and full-game ladders mutually consistent; its estimation requires period-level history of both teams.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Regressing fumble-recovery luck changes expected period margin by well under half a point; one early turnover is a realised random event, not a repeatable team trait that the pregame input can predict.

interactions.mechanism: Expected points in a period equal possessions times scoring rate, so receiving the opening kickoff matters much more for an offence with a high touchdown rate: the extra drive is worth about 0.5 times that team's points per drive, a bigger edge for an elite offence than for a poor one.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress Q1 and Q3 margin on receive-first indicator interacted with team points per drive terciles; compare slopes.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect: second-half margins depend on halftime state: when the leader is up three scores, depth and rotation determine whether the margin shrinks, grows or stays; below that lead the first-half dynamics persist, so the regime switches at roughly 21 points. The input cfb.blowout_management is itself audited WEAK, so this regime switch is a conjecture to test, not a basis for the model.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition on halftime lead bins and estimate the second-half margin distribution separately for leads above and below 21.

interactions.mechanism: End-of-half scoring depends on possession order and whether a team plays to score or holds the ball: the team receiving the second-half kickoff has an incentive to hold for a field goal before the half, raising the other team's chance of scoring in Q2.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare Q2 margins when the first-half receiver holds the last possession vs not, split by two-minute efficiency terciles.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis, not a demonstrated effect: a backup quarterback is scripted conservatively in Q1, so Q1 margin shrinks toward zero, but only if the offence's opening script was prepared for him; once the game opens up in later quarters the penalty grows, so the effect of a QB change on period margin depends on the period index.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the margin residual of backup-quarterback games by period; test a monotone increase in the penalty from Q1 to Q4.

interactions.mechanism: The 2H winner and the full-game winner are strongly dependent through overtime, and 1HFT-type markets require a joint tie-and-winner event; marginal quarters are positively correlated through team strength but only weakly so, which defeats independent-leg pricing.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the empirical correlation matrix of period margins by expected margin bin and test independence on pairs (1H, 2H) and (Q3, Q4).

interactions.mechanism: Given a first-half tie the full-game outcome is decided by second-half scoring and possibly overtime, so the conditional win probability is flatter than the unconditional one and the overtime spillover pushes it toward the pre-game favourite only weakly; a small tie probability times a near-even conditional prices the 1HFT leg.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the winner model on halftime-tied games only, compare its slope in rating gap with the unconditional full-game slope, and check calibration of the product on historical 1HFT-style outcomes.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at zero margin plus lumps at 3, 6-8; probability of a margin >= 8 within a quarter is far below a Gaussian prediction
nonlinearities.why: A quarter has only 5-6 combined drives, so margins above 7 require multiple scores; a continuous model misprices tie probability and rung 7.5 by several percentage points.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold near a 21-point lead; weak effect below, strong compression above
nonlinearities.why: Starters stay in until the game is effectively decided; the effect on second-half margin appears only past a lead of about three scores.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function: one extra possession (about 0.5 drive) for the receiving team in Q1 and Q3, none elsewhere
nonlinearities.why: The possession order effect is binary rather than continuous and is concentrated in specific quarters; averaging across periods hides it.

contract.settlement_definition: Quarter and half total markets (KXNCAAF1QTOTAL, 2QTOTAL, 3QTOTAL, 4QTOTAL, 1HTOTAL, 2HTOTAL) settle YES if the two teams collectively score more than the half-point strike in that period, counting only points in that period; the 2nd half includes overtime (as the 2HTOTAL rules state) and the 4th quarter excludes overtime. KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL settles YES if the named team alone scores over its strike in the first half. Postponed games starting within 48 hours remain open and settle on the official final result; otherwise a fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 4th quarter (excluding overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Fourth-quarter totals exclude overtime, so the distribution is regulation-only and unaffected by ties.

rules_evidence.quote: Only points scored during the 2nd half (including overtime) of play count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Second-half totals include overtime periods, adding a rare positive increment from tied games.

rules_evidence.quote: If the teams collectively score more than 7.5 points in the 1st quarter
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike construction is strictly greater than a half-point value, so a total of 8 or more points in 15 minutes is needed.

rules_evidence.quote: If Notre Dame scores over 6.5 points in the 1st half of the Miami (FL) vs Notre Dame college football game
rules_evidence.establishes: The team-total variant counts only one team's points in the first half with a half-point strike.

variants_and_edge_cases: Period scope by series: 1Q to 3Q and 1H cannot include overtime, 4Q explicitly excludes it, 2H explicitly includes it; the 1HTEAMTOTAL primary text states the scope ('scores over 6.5 points in the 1st half'), what is unstated is how a suspension is handled.

Strike levels in the samples are very low for halves (6.5 for 1H and 2H totals) relative to typical first-half totals (not quantified here: the left-tail frequency of 1H totals of 6 or fewer points must be measured, see cfb.period_total_dispersion validation), so the ladders have many rungs and the sampled rung is one of many nested events.
Safeties, two-point conversions and defensive scores count as points for the team or game; the sampled text does not say otherwise, but extra-point returns are not discussed.
Quarter totals have large mass at 0 and 7, meaning .5 strikes at 6.5 and 7.5 carve very different probabilities (P(total >= 7) versus P(total >= 8)).
A postponed or suspended game starting within 48 hours remains open; a game suspended mid-period (weather) with resumed play affects period labelling and is not addressed.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official period scoring from the final box score; Kalshi text says official final result but does not name the stats provider.

mechanism.summary: A period total is the sum of points from both teams in a short window: the number of combined scoring chances (drives that fit in the period, capped by clock) times the probability and size of scores, which come in lumps of 3, 6, 7 and 8, so the distribution is a compound count with a large mass at zero and at the key sums. The mean is a non-uniform share of the game total (end-of-half drives, scripted openers, lead-dependent late periods), while variance is large relative to mean. Overtime matters only for the second half, and for team-total variants only one side's scoring process enters.

stages.name: Game-level scoring expectation allocated to the period
stages.description: A pregame expected total (from opponent-adjusted offences and defences and conditions) is allocated across periods by a share that depends on expected game script: Q2 and Q4 hold two-minute drives and are scored at higher rates per minute, Q1 starts with scripted plays, Q3 starts after halftime adjustments. The share also depends on the gap, since big leads reduce Q4.
stages.distribution: Allocation shares vary around 0.2-0.3 per quarter with game-level dependence; shares are estimated from league history and have sampling noise of a few percentage points.

stages.name: Drive budget inside the period
stages.description: How many drives fit into 15 minutes is set by both teams' seconds per drive, run-pass mix, turnovers and end-of-period truncation; Q2 and Q4 end with abrupt clock stops and sometimes kneel-downs, while Q1 and Q3 usually do not. A slow period of four combined drives caps the total in a way that a mean-based approach hides.
stages.distribution: Count of drives (4 to 7 combined) with threshold effects at low counts; truncation of the last drive at the period end.

stages.name: Points per scoring chance and lumpy scoring
stages.description: Each drive ends in 0, 3, 6, 7 or 8 points with team-specific touchdown-versus-field-goal mix; the period total is the sum of those jumps. End-of-half field-goal decisions, scripted openers and turnovers shift the probability of scoring; kickers matter at the margins because a 3 versus a 0 flips a low rung.
stages.distribution: Compound count with lumps at 3 and 7 and a negative-binomial-like number of scoring drives; overdispersed relative to Poisson.

stages.name: Script and personnel shocks late in the game
stages.description: In Q3 and Q4, lead-dependent behaviour (clock burning, starter removal, garbage-time scoring by the trailing team) reshapes the total; quarterback status and weather change scoring rates in every period but with period-specific timing (wind rising in the second half).
stages.distribution: Conditional mixture: tight totals in competitive games versus bimodal totals in blowouts; discrete shocks from quarterback and weather.

stages.name: Series scope and settlement
stages.description: Series differ in scope: 2H includes overtime, 4Q excludes it, 1H team total counts a single team, and the rung strike lies on the half-point so the settlement threshold is a specific integer of points. The ladder of rungs for one period is a nested family and must be internally consistent.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the pmf to rung probabilities; consistency constraint across rungs (monotone survival).

cfb.period_share_of_total.label: League-baseline share of scoring by period conditional on expected total and gap
cfb.period_share_of_total.mechanism: Fraction of regulation points scored in each quarter by games with similar expected total and rating gap.
cfb.period_share_of_total.rationale: Allocating a game total to quarters with equal quarters is wrong: end-of-half possessions, scripted openers and lead-dependent second halves make shares unequal and dependent on the gap (blowouts cut Q4 scoring) and on the total. The share is a structural baseline separate from team-specific history.
cfb.period_share_of_total.measurement: From FBS games since 2014 compute E[points in period k] / E[regulation points] by bins of expected total (non-market, 4 bins) and absolute expected margin (5 bins), with shrinkage k = 150 games to the pooled share; also store the variance and the share of games with zero points in the period. Apply to the pre-game expected total from a ratings model; exclude overtime from all quarters and add it only to 2H for the 2H contract.
cfb.period_share_of_total.why: Directly produces the mean of every quarter, half and 1H team-total rung from one game-level estimate.

cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.label: Combined drives and clock budget per period
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.mechanism: Expected number of combined drives that fit in the period and the probability that a possession is cut off by the clock.
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.rationale: A quarter holds about five or six combined drives, and the last drive of Q2 and Q4 is truncated by the clock; slow, run-heavy teams can reduce the combined drive count in the first period to four, which lowers the total in a threshold manner at the 7.5 rung.
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.measurement: For each team compute seconds per non-garbage drive by period (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4 separately) over the last 10 games with 0.8 decay; combined drives in period k = 900 / (0.5 (d_a + d_b)) minus end-of-period truncation fraction (empirical 0.1-0.3 drive for Q2 and Q4), with the 2023-onward running-clock regime as a covariate. Output mean and SD of combined drives and P(drives <= 4).
free_sources: CFBD drives with clock fields (free key)
cfb.period_drive_clock_budget.why: Quarter and half totals need a count of scoring trials inside a short window; this input gives that count and its threshold behaviour.

cfb.period_total_dispersion.label: Period-total dispersion and zero-scoring mass
cfb.period_total_dispersion.mechanism: Variance-to-mean ratio and the probability of a scoreless period for team pairs, given expected points.
cfb.period_total_dispersion.rationale: Single-quarter totals are overdispersed relative to Poisson in points but heavily mass-concentrated at 0, 3 and 7; rungs at 7.5 are sensitive to whether the probability of scoring zero in the period is 15 or 25 percent. Explosive teams and field-goal teams differ in the lumpiness for the same mean.
cfb.period_total_dispersion.measurement: Fit a compound model per period: number of scoring drives N ~ negative binomial with mean mu_k and dispersion r (fit on FBS 2014 onward), points per scoring drive from a 3/6/7/8 mixture with team-specific touchdown share (touchdown share shrunk k = 25 scoring drives). Output P(total = 0), P(total >= 8), and the full pmf up to 28. As-of last completed game. Left-tail validation: on held-out seasons compare predicted P(1H total <= 6), P(2H regulation total <= 6) and P(quarter total = 0) to realised frequencies by expected-total bin (reliability table with binomial intervals); refit the negative-binomial dispersion if the left tail is miscalibrated.
raw_data: scoring drives by period with points
cfb.period_total_dispersion.why: Gives the exact probability of crossing 6.5 / 7.5 / 13.5 rungs rather than a normal approximation to a lumpy count.

cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.label: Garbage-time scoring profile
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.mechanism: How many points the trailing team and the backups score late when the margin exceeds the garbage-time threshold, and how fast the leader burns clock.
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.rationale: In Q4 totals the effect of a lead is double-edged: the leader scores less and runs the clock, the trailer scores late against backups; the net effect depends on coach pull-point, backup quality and defensive depth, and differs across the 4Q-only and 2H contracts.
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.measurement: Define garbage time by margin thresholds above (Q3 > 27, Q4 > 21; verify against published practice); for each team compute points scored and allowed per garbage-time minute and seconds per play when leading, over 2 seasons with 0.5 decay and shrinkage k = 100 snaps; combine with the probability of reaching garbage time from the pre-game rating gap.
free_sources: CFBD plays with score state (free key)
raw_data: plays with period, clock, score diff, offense
cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile.why: Fourth-quarter and second-half totals diverge from a share-of-total rule precisely in games with large gaps; this input quantifies that divergence.

cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.label: Overtime points increment to the second-half total
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.mechanism: KXNCAAF2HTOTAL counts overtime points, so the 2H total is regulation second-half points plus, with probability P(tied after 60 minutes), the combined points of all overtime periods.
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.rationale: With roughly a 6 percent chance of overtime and around 7 to 10 combined overtime points when it happens, the 2H mean shifts by about half a point and the variance and right tail grow, which matters for a 6.5 rung on a low count; 1Q-3Q, 1H and 4Q contracts exclude overtime and get zero increment.
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.measurement: P(OT) from cfb.ot_model: logistic/GAM of tie after regulation on absolute non-market expected margin (SP+ or own rating) and expected total, fitted on FBS games 2005 onward with prior strength 200 games. Conditional on OT, combined overtime points = sum over periods of per-possession scoring (touchdown about 0.65 per possession from the 25 with 7 points plus a field-goal share, two-point attempts from the third overtime onward); fit the pmf of combined overtime points on FBS overtime games 2005 onward (about 1,000 games), shrunk to pooled with prior strength 50 games. Output E[increment] = P(OT) x E[OT total] and the pmf to convolve with the regulation 2H pmf. Set to zero for non-2H contracts. As-of last completed game.
free_sources: CFBD games line scores with overtime (free key)
cfb.second_half_ot_total_increment.why: KXNCAAF2HTOTAL (sampled rung 6.5, text states the 2nd half includes overtime) is shifted and fattened in the right tail by overtime; the other quarter and half totals are not.

cfb.team_period_points_share.label: Team share of period points from non-market team strengths
cfb.team_period_points_share.mechanism: Splits the game-level expected points in a half between the two teams using each offence points per drive against the opposing defence, plus the receiving team in the half, for KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL.
cfb.team_period_points_share.rationale: The team-side 1H total is not half of a team full-game total: the share depends on who receives the opening kickoff and which team has the stronger offence against the weaker defence, and first-half scoring is lumpy. Without a non-market allocation the series would need the benchmark team-total split.
cfb.team_period_points_share.measurement: Expected 1H points for team A = (E[game 1H points] from cfb.period_share_of_total) x w_A, with w_A = A expected game points / (A + B expected game points) where expected points come from opponent-adjusted off_ppa and def_ppa (current season with 6-game half-life shrunk to prior season with k=4 games), then add 0.5 x A points per drive if A receives the first-half kickoff and subtract 0.5 x B points per drive if B does not receive. Output mean and a negative-binomial scoring-drive dispersion fitted on FBS 2014 onward. As-of the Saturday preceding kickoff; no price or line input.
free_sources: CFBD games, drives and PPA (free key)
raw_data: team points per drive and opponent-adjusted PPA
cfb.team_period_points_share.why: KXNCAAF1HTEAMTOTAL needs a team-side allocation of first-half points that does not use any market total split.

cfb.q_scoring.reason: Team quarter scoring history is the target-matched feature, but 12 games per quarter is a tiny sample; needed in a shrunk form where the signal is the structural share (end-of-half, scripted opener) not the realised noise.

cfb.half_split.reason: First-half share of scoring is a sum of Q1+Q2 shares already in q_scoring; the half is also less volatile than quarters but needs no separate input, only a different aggregation.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Defined from the game total and spread, which are prices; for period totals the expected game points should come from non-market ratings and the quote used only to measure edge.

cfb.opening_poss.reason: For a combined total the number of Q1 possessions is the same regardless of who receives; the order matters for who holds the ball at the end of Q2 (a small change in expected scoring), so the effect on totals is far smaller than on period sides.

cfb.first_drive.reason: Scripted opening drives can lift Q1 scoring for both teams, but one drive per game makes this a very noisy feature; use only a shrunk average of both opening-drive point rates.

cfb.pace.reason: Plays and drives in a 15-minute period scale directly with tempo; however pace differs between periods (end-of-half hurry-up, clock-killing in Q4), so a season average must be period-adjusted.

cfb.script.reason: Expected score state alters tempo and pass rate within the period; for Q1 it is nearly irrelevant (the score is level), for Q4 it is the dominant context.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Primary only for Q3/Q4 and second-half totals; for Q1 and Q2 the starters are in and the input has no role, which the original primary label hides.

cfb.coaching.reason: Tempo and halftime management claims need measurable definitions (second-half seconds per play versus first-half, end-of-half aggressiveness) before they carry weight.

cfb.kicker.reason: Field-goal chances at the end of each half add points in Q2 and Q4 totals; kicker range matters, but effect is limited to a single drive per half.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind picks up or fades during games, so period-specific effects exist, but the pregame forecast resolves only the average conditions; second-half wind forecast is less reliable.

m.rules_text.reason: Series differ: the 2H total includes overtime, the 4Q total excludes it, and the team-total 1H is stated in the title; each rung must be parameterised by its text.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Cross-rung consistency of period total quotes diagnoses stale quotes and the market's implied lattice, but it is price-derived and not an outcome driver.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: A backup quarterback lowers all period totals and widens uncertainty, but the period-specific effect is not shown; because period totals are noisy the signal-to-noise is low.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Opponent-adjusted offensive efficiency sets points per possession in each period; PPA for a single period is not stable, so the full-season value is scaled by the period's possession budget.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Defensive counterpart; same use, scaled by the possession budget; connectivity and sample caveats as in sides and totals archetypes.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: A single early turnover can settle a quarter total, but it is a realised event; regressing past turnover luck shifts the expected period total by tenths of a point and does not repay the complexity.

interactions.mechanism: Probability of crossing the 7.5 rung in a quarter jumps when the combined drive count falls from six to four, because with four drives it takes two scoring drives for more than seven points and the zero-scoring mass rises sharply; the effect of tempo is non-linear and strongest for slow-tempo pairings.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(quarter total >= 8) by predicted combined drives count and test a break at five drives.

interactions.mechanism: Fourth-quarter share of the game total depends on the expected gap: when the gap is small, Q4 holds the highest share (two-minute drills, urgency); when large, the leader's rate falls and the trailer's garbage-time scores partially offset, so Q4 share turns down.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate Q4 share by gap bins; compare to the pooled share and fit a piecewise function.

interactions.mechanism: End-of-half field-goal decisions interact with kicker range: a coach with a reliable kicker takes three points before the half, which raises Q2 and Q4 totals in lumps of three and thickens the pmf at 3 and 10, while an unreliable kicker leads to turnovers on downs and thinner mass at 3.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the Q2 total pmf by kicker accuracy tercile and decision-aggressiveness tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Wind that rises in the second half cuts the passing offence's scoring rate and the effect is amplified for fast-tempo pass-heavy offences, so the second-half total responds to the product of forecast wind trend and offensive pass reliance, not to the average forecast.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact forecast wind trend (late minus early) with pass-reliance terciles in a model of 2H and 4Q totals.

interactions.mechanism: The overtime increment exists only in games tied after regulation, which are close games where starters stay in and the 2H regulation total is least compressed by blowout management; so the increment is not independent of the regulation second-half total and adds right-tail mass exactly where the 6.5 rung is least at risk.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare 2H totals including overtime against regulation 2H totals, split by pre-game absolute margin bins, and test whether adding the increment to a regulation pmf reproduces the empirical 2H distribution.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at about four combined drives, weak above six
nonlinearities.why: The count of scoring trials is small, so each lost drive removes a large fraction of expected points; the probability of a scoreless period is convex in drive count.

nonlinearities.shape: Point mass at 0 and lumps at 3, 6, 7, 10; survival function is stair-stepped, not smooth
nonlinearities.why: The probability that a quarter total exceeds 7.5 differs by about a third from the probability it exceeds 6.5 because 7 is the most common touchdown outcome; a continuous distribution cannot reproduce that.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise: no effect until lead exceeds about three scores, then offsetting declines and increases
nonlinearities.why: Late leads change who scores and how fast the clock moves only beyond a threshold; below it the quarter looks like a competitive one.

contract.settlement_definition: Season futures settle on the resolved season result: win-total markets (KXNCAAFWINS, 12 or more wins) count only official regular-season games; undefeated markets count regular-season games only, and home-undefeated counts only games at the team's official home stadium (neutral sites excluded); conference champion markets settle on winning the conference championship game and qualifier markets on being in it (read only from the SEC text 'wins the 2026 College Football SEC Championship Game' and the Big Ten/C-USA qualifier texts; Ivy League has no championship game, so that reading cannot hold there, and other conference series are TITLE_ONLY); bowl-selection settles on being selected, not on playing; playoff-stage markets settle on qualifying for the CFP, quarterfinals, semifinals or championship game; regular-season top-N finish markets resolve all tied teams as achieving the position; head-to-head wins resolve a Tie leg when equal.

rules_evidence.quote: Only official regular season games count towards the team's win total. Ties do not count as wins.
rules_evidence.establishes: Win totals exclude conference title, bowl and playoff games, so the contract is a count over the regular-season schedule.

rules_evidence.quote: The market resolves to Yes if Wyoming has been selected to play, regardless of whether they actually compete in a bowl game or the College Football Playoff.
rules_evidence.establishes: Bowl contracts settle on selection, so opt-outs and cancellations after selection do not matter and the decision-maker (bowl committees) matters.

rules_evidence.quote: all tied teams will resolve as having achieved that position
rules_evidence.establishes: Regular-season top-5 finishes are decided by conference record and ties pay every tied team, which makes the market monotone in ties.

rules_evidence.quote: Neutral site games do not count as a home game for either team.
rules_evidence.establishes: Home-undefeated contracts need the venue designation of each game, so neutral and bowl-week sites alter the product of probabilities.

rules_evidence.quote: Conference championships, bowl games, and College Football Playoff games do not count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Head-to-head win markets compare regular-season win counts only and include a Tie leg when equal.

rules_evidence.quote: after Issuance and before the 2030-31 college football season
rules_evidence.establishes: Qualification-before-2030 market spans multiple seasons, so it is a multi-year hazard of making the playoff rather than a single-season probability. It also depends on the Issuance date (only qualification events after issuance count) and on the CFP format over 2026-2029 (12 or 24 teams), neither of which the sampled text fixes.

variants_and_edge_cases: The archetype contains single-season counts (WINS, UNDEFEATED), conference structure events (SEC/ACC/B12/B10/MAC/AAC... champion and qualifier), selection outcomes (BOWLGAME, PLAYOFF, QF, SF, FINALIST, SEED, TOPSEED, CFPCONF), a multi-year event (TFUT before 2030) and a combination event (KXNCAAFLSUTEX2X: LSU beats Texas in the regular season and wins the national championship).
Selection-versus-participation: BOWLGAME settles on being selected, whereas PLAYOFF and QF depend on committee selection and format rules that differ by season (number of teams, auto bids, seeding).
Regular-season top-N finish markets pay all tied teams, a ties rule that makes probabilities sum above one across teams.

Several series (SEED, TOPSEED, CFPCONF, LSUTEX2X, CONFMATCHUP, AAC/MAC/CUSA qualifiers) have no sampled rules text and are TITLE_ONLY here; some titles (Pac-10 Champion, FCS champion) refer to non-FBS or defunct entities and their settlement is not inferable.
Realignment: the Pac-12 champion and qualifier markets in 2026 imply a reconstituted conference with new members and game formats not in historical data.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official NCAA, conference and CFP committee results (final standings, official conference championship result, CFP selection show); the Kalshi text cites Source Agencies for some markets but names no provider for win counts.
