mechanism.summary: Season-level outcomes are functions of the whole schedule and of several layers of rules: team strengths are uncertain and correlated draws (with shocks from quarterback injury), each game is a noisy contest whose probability depends on site, rest and matchup, regular-season wins determine conference standings through unbalanced schedules and tiebreakers, conference champions and ranked teams are selected by committee into a bracket whose size and seeding rules vary by season, and long-dated contracts add a random walk of program strength. Settlement wording (regular season only, selection not participation, ties paid to all) changes which function of the simulation is the target.

stages.name: Team-strength prior with correlated uncertainty
stages.description: Start-of-season ratings combine last year's performance regressed by returning production, recruiting talent and portal changes; the uncertainty is large (several points) and shared across a team's games, and connectivity is thin across conferences. In-season, ratings update by results, but the same posterior draw affects every remaining game, which creates correlation that drives the tails of win-count contracts.
stages.distribution: Latent Gaussian rating vector with prior SD 5-6 points, shrinking with games; joint posterior with positive correlation across a team's games.

stages.name: Quarterback and key-player shocks
stages.description: Single-player availability alters a contender's rating by several points; the probability of the starting quarterback missing at least one regular-season game is large enough to matter, and the replacement quality varies widely. These shocks generate the heavy lower tail of team strength and lower the favourite's title concentration.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per game with heavy-tailed rating impact; mixture over games missed.

stages.name: Schedule path and game outcomes
stages.description: Each remaining game has a win probability from the rating difference, home-field edge and rest; the regular season win count is a Poisson-binomial with correlated draws, and special counts (undefeated, home-undefeated, head-to-head wins) are products or comparisons of these. Unbalanced conference schedules matter because teams in the same conference do not play each other equally.
stages.distribution: Poisson-binomial (correlated) counts; undefeated probabilities are products of per-game probabilities so tiny differences compound.

stages.name: Conference standings, tiebreakers and title game
stages.description: Conference records determine standings; ties are broken by head-to-head, common opponents and other conference-specific rules, which are nonlinear in the remaining schedule. The title game pairs the top teams under the season's format; the champion is the winner of that game or the top team under the format, and a tied top-N finish pays every tied team.
stages.distribution: Discrete order statistics with tiebreaker thresholds; probabilities depend on small differences in head-to-head results.

stages.name: Committee selection and bracket path
stages.description: The CFP committee ranks teams by resume rather than by rating; conference champions and a seeding rule determine who enters the bracket and where; rank moves slowly week to week and is sensitive to who loses to whom. Berth, seed, quarterfinal, semifinal and finalist probabilities are bracket-path products and depend on the format in force that season.
stages.distribution: Ordinal selection with inertia; bracket progression product of conditional win probabilities with seed-dependent opponents.

stages.name: Multi-year horizon and cross-contract coherence
stages.description: Long-dated contracts such as qualifying before 2030 require a multi-season random walk of program strength with coach exits and recruiting momentum; all futures are linked by shared draws, so probabilities across contracts must be coherent. Settlement wording choices (regular season only, ties) determine which function of the draws is evaluated.
stages.distribution: AR(1)-type mean reversion of team strength across seasons; union probability over four seasons.

stages.name: Bowl eligibility and selection
stages.description: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME is settled on selection, not participation: a team needs 6 wins (or an APR-ranked 5-7 fallback when eligible teams fall short of slots), then competes for its conference tie-in slots, with the CFP taking top teams first and bowl committees choosing the remainder; the contract list of eligible bowls excludes FCS playoffs.
stages.distribution: Threshold event on a win count (>=6) combined with a slot-shortage regime; bubble teams (5-7 to 6-6) carry the probability mass while 8-win teams are near-certain.

stages.name: Lower-division and Ivy champion mechanics
stages.description: FCS, D3 and Ivy League champion markets are filed here but follow different formats: FCS has a seeded playoff bracket, D3 a larger bracket, and the Ivy League has no championship game and decides the title on conference record with possible shared titles; each needs division-specific ratings rather than SP+.
stages.distribution: Single-elimination bracket survival for FCS and D3; a conference-record race with ties for the Ivy League.

talent_strength.note: Preseason and in-season ratings with correlated uncertainty plus a multi-year trajectory.

opponent_matchup.note: Season-level outcomes aggregate dozens of games, so unit-level matchups are second-order relative to schedule composition and rating uncertainty; matchup effects are absorbed into game win probabilities in the schedule vector.

role_personnel.note: Quarterback identity and replacement quality; other positions are not separately modelled for season contracts.

availability_news.note: Injury hazard and portal/eligibility events; no official injury feed exists.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach quality and coaching changes affect multi-year program strength and in-season stability, but no input defines coach effects separately from team ratings for futures; the program trajectory index only includes tenure and contract status.

environment.note: Weather and venue effects act per game and wash out over a season-long schedule except for the home-field component, which is carried in game win probabilities through the site term.

game_context_script.note: In-game script matters for margins but season contracts depend on win/loss only, so score-state effects do not enter beyond the game win probability; scoring margin affects only ratings.

pace_volume.note: Pace and possession counts determine per-game scores, not season outcomes directly; the count of games is fixed by the schedule and counted without volume.

efficiency_conversion.note: Efficiency enters through opponent-adjusted ratings and luck-adjusted records.

distribution_variance.note: Correlated rating draws and the Poisson-binomial distribution of wins; the simulation output (season_sim_distribution) is WEAK as an input and futures_coherence is BENCHMARK_ONLY, both removed.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Schedule path, bye and rest, and committee behaviour.

officiating_rules.note: Format, tiebreaker and title-game rules are the rule layer.

settlement_contract.note: Regular-season-only counts, selection not participation, ties paid to all, neutral exclusion and multi-year window.

cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.label: Remaining-schedule game win probability vector
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.mechanism: Game-by-game win probabilities for every unplayed game, from non-market ratings with site, rest and injury state.
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.rationale: Futures contracts on wins, undefeated seasons, conference title and playoff berth are functions of the whole schedule: a team's chance of 12 wins depends on the order, site and quality of each remaining game, and on correlated rating uncertainty; a scalar strength-of-schedule loses the product structure that drives P(undefeated).
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.measurement: For each team and each unplayed game compute P(win) = logistic(rating_diff / 13.5 + site_effect) using non-market ratings (SP+ or own, updated through the latest completed week), site effect 2.5 points home / 0 neutral, rest-adjust only for known byes; carry rating posterior SD into correlated draws (see cfb.rating_posterior_draws). Output vector and its Poisson-binomial distribution of wins. As-of the most recent Sunday.
cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities.why: Win-total, undefeated, home-undefeated, head-to-head wins and conference-title contracts all reduce to this vector plus rules.

cfb.rating_posterior_draws.label: Correlated rating posterior draws for season simulation
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.mechanism: Joint posterior samples of all team ratings so that uncertainty is shared across the games of a team and across teams in a conference.
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.rationale: Treating game outcomes as independent given point estimates understates the variance of season totals: a team whose true strength is 3 points above the estimate wins more of every remaining game. Joint draws also propagate connectivity uncertainty across conferences, which matters for conference win counts and playoff selection of Group-of-Five teams.
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.measurement: Bayesian rating model fitted to FBS game margins with team-level latent strength, home-field and prior from last season (shrinkage by returning production); draw 4000 posterior samples of the rating vector as of the latest week; for each sample simulate remaining games with game noise SD 13 points and add portal-churn variance inflation to the prior. Keep draw ID for cross-contract consistency.
free_sources: CFBD games and returning production (free key)
cfb.rating_posterior_draws.why: Correlated uncertainty is the main reason conference win-count markets and champion probabilities are fatter-tailed than independent-game simulations.

cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.label: CFP committee selection and ranking model from resume metrics
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.mechanism: Predicted committee rank from record, strength of record, quality wins and losses, conference champion status and previous ranking.
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.rationale: Playoff berth, seed and top-N ranking contracts are decided by a committee, not by the ratings: the committee emphasises wins over ranked teams and conference championships, penalises losses depending on opponent and timing, and moves slowly week to week. A rating-only model misses the selection layer.
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.measurement: Fit an ordered-response or rank regression for each committee release 2014 to latest: rank ~ ESPN Strength of Record or equivalent resume metric (computed from own ratings if unavailable), number of wins over top-25 and top-50 opponents, losses (count and margin), head-to-head, conference-champion flag, previous week rank (inertia coefficient), and week index; evaluate by rank error and by the probability of making the field. Output predicted rank distribution for each team at each future release date.
free_sources: ESPN FPI/Strength of Record pages (free scrape)
cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model.why: The contracts on playoff, quarterfinal, semifinal, seed and conference representation are selection outcomes whose mapping from results is committee-specific.

cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.label: Conference membership, schedule format and title-game rules by season
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.mechanism: Season-specific table of conference members, number of conference games, title game participants rule and tiebreakers.
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.rationale: Realignment changes the set of teams and the format of every conference contract (for example a reconstituted Pac-12, divisionless Big Ten and SEC, Big 12 title game with the top two teams); a historical conference average built on old membership misprices strengths and tiebreaker paths.
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.measurement: Maintain a table keyed by (season, conference, team) with membership dates, number of conference games (8 or 9), who plays whom (unbalanced scheduling), title game qualification rule (top two by conference winning percentage with tiebreak order), and champion determination. Update on realignment announcements; version by effective date; use to compute valid conference simulations.
free_sources: CFBD teams and conferences endpoints (free key)
cfb.conference_membership_and_schedule_m.why: Conference champion, qualifier and top-finisher markets depend on structure, and the 2026 season contains markets for conferences with changed membership.

cfb.program_trajectory_index.label: Program trajectory index for multi-year contracts
cfb.program_trajectory_index.mechanism: Composite of coach tenure, recruiting trend, portal net value, financial resources and past performance for the next four seasons.
cfb.program_trajectory_index.rationale: KXNCAAFTFUT asks whether a team makes the CFP before 2030, which cannot be answered with this year's rating alone: it depends on coach stability, talent pipeline, and revenue-sharing resources over four seasons, and on a random walk of team strength with regression to the mean.
cfb.program_trajectory_index.measurement: Annual team strength follows an AR(1) process: rating_t+1 = mu + 0.7 (rating_t - mu) + shock with shock SD 4 points (placeholder values 0.7 and 4, unsourced and unfitted; to be estimated on 2014-2025 rating changes) augmented by observed 3-year recruiting rank trend, portal net transfer rating change and head-coach tenure/contract status; simulate 4 seasons ahead, add coach-exit hazard and realignment membership, compute P(at least one CFP berth) per path. As-of preseason, updated at the portal window.
free_sources: CFBD talent and portal endpoints (free key)
cfb.program_trajectory_index.why: Only a multi-season strength process with program inputs can price long-dated qualification contracts.

cfb.qb_availability_hazard.label: Starting-quarterback availability hazard and replacement path
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.mechanism: Probability distribution of quarterback games missed for each contender over the remaining schedule, with the backup's quality.
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.rationale: Top-heavy playoff and title contracts depend on single-quarterback injuries: with an annual per-game miss rate near several percent the chance of losing the starter for at least one game across 12 games is substantial, and the drop to the backup's strength is large; ignoring it makes title probabilities too concentrated.
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.measurement: Per-game probability that the starter misses a game = base rate estimated from FBS history (to be measured, assume a few percent per game) x mobility/rushing-volume multiplier (designed rushes per game relative to norm) x prior injury history flag; backup rating from prior-year snaps and recruiting composite with shrinkage k = 100 dropbacks; combine in the rating draw to get a mixture over games missed. As-of weekly.
free_sources: CFBD player usage and rosters (free key)
cfb.qb_availability_hazard.why: Supplies the injury-driven fat tails to team strength draws used in all season-level contracts.

cfb.bowl_selection_state.label: Bowl eligibility, slot balance and conference tie-in selection model
cfb.bowl_selection_state.mechanism: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME settles on being selected (not playing) for a certified Division I bowl or the CFP: the chain is 6-win eligibility, the count of eligible teams against bowl slots, conference tie-in order, bowl committee choices and top teams taken by the CFP.
cfb.bowl_selection_state.rationale: Selection is not a function of wins alone: when eligible teams (6 or more wins) exceed slots, the weakest eligible teams miss out; when slots exceed eligible teams, 5-7 teams are taken (typically ranked by APR, a rule that changes by season); a conference with more eligible teams than tie-ins sends the surplus to open slots with bowls choosing by expected draw and travel, so a 6-6 mid-major is a bubble case while a 7-5 power team is safe.
cfb.bowl_selection_state.measurement: Per simulation of the season (the cfb.rating_posterior_draws and remaining-game win probabilities), compute each team regular-season wins, flag eligibility at >=6 wins (and, for 5-7 teams, an APR-ranked fallback list), count eligible teams per conference, allocate teams to bowl slots by the season tie-in table (conference, pick order, bowl slot count 2026 list from the rules text) with a selection score of wins, rank and historical draw (seed to be fitted on bowl selections 2014-2025), and remove the CFP field first. Output P(selected) per team and per-conference shortage probability of eligible teams below slots. Re-run weekly; the bowl list is the one in the contract text.
free_sources: CFBD games and bowl records (free key)
NCAA bowl lists and APR releases (free scrape)
raw_data: bowl tie-in table by conference and year
cfb.bowl_selection_state.why: KXNCAAFBOWLGAME (sampled WYO, rules text: selected to play in a bowl game or the CFP, regardless of whether they actually compete; only NCAA-certified Division I bowls count) needs eligibility and slot-balance logic that no win-total or title model supplies.

cfb.lower_division_title_model.label: FCS, Ivy and lower-division title bracket model
cfb.lower_division_title_model.mechanism: For FCS, D3 and Ivy League champion markets: team strength from FCS-specific results and the postseason format (FCS playoff bracket and seeds; Ivy League has no title game and awards titles on conference record, possibly shared).
cfb.lower_division_title_model.rationale: FBS ratings (SP+) do not cover these teams; FCS results require their own rating from scores with large mismatch capping, a 24-team bracket with seeds and byes, and the Ivy champion is decided by conference record with possible co-champions, so a market on a single Ivy champion depends on tie handling in the contract (unread, title only).
cfb.lower_division_title_model.measurement: Fit an Elo-style rating on FCS (and D3/Ivy) game scores 2014 onward with margin cap 21 points, home-field 2.5 points, preseason carry-over 0.7 shrunk to conference mean, and rating SD from the game count; simulate the conference race (Ivy: record-based, shared title probability reported separately) and the FCS bracket from the announced seeds, 20,000 runs, weekly. Output P(champion) per team and P(co-champion) where applicable. No market input; as-of last completed week.
free_sources: NCAA statistics and FCS schedules (free scrape)
raw_data: FCS, D3 and Ivy game results
FCS playoff bracket and seeds by season
cfb.lower_division_title_model.why: KXNCAAFCS, KXNCAAFFCS, KXNCAAFD3 and KXNCAAFIVY are TITLE_ONLY outright markets on divisions and a conference that the FBS-centred inputs do not cover.

cfb.standings.reason: Conference standing and tiebreaker state decides title-game and champion contracts, but the label bundles three different things (standings arithmetic, tiebreaker rules and a CFP ranking model); the tiebreaker and championship-game qualification rules should be separate rule tables by season and conference.

cfb.playoff_format.reason: Format rules (number of teams, automatic bids for conference champions, seeding method) determine how strength becomes berth, seed and finalist probabilities and change by season; it is a rule table mislabelled as market structure, and 2026-27 details beyond the 12-team model are not verified.

cfb.market_ratings.reason: Strength backed out of futures or game prices is the comparator for edge; as an input it removes the possibility of independent information and imports the quote's errors into every conditional probability.

cfb.sp_plus.reason: A second independent estimate of team strength; for futures the preseason SP+ is mostly a function of returning production and recruiting, so it is correlated with roster_continuity and talent.

cfb.roster_continuity.reason: Returning production sets the preseason prior width; its weight decays as games are played, and it overlaps with transfer_roster which should be merged into a net production measure.

cfb.talent.reason: Recruiting composite gives a durable ceiling and depth prior; most useful for multi-year contracts (KXNCAAFTFUT before 2030) where it persists, much less for a team whose current-year rating is known.

cfb.schedule_strength.reason: A scalar summary of remaining difficulty loses the sequence, home/away and rest of each game; the simulation needs a game-by-game vector of win probabilities (cfb.remaining_game_win_probabilities) of which this scalar is a derived summary.

cfb.pythag_luck.reason: Close-game record luck regresses; matters for ranking resume (committee looks at record) and for expected wins when only the record is observed, but small by comparison with the schedule path.

cfb.polls.reason: Generic label (category other); the useful part is a measurable model of how committee and AP rank respond to results, which is separately handled in the polls archetype; attach as a feature of committee behaviour, not as a mood indicator.

cfb.qb.reason: Quarterback injury and regime drives title-odds variance for top-heavy contenders; as defined it mixes status and performance, and a hazard rate with replacement quality is the missing structural piece.

cfb.award_narrative.reason: No award series is attached to this archetype in the ledger (awards live in the awards_and_honors archetype), so Heisman narrative has no path into season-level conference, playoff or win-total contracts.

cfb.futures_coherence.reason: Sum-to-one and implication constraints across linked futures are price relationships used to detect stale quotes; they say nothing about team strength or schedule and cannot be inputs.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures de-vigged give a comparator for each contract; again a benchmark, not an input, and futures books carry large holds that must be removed.

m.rules_text.reason: Settlement wording differs across series: regular-season only (wins, undefeated), selection not participation (bowl), ties resolved to all-tied-yes (regular season top N), neutral sites excluded (home undefeated), multi-year window (TFUT).

cfb.transfer_roster.reason: Portal churn drives preseason rating changes and can swing a futures prior by multiple points; it is only valid for the roster known at the vintage date and needs a timestamped transfer table.

m.quote_history.reason: Futures quote history reveals when and how strongly the market reacted to results and injuries; useful to study efficiency and information timing, not an input.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Futures books are thin; depth governs executable size and not any determinant of the season outcome.

m.fees.reason: Fees matter more for long-dated futures held for months (capital lock-up) but have no relation to the football outcome.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest in futures indicate liquidity and crowding in popular contenders; not a determinant of results.

m.trade_tape.reason: Tape of futures trades shows informed flow around injuries or committee rankings; a validation tool, not a feature.

m.lifecycle.reason: For futures the lifecycle matters because contracts can settle early once mathematically decided (e.g., a team eliminated from a conference title) and because determination dates (bowl selection, CFP committee release) fix the information set.

cfb.season_sim_distribution.reason: This is the output of the season simulation, the thing being estimated, not an input; listing it as an input risks leakage and circularity, and it should be replaced by the simulation's ingredients (game win vectors, rating draws, rules).

interactions.mechanism: Playoff berth probability is a steep step in the number of losses: a team with zero or one loss is very likely in, a team with three losses rarely, and which side of the step the team lands on depends on who the losses came against and when; the committee's treatment of one loss also depends on conference championship status.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(berth) by loss count and quality of losses on historical committee years; fit a step with conference champion and loss-timing interactions.

interactions.mechanism: A contender's title odds are a mixture over quarterback health states: with the starter its rating is high, with the backup it falls several points, and the draws shared across games produce fat tails; top-heavy contenders (one dominant quarterback) have more mass in the downside branch.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate title odds with and without the hazard, and test whether realised outcomes of teams with elite QBs show larger deviations from rating-implied expectations.

interactions.mechanism: Conference championship qualification depends on unbalanced schedules and head-to-head tiebreakers: a team that has already beaten its closest rival holds the tiebreaker and needs fewer wins, so remaining head-to-head games have asymmetric value that a simple expected-wins model misses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare conference qualifier probabilities from a full tiebreaker simulation against a ranking by expected wins on historical seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Over a four-year horizon the contribution of current talent decays toward a program mean while portal and revenue resources renew it; the incremental value of an extra recruiting-class point is large in year one and small by year four.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit multi-season rating AR(1) with recruiting and portal covariates and test the lag structure of their coefficients.

interactions.mechanism: Selection rules differ between seasons (field size, automatic bids for champions, seed construction) so the same resume gives different berth probability under different formats; contracts for the same season must use the format regime in force, and the 24-team expansion market implies a possible future regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit berth probability separately by regime and test if pooling across formats worsens calibration.

nonlinearities.shape: Product structure: P(undefeated) = prod p_i; small per-game changes compound exponentially
nonlinearities.why: A team with 85 percent win probability in each of 12 games has a 14 percent chance of an undefeated season but at 90 percent it is 28 percent; the market price must reflect compounding, not averaging.

nonlinearities.shape: Steep logistic in loss count with a conference-champion shift
nonlinearities.why: Berth probability falls from near certainty at 0-1 losses to a small fraction at 3, and a shifted threshold for champions of strong conferences.

nonlinearities.shape: Positive skew in aggregate win-count variance from correlated draws
nonlinearities.why: The variance of the total of wins across a conference is greater than the sum of independent game variances because of shared rating uncertainty, producing fat tails in count markets.

contract.settlement_definition: KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL settles YES if the named team scores more than the half-point strike (for example New Mexico over 45.5) in the game; the sampled rules text does not state whether overtime points count. A game postponed but started within 48 hours stays open and settles on the official final result; otherwise a fair price. KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT (team rushing attempts) is a stat contract misfiled in this archetype (belongs with the team stat-count series), so claims about its inputs are conditional on that re-filing, with no sampled rules text, so its settlement scope is not known.

rules_evidence.quote: If New Mexico scores over 45.5 points in the New Mexico vs Nevada college football game originally scheduled for Nov 6, 2026
rules_evidence.establishes: The strike is a strict greater-than on one team's points, so 46 or more points are required; no push is possible.

rules_evidence.quote: If the game is postponed but begins within 48 hours of its originally scheduled start time, the market will remain open and resolve based on the official final result.
rules_evidence.establishes: Postponements under 48 hours do not void; beyond that the market resolves to a fair price per the same text.

rules_evidence.quote: New Mexico over 45.5 points scored
rules_evidence.establishes: This is the market title, not rules text: it confirms a one-team points total with a half-point strike and says nothing about overtime.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime treatment is not stated in the sampled KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL text (unlike 4Q and 2H contracts); a team that scores in overtime could cross the strike, and overtime frequency is asserted rather than sourced (to be measured by cfb.ot_model).

KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT (team total rushing attempts) is a stat-count series misfiled here (see series_mapping_issues); no rules text sampled, so the settlement of sacks and kneel-downs is unknown (NCAA stats count sacks as rush attempts, which is not confirmed in the contract).
Points scored by a team include defensive and special-teams touchdowns and safeties; the sampled text says scores over without exclusion of non-offensive scores.
A very high strike (45.5) for a team belongs to a mismatch or an elite offence and the ladder is nested with rungs down to the low teens.
Cancellation or non-start within 48 hours resolves to a fair price, so weather suspension of an unfinished game is a distinct edge case not covered by the sample.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official final result of the game per the Kalshi wording; the stats provider is not named in the sampled text.

mechanism.summary: A team's points equal its own drives times points per drive (plus non-offensive scores), where its drives are a share of the game's possessions that depends on the opponent's clock control and turnovers, and where points per drive come from the team's offence against the opponent's defence with a style-dependent split between passing and rushing. The central problem is that the team total is a one-sided slice of a game with a script: a favourite's scoring is capped by blowout management while the underdog's total is lifted by garbage-time drives and constrained by its own offence. The distribution is lumpy (3 and 7 multiples) with a long right tail from short fields and return touchdowns.

stages.name: Own possession count after opponent control
stages.description: The team does not get half the combined drives: the opponent's slow, clock-burning offence trims its chances, turnovers and special-teams plays create asymmetry, and quick scores return possession to the opponent sooner. Own expected drives equal a share of game drives that is estimated from drive-level records rather than from season plays per game.
stages.distribution: Count of own drives, roughly 10 to 14, Gaussian-like with SD of about 1.5; share varies with matchup tempo.

stages.name: Points per drive from offence against defence
stages.description: Own points per drive depend on the opponent-adjusted offence, the opposing defence's pass and rush components, red-zone finishing and kicker range; strengths are not symmetric because a pass-first offence meets only the secondary's quality while a run-first offence meets the front. Late personnel news on quarterback, line and skill players moves this term.
stages.distribution: Per-drive 0/3/7 mixture with team-specific TD share; mean points per drive about 2.0-2.4 for typical FBS offences with wide cross-team spread.

stages.name: Script cap or lift on the team's scoring
stages.description: Once the team leads by three scores the coach substitutes and runs the clock, capping its total; the trailing team passes more and benefits from garbage possessions. Persistence of scoring after a lead is coach-specific and creates a bimodal relationship between rating gap and team total: elite teams vs weak ones either reach 50 or stall at 38.
stages.distribution: Mixture: competitive-game regime (tight, near its mean) versus blowout regime (capped for leaders, lifted for trailers).

stages.name: Conditions and dependence on opponent score
stages.description: Weather affects pass-heavy attacks more, and the relationship between the team's points and the opponent's points (positive via pace, negative via clock control and script) determines the variance of the team total relative to the game total. The ladder must be consistent with the game total and spread distributions.
stages.distribution: Bivariate score distribution with regime-dependent correlation; wind effect threshold-like.

stages.name: Contract mechanics and stat-variant series
stages.description: The strike is a half-point greater-than on one team's points; overtime treatment is not stated; the archetype also contains a rush-attempt series whose count follows plays times run share (with sacks possibly counted as rushes in NCAA statistics) and is driven by script rather than scoring. Conditional input set: if overtime counts in KXNCAAFTEAMTOTAL, cfb.ot_model (P(tie after 60 minutes), overtime scoring; see the overtime archetype tie curve) adds an increment to the team points distribution; if not, it drops out.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from pmf to rung; for rush attempts a count with strong script dependence.

cfb.own_drive_share.label: Own share of combined possessions
cfb.own_drive_share.mechanism: Fraction of the game's total drives that the team receives, after turnovers, special-teams outcomes and the opponent's clock use.
cfb.own_drive_share.rationale: A team's points equal its drives times points per drive; its drive count is not half of the game total because turnover and quick-score differences give one side extra possessions, and a team that burns clock on its own drives reduces the opponent's possessions. A team total rung depends on its own count, not on the average pace.
cfb.own_drive_share.measurement: For each team compute its drive share = own drives / (own + opponent drives) in each of the last 10 games, opponent-adjusted by the opponent's mean share allowed, with 0.8 decay and shrinkage k = 5 games to 0.5; add components: average drive duration (own), opponent drive duration allowed, turnover differential per drive. Expected own drives = share x expected combined drives (non-market total pace). As-of last completed game.
raw_data: drive table with start/end clock and results
cfb.own_drive_share.why: Separates the team's scoring trials from the game's, which the existing pace input (plays per game) does not.

cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.label: Leader scoring persistence (points per minute when leading by 14+)
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.mechanism: How much a team keeps scoring after taking a large lead, versus pulling starters and running the clock.
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.rationale: A heavy favourite's team total lies in the tail of its ability: coaches like some that keep their offence on the field, while others run the ball and substitute early; the same rating produces team totals that differ by 7-10 points depending on persistence. The underdog's mirror image is garbage-time scoring.
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.measurement: For each team, points scored per minute of game time when leading by 14 or more in Q2-Q4, over 2 seasons with decay 0.5 per season, relative to the points per minute when within one score; shrinkage k = 60 minutes to the FBS mean; compute also the time of first substitution by backups (depth-chart snap shift) when available. Combine with the probability of reaching a 14-point lead from the rating gap to obtain expected own points.
free_sources: CFBD plays with score state (free key)
raw_data: plays with period, clock, score diff, offense
backup quarterback and running back snaps
cfb.leader_scoring_persistence.why: Directly governs the high rungs where a favourite is expected to reach 45+ points.

cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.label: Own-versus-opponent score covariance
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.mechanism: Covariance between a team's points and its opponent's points given the expected margin and total.
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.rationale: Own and opponent scores are positively correlated through pace and negatively through script and clock control, so the variance of own points depends on the regime; a team total over 45.5 is more likely in shootouts where both score, and less likely when the opponent runs the clock.
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.measurement: From FBS games since 2014, compute residual correlation between team points and opponent points after removing expected team points from non-market ratings, by bin of expected margin (-14 to +14) and expected total; shrink bin correlations to pooled correlation with k = 150 games. Use the covariance matrix to turn a game-level total and margin model into a joint bivariate distribution; check consistency with the team total ladder. Functional form: team points as negative-binomial scoring-drive counts joined by a Gaussian copula with rho = rho0 + rho1 x |expected margin| + rho2 x expected total (coefficients fitted by maximum likelihood on FBS 2014 onward; the sign change of rho is a hypothesis to test, not an assumption). Tail check: validate P(team points > 45) calibration on held-out games with expected team points above 38, since rungs like 45.5 sit in the far right tail.
cfb.team_pair_score_covariance.why: Ensures the own-score distribution is consistent with game total and spread distributions instead of being fitted separately.

cfb.script_rush_attempts.label: Script-driven team rush attempts including sacks
cfb.script_rush_attempts.mechanism: Expected team rushing attempts as plays times run share given the expected lead, counting sacks as rushing attempts under NCAA statistics.
cfb.script_rush_attempts.rationale: KXNCAAFTEAMRSHATT sits in this archetype and counts a team stat, not points; in NCAA statistics a sack is recorded as a rushing attempt with negative yards, so attempts rise with sack-prone offences, and run share rises sharply for leaders.
cfb.script_rush_attempts.measurement: Rush attempts = plays x run share, where run share = neutral-situation run share (first/second down, score within 7) + lead effect (piecewise: +0.10 when leading by 14+, -0.10 when trailing by 14+) estimated by logistic regression on historical plays, plus sack rate x dropbacks (NCAA convention to be verified in the official stat definition). Opponent run-defence adjust by opponent's attempts allowed; shrink with k = 6 games. As-of last game.
free_sources: CFBD plays with play types incl. sacks (free key)
cfb.script_rush_attempts.why: Provides the missing input for the rush-attempt series, whose variance sits in script and sack accounting rather than in scoring.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Defined as implied team means from game total and spread, which are both prices; the same split can be rebuilt from non-market expected margin and total, and the quoted version is useful only as the comparator for edge.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Own opponent-adjusted offence is the strongest determinant of the team's mean, but PPA converts to points only through drives and finishing, so it must be paired with drive count and scoring-trip finishing, not treated as a points estimate.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Opponent defence suppresses own points; its pass and rush components affect different offences differently, so the aggregate value understates the matchup term that the interactions below address.

cfb.pace.reason: Own tempo matters but the opponent's clock use limits possessions; own possession share, not own plays per game, is the relevant volume and the original label ignores the opponent's effect.

cfb.redzone.reason: Red-zone TD rate moves points per trip by up to a point per game but regresses heavily; a high rung like 45.5 requires several touchdowns where the rate matters, though the sample per season is small.

cfb.kicker.reason: Own kicker range and accuracy set the share of drives that end in 3; matters for mid rungs where a field goal decides the integer outcome, less for tail rungs.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: Own starting quarterback explains a large share of own-team scoring variance and is the main late news item; a backup also affects tempo and run share.

cfb.skill_avail.reason: Absent receivers or backs lower the ceiling and need replacement-quality estimates; effect smaller than quarterback and usually smaller than offensive line.

cfb.ol.reason: Own line continuity affects sack rate and run efficiency and thereby points; label mixes offensive and defensive lines, and the defensive-line part belongs to the opponent's matchup, not to own scoring.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: Strongly relevant here: a heavy favourite's team total is capped by starter removal and clock running, and an underdog's total rises with late garbage drives; the behaviour is coach-specific and sets the upper tail of the rung distribution.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind and rain affect own scoring according to the team's pass or run reliance; the effect must be crossed with style, not applied uniformly.

cfb.score_resid.reason: Residuals relative to lines tie the calibration to the market; the intended clustering at multiples of 3 and 7 can be modelled directly from team score pmf by drive outcomes without reference to quotes.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook team totals and spread-total implied splits are the comparator for edge; not an input for the same reason as for game totals.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Consistency of the team total ladder with the game total and spread ladders is a diagnostic of staleness; derived from prices and cannot explain scoring.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is the market's own output; it measures when information was absorbed (useful for timing studies and closing-line value) but is not a cause of the team total outcome and must not enter a fundamentals model.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread govern whether a team total edge is tradable, not whether the event occurs; keep for execution and sizing, not as an outcome input.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule changes net edge on team total contracts (largest near 50c) but has no causal link to the result; an execution parameter, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe liquidity and price reliability for team total quotes; useful to weight benchmark trust, irrelevant to the outcome process.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades show informed flow and fill realism for team total contracts; it is market microstructure used to validate fills, not a determinant of the outcome.

m.lifecycle.reason: Open/close/halt/postponement events matter here because the 48-hour postponement clause converts a delayed team total market to a fair-price settlement; needed to define the information set and void handling.

cfb.offense_style.reason: Option, air-raid and RPO styles change possession count and explosiveness; relevant to variance as much as to mean, and overlaps with pace and pass-rate descriptors.

cfb.secondary_coverage.reason: The pass half of the opponent defence; paired with cfb.run_defense (now attached) so the style x opposing unit interaction can be tested on both halves.

interactions.mechanism: A strong offence's expected total keeps rising with rating gap only until a three-score lead; beyond that, conservative coaches cut the team's points while persistent coaches keep scoring, so the response to rating gap flattens at a coach-specific level.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot team points versus pre-game gap by persistence tercile and test for a break at gap 21-24.

interactions.mechanism: A pass-first offence is hurt by a good secondary but not by a good front, and a run-first offence the reverse; the appropriate matchup term is the product of style share with the opposing unit's quality, not the sum of overall offence and defence.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit own points on style share x opposing unit allowed values; compare with additive offence-plus-defence baseline.

interactions.mechanism: A backup quarterback behind a depleted line loses more than either shock alone, while a healthy line with a backup can still produce points through the run game; the effect is conditional on the other components of the offence.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast team totals in games with QB change plus OL loss versus QB change alone and OL loss alone.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis, not an established effect: own and opponent points move together through pace but diverge through clock control; the correlation changes sign across regimes, so team total variance cannot be obtained from the game total variance by a fixed fraction.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate correlation of own and opponent points by expected margin and expected pace buckets; confirm sign flip.

interactions.mechanism: Above a wind threshold a pass-first team's scoring regime switches to short fields and field goals which are also limited by wind, while a run-first team is mostly unaffected; the team total's sensitivity to forecast wind is thus regime-dependent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare team points in windy versus calm games by pass reliance and kicker range.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave with a cap: team points flatten once the lead exceeds roughly 21
nonlinearities.why: A favourite does not keep scoring proportionally to its rating edge because starters leave and the clock runs; the cap differs by coach, so the high rungs are less probable than a linear rating-to-points map suggests.

nonlinearities.shape: Linear in drives but with threshold at about 9 drives: below that, the team total rarely exceeds mid rungs
nonlinearities.why: A team with few drives needs high efficiency to reach a high rung, and below some drive count the probability collapses faster than the mean implies.

nonlinearities.shape: Sign changes from positive (shootouts) to negative (clock control) across expected-pace regimes
nonlinearities.why: The variance of team points depends on the covariance regime, which alters tail probabilities of high rungs independently of the mean.

contract.settlement_definition: The live series are team or game touchdown counts and a first-team race, not named-player scorers: KXNCAAFTOTALTD counts all touchdowns by both teams (for example 8 or more), KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD counts a team's rushing touchdowns, TEAMRECTD receiving touchdowns, DSTTD defensive or special-teams touchdowns (one or more), and FIRSTTDTEAM settles on which team scores the game's first touchdown, including defensive and special-teams touchdowns, with a No team scores a TD outcome. Overtime touchdowns count (first or second overtime in the sampled text) and successful 2-point conversions do not. Postponement under 48 hours stays open; otherwise a fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: A touchdown scored by another player after recovering a fumble by the rushing player does not count as a rushing touchdown
rules_evidence.establishes: Rushing touchdowns are credited to the rusher only, so fumble-recovery touchdowns by teammates are excluded from the rushing count, a settlement detail that affects the label.

rules_evidence.quote: If the first touchdown of the game is recorded in overtime, then the market for that team still resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: The first-TD market spans the full game including overtime, so a game with no regulation touchdown still has a first-TD team.

rules_evidence.quote: Successful 2-point conversions, including those in overtime, do not count for this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Total touchdown counts exclude two-point conversions, so the count is of six-point scores only.

rules_evidence.quote: Any defensive or special teams touchdowns recorded during the first or second overtime periods counts toward the total.
rules_evidence.establishes: Defensive and special-teams touchdowns in overtime periods one and two count; strikes are one or more touchdowns.

mechanism.summary: Touchdown counts equal the number of scoring trips times the probability each trip ends in a six-point score, plus non-offensive touchdowns (their inclusion is read for KXNCAAFTOTALTD, KXNCAAFDSTTD and KXNCAAFFIRSTTDTEAM; for KXNCAAFTEAMTD it is assumed, no rules text), split into rushing, receiving and returns by goal-line play calling and turnover returns. Scoring trips follow possessions and efficiency (the same machinery as team and game totals), but the live contracts settle on counts of touchdowns and not points, so finishing (touchdown versus field goal) is the central variable. First-touchdown markets are a race between two arrival processes with a head start for the receiving team, and counts above the mean live in a heavy tail created by mismatches and shootouts.

stages.name: Scoring trips and touchdown conversion
stages.description: A team produces scoring trips (first downs inside the opponent 40) in proportion to its possessions and efficiency against the opposing defence; each trip ends in a touchdown with probability set by goal-line efficiency, play calling and kicker alternatives. Touchdown count rather than points is the quantity, so a field-goal-heavy offence has the same points but fewer touchdowns.
stages.distribution: Binomial or compound count of touchdowns per trip with overdispersion across teams and games.

stages.name: Touchdown type: rushing versus receiving
stages.description: Close-range plays favour runs and quarterback sneaks, longer scores favour receiving; the split depends on the offence's scheme, quarterback mobility and score state (leaders run, trailers pass). Backups and depth-chart roles change who scores but only marginally change the team's rushing count, and the fumble-credit rules decide edge cases.
stages.distribution: Multinomial split of touchdowns by type with team-specific share; shares shift with lead size.

stages.name: Race for the first touchdown
stages.description: The first team to score a touchdown is determined by the order in which two hazard processes first fire; the opening possession order, scripted opening drives and defensive scores matter, and there is a probability that neither team scores in the full game. Overtime touchdowns count, so a game with no regulation touchdown is still decided.
stages.distribution: Competing hazards with a deterministic head start for the opening receiver; a small point mass of no-touchdown games.

stages.name: Defensive and special-teams touchdowns
stages.description: Return touchdowns require opposing turnovers or kick-return opportunities and are rare, partly skill (ball-hawking defences, return specialists) and partly luck, with rule changes on kickoffs altering exposure. They add to totals and race markets but are excluded from the rushing and receiving counts.
stages.distribution: Rare-event Poisson with small rate (game probability of at least one on the order of 15 to 25 percent, to be fitted).

stages.name: Count dispersion, availability and settlement
stages.description: High-count rungs (total TDs of 8 or more, rushing TDs of 5 or more) are tail events where clustering in mismatches fattens the distribution; late availability and eligibility news affect team strength rather than the count directly. Two-point conversions never count; overtime touchdowns do.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial with dispersion that increases in expected total and gap; tail sensitivity to blowouts.

talent_strength.note: Team scoring efficiency at the touchdown level plus non-market opponent-adjusted strength (SP+, PPA) now attached; the benchmark team_total_split is removed.

opponent_matchup.note: Opposing defence TD per trip allowed by type and overall opponent-adjusted defence; cfb.dvp (named-position matchup, WEAK) removed.

role_personnel.note: Mobile quarterback and skill-player availability for the rushing/receiving type split; depth_chart and player_usage (WEAK, named-player only) removed.

availability_news.note: Quarterback status (the main news item) and skill-player absence shift the trip count and type shares; suspension_eligibility (WEAK) removed.

coaching_scheme.note: Goal-line play calling and scripted openers.

environment.note: Wind and rain (cfb.weather_pit) shift the run/pass touchdown split and the count; the size of the effect is unquantified (weather_effect_on_td_split).

game_context_script.note: Lead-dependent run share and opening possession.

pace_volume.note: Expected scoring trips = possessions (cfb.pace, cfb.drives) x trip rate; cfb.td_per_scoring_trip supplies only the per-trip conversion, so the volume side is measured by the attached pace and drives inputs.

efficiency_conversion.note: TD conversion and type, plus non-offensive scores.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest, rivalry and bowl stakes shift scoring slightly but there is no argument that they change touchdown-specific outcomes beyond the game-level scoring mean, so no separate input is justified for TD counts.

officiating_rules.note: Settlement rules for two-point conversions, fumble credit and overtime; targeting and other penalties are second-order.

settlement_contract.note: Counts exclude two-point tries, overtime touchdowns count in periods 1-2, race market includes defensive scores.

cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.label: Touchdowns per scoring trip (drives reaching opponent 40) with type split
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.mechanism: Expected touchdown count from the number of drives reaching scoring range and the touchdown conversion rate, split into rushing, receiving and non-offensive.
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.rationale: All live series count touchdowns, not points: a drive that ends in a field goal produces no TD, so TD count depends on finishing (TD versus FG versus turnover) more than on points; the type split determines TEAMRSHTD and TEAMRECTD.
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.measurement: For each team: trips = drives with a first down at or inside the opponent 40; TD per trip over last 10 games with 0.85 decay, opponent-adjusted by the opponent defence's TD per trip allowed, shrinkage k = 25 trips to the FBS mean; split of TDs by type (rush, pass, other) over 2 seasons with shrinkage k = 30 TDs. Expected team TDs = expected trips x TD per trip; variance from negative binomial with fitted dispersion.
raw_data: drives with start/end field position and result
scoring plays with type (rush, pass, return)
cfb.td_per_scoring_trip.why: Converts efficiency into the count variable the live contracts settle on, and separates rushing from receiving touchdowns.

cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.label: Goal-to-go and short-yardage run/pass mix
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.mechanism: Share of goal-line and short-field plays that are runs (including quarterback sneaks and designed runs) versus passes.
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.rationale: Within the same number of touchdowns, the split between rushing and receiving depends on goal-line play calling: option and power-run offences score rushing touchdowns at close range where spread passing offences score receiving touchdowns, and trailing or leading status shifts the mix.
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.measurement: Compute run share on plays inside the opponent 10 and on 3rd/4th-and-short, by team over 2 seasons with decay 0.5 per season and shrinkage k = 40 plays to the conference mean; add TD conversion rate by type; condition on score state with a logistic model (leading by 14+ increases run share by 0.10-0.15 in the fit). Output expected rushing and receiving TD counts given expected total TDs.
raw_data: plays inside opponent 10 with run/pass and result
cfb.goal_to_go_run_pass_mix.why: Controls the rushing versus receiving touchdown split: KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD (5+) and TEAMRECTD (1+) are functions of this mix.

cfb.first_td_race_rate.label: First-touchdown race (hazard and no-touchdown mass)
cfb.first_td_race_rate.mechanism: Rate at which each team scores its first touchdown, including defensive and special-teams touchdowns, and the probability that neither scores in the full game.
cfb.first_td_race_rate.rationale: First team to score a touchdown is a race between two hazards with a deterministic head start for the receiving team on the opening possession, and with a small chance that neither scores (low-scoring game); overtime still counts for this market.
cfb.first_td_race_rate.measurement: From games since 2014, model time to first TD per team as a piecewise-constant hazard by drive index; hazard depends on team TD per trip, drive pace, opening possession order (receive-first adds probability mass at drive 1) and opponent's early defence; shrink to league hazard with k = 10 games; compute P(team A first) = integral; add P(no TD in 60 min + overtime) from low-total regimes (calibrated on FBS history). As-of kickoff with opening possession probability from cfb.opening_poss. Non-offensive and overtime components: add a defensive/special-teams touchdown arrival hazard per possession of the opponent (from cfb.dst_td_propensity) that can fire before any offensive possession ends; the No-team-scores outcome mass = P(no TD in regulation, from the hazards) x [1 - P(tie after 60 minutes, cfb.ot_model) x P(a touchdown in overtime periods 1-2 | tie)], since the contract settles the first touchdown in the full game including overtime.
free_sources: CFBD plays and scoring plays (free key)
raw_data: scoring plays with time and drive index
cfb.first_td_race_rate.why: The first-TD market needs the order of arrival of two Bernoulli processes, not a count, and has an explicit No TD outcome.

cfb.dst_td_propensity.label: Defensive and special-teams touchdown propensity
cfb.dst_td_propensity.mechanism: Probability that a game contains at least one touchdown scored by a defence or special teams, from turnover returns, kick returns and blocked kicks.
cfb.dst_td_propensity.rationale: DST touchdowns require the opposing offence to turn the ball over in a returnable place or special teams to give returns; they depend on interception and fumble rates, return specialists and the rules for kickoff returns, and are rare events with fat tails.
cfb.dst_td_propensity.measurement: Expected DST TDs per team-game = interceptions forced per game x pick-six rate (shrunk k = 40 INTs to the FBS mean) + fumbles forced x return-TD rate + kick/punt return TD rate for the returner + blocked-kick rate, each opponent-adjusted by the opposing offence's turnover rate; game probability = 1 - exp(-lambda_total) with lambda total = sum of both teams. Kickoff rule regime recorded by season. As-of last game.
raw_data: plays with interception, fumble, return, blocked kick and TD flags
cfb.dst_td_propensity.why: Direct input for KXNCAAFDSTTD and a component of the first-TD and total-TD markets.

cfb.td_count_dispersion.label: Touchdown count dispersion and tail probabilities
cfb.td_count_dispersion.mechanism: Variance-to-mean ratio of team and game touchdown counts and tail probability of 5+ team rushing or 8+ game touchdowns.
cfb.td_count_dispersion.rationale: Counts like total touchdowns 8+ and rushing touchdowns 5+ sit in the upper tail where a Poisson underestimates the probability because scoring drives cluster in mismatches and shootouts.
cfb.td_count_dispersion.measurement: Fit a negative binomial to game TD counts by expected-total and gap bins from FBS 2014 onward: mean mu(bin) and dispersion r(bin); report P(N >= k) for k in 1..12 with a 95 percent interval from bootstrapped games; shrinkage to pooled dispersion with k = 150 games. For team rushing TD counts fit separately by team style bucket.
free_sources: CFBD games and scoring plays (free key)
raw_data: touchdowns by game and team and type
cfb.td_count_dispersion.why: Gives tail probabilities for high-count rungs where a continuous model fails.

cfb.td_rates.reason: Role-based anytime and first-TD scoring rates apply to named-player markets, but every live series in this archetype (first team TD, total TDs, team rushing/receiving TDs, DST TDs, team TDs) is a team or game count; per-role rates are not defined for them.

cfb.team_total_split.reason: Expected team touchdowns derived from implied team totals are derived from prices; the TD count should be built from drives and TD per scoring trip using non-market ratings, with the quote kept as the comparator.

cfb.player_usage.reason: Target, carry and snap shares allocate scoring among players but the live contracts count touchdowns by team or by type; only the rushing/receiving split of the team matters, which is a play-calling mix and not a player share.

cfb.qb_rushing.reason: Quarterback designed runs and sneaks produce a large share of goal-line rushing touchdowns, which count in KXNCAAFTEAMRSHTD; useful as the team-level rushing-TD share, not as a player-level scorer feature.

cfb.blowout_management.reason: In lopsided games the leader runs the ball with backups and the trailer passes late, shifting the rushing/receiving split and the total count; relevant to counts above 5 rushing TDs or 8 total.

cfb.skill_avail.reason: Absent receivers or backs matter for the type split and for the number of scoring drives only modestly; as a team-level input its effect is much smaller than for named-player markets.

cfb.depth_chart.reason: Which back holds the goal-line role changes the player scorer but not the team's rushing-TD count; relevant only if named-player series are listed, which the ledger does not currently show.

cfb.opening_poss.reason: Receiving the opening kickoff gives the first possession and raises the probability of scoring the first touchdown by a few points; the toss is unknown pregame so it is only a forecastable tendency.

cfb.first_drive.reason: Scripted opening-drive touchdown rate bears directly on the first-TD race but rests on about twelve drives per team-season, so it requires heavy shrinkage.

cfb.dvp.reason: Defence versus position is defined for named receivers and backs; a team-level rushing-TD or receiving-TD count is better matched with the opposing defence's TD rate allowed by type than with positional matchups.

cfb.in_game_exit_risk.reason: In-game injury or removal risk of a starter has little effect on a team's total touchdown count, and is a player-market concept; negligible here.

m.rules_text.reason: Contract definitions drive counts: two-point conversions excluded, overtime TDs counted, fumble recoveries not credited as rushing TDs, and the first-TD market counts defensive and special-teams scores; essential to the label.

cfb.suspension_eligibility.reason: Suspended players change who scores, not the count of team touchdowns; keep only for a future named-player market.

cfb.transfer_roster.reason: New transfers change goal-line roles in named-player markets; for team TD counts the effect is already inside team ratings and offensive style.

m.quote_history.reason: Kalshi price history is the market's own output; it measures when information was absorbed (useful for timing studies and closing-line value) but is not a cause of the touchdown count outcome and must not enter a fundamentals model.

m.orderbook_depth.reason: Depth and spread govern whether a touchdown count edge is tradable, not whether the event occurs; keep for execution and sizing, not as an outcome input.

m.fees.reason: Fee schedule changes net edge on touchdown count contracts (largest near 50c) but has no causal link to the result; an execution parameter, not an input.

m.volume_oi.reason: Volume and open interest describe liquidity and price reliability for touchdown count quotes; useful to weight benchmark trust, irrelevant to the outcome process.

m.trade_tape.reason: Executed trades show informed flow and fill realism for touchdown count contracts; it is market microstructure used to validate fills, not a determinant of the outcome.

m.lifecycle.reason: Open/close/halt/postponement events matter here because the 48-hour postponement clause converts a delayed touchdown count market to a fair-price settlement; needed to define the information set and void handling.

interactions.mechanism: Team rushing touchdowns equal TD count times rushing share, and the rushing share is higher with a mobile quarterback and a power-run goal-line mix; both the count and the share vary across teams, so the product has more spread than either factor.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit rushing TD counts with an interaction of expected TDs and goal-line run share; compare with an additive version.

interactions.mechanism: In a one-sided game the leading team runs near the goal line and uses backups, raising the rushing share and total TD count for the leader, while the trailing team throws and adds receiving touchdowns; the combined effect on high-count tails depends on the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rushing and receiving TD counts by gap bin and leader/trailer role.

interactions.mechanism: First-TD probability depends on the receiving team's head start and each team's early hazard, and defensive touchdowns add a third arrival channel that can reverse the order when the opposing offence is turnover-prone; the three are not independent because the same offence both scores and turns over.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(first TD by team) as a function of opening possession and turnover-proneness; test the interaction of receive-first with pick-six rate.

interactions.mechanism: A defensive or special-teams touchdown flips the game script, and the knock-on effect on the opponent's passing and rushing touchdown counts depends on the pre-game expected margin: it is large in an evenly matched game where the scorer's lead changes the trailing team's play mix, and small when the scorer is already a heavy favourite or the opponent is far behind anyway.
interactions.how_to_test: Using SP+ expected margin bins, compare rushing and receiving touchdown counts of the team that conceded a DST touchdown against those in games without one, and test whether the gap shrinks as the absolute expected margin grows.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy right tail: variance exceeds Poisson mean and grows with expected total
nonlinearities.why: The probability of 8 or more touchdowns is several times the Poisson value at the same mean because high-scoring teams cluster in shootouts and mismatches.

nonlinearities.shape: Head-start step for the receiving team plus a small point mass at no touchdown
nonlinearities.why: The opening possession order gives a discrete advantage that cannot be represented by a smooth rate, and some games have no touchdown at all.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in lead size: run share rises sharply beyond a 14-point lead
nonlinearities.why: Leading teams run in short yardage and burn clock, so the type split is sensitive to the lead once it is two scores.
