contract.settlement_definition: Voted-award series (AP conference Defensive Player of the Year, Biletnikoff, Bear Bryant Coach of the Year) settle YES if the named person wins the award in the stated season; if the player does not play in the season for any reason the market resolves No; if several people share the award, YES pays 1/N rounded down. Leader series (most rushing yards, passing touchdowns, receiving yards or sacks in Division I or a conference) settle on regular-season totals only, conference championship games excluded, with ties paying 1/N and No if the player does not play. Finalist markets settle YES if the player is named a finalist, and all resolve No if finalists are not announced before the winner. The draft-declaration market requires a public, unequivocal announcement of entry into the regular NFL draft before Feb 2, 2027.

rules_evidence.quote: If Will Heldt does not play in the 2026 college football season for any reason, the market for that player resolves to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: A player who is injured, transfers or is suspended out of the season resolves No, so participation is part of every voted-award contract.

rules_evidence.quote: If multiple players are tied for the most passing touchdowns at the end of the regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Leader contracts pay 1/N to tied leaders, so ties are not a push and share the payout; totals at the end of the regular season determine the result.

rules_evidence.quote: In the event that finalists are not announced and reported by one of the Source Agencies prior to the award winner being announced, then all markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Finalist contracts depend on the award body publishing a finalist list, a procedural risk independent of performance.

rules_evidence.quote: Rumors, speculation, projections, and statements that the player is considering entering do not count.
rules_evidence.establishes: The declaration must be an unequivocal public announcement, so information flow and the announcement window matter, and a later change of plans does not undo it.

rules_evidence.quote: If JaMarcus Shephard wins the Bear Bryant Coach of the Year award in 2026-27 college football season
rules_evidence.establishes: Coach awards settle on the award body's selection; no tie or no-play clause appears in the sampled text.

variants_and_edge_cases: Six different mechanisms share this archetype: conference leaders (cumulative stat order statistic), voted conference awards (AP voters), national position award (Biletnikoff), finalist selection, coach of the year, and a player decision (NFL draft declaration); the sampled series share only the participation and tie clauses.
The sampled AP conference awards (Defensive Player of the Year) and several others have status inactive in the evidence, so contract timing can lapse before the ballot is known.

Leader markets count regular season games only and exclude conference championship games; a player who transfers within FBS during the season carries his totals only if he remains in the named conference.
Ties in voted awards (co-winners) pay 1/N and ties in leader totals pay 1/N, so a rung probability sums over shared outcomes.
Title mentions Heisman and Defensive Heisman in the registered contract_types, but no live Heisman series appears among the sampled live series; the Heisman mechanism is not directly verifiable here.
contract.settlement_data_source: Award bodies' official announcements and Associated Press results for voted awards; official NCAA season statistics for leader markets; NFL early-entry lists and public announcements for the draft; Kalshi text refers to Source Agencies for some series.

series_mapping_issues.issue: Player career decision (public announcement of NFL draft entry), not an award or stat leader; shares the declare-for-draft leg with KXNCAAFTRANSFER in the coaching archetype

mechanism.summary: The archetype mixes order-statistic races on cumulative counting stats, voted awards decided by an electorate responding to visible statistics and team success, and discrete decisions by people (draft declaration, coach selection). For leader contracts, probability equals the chance that a candidate's final cumulative total exceeds all others': current total plus projected remaining production, which is a product of usage, efficiency, opponent and games remaining and is truncated by injury hazard. For voted awards the process is a vote-share contest whose determinants differ by award and electorate. Settlement clauses on participation, ties and announcement timing are decisive.

stages.name: Candidate pool and participation
stages.description: Only players who play contribute; the candidate pool for a stat leader is the few dozen high-usage backs, receivers, pass catchers or edge rushers, with injury and benching hazard removing some each week. A candidate who misses a game falls behind and a candidate who sits out the season resolves No, so participation is the first filter for every series.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli participation per game with fat-tailed season-ending probability; heavier for high-workload positions.

stages.name: Production accumulation to the end of the regular season
stages.description: Cumulative totals come from per-game production (usage times efficiency against each remaining opponent), the number of games left, and the team's offensive or defensive scoring script (a trailing team passes more, a leading team runs). The answer is the maximum across candidates, so closeness of competitors and correlation (teammates share team volume) determine probabilities.
stages.distribution: Sums of overdispersed per-game counts; maximum of correlated sums; ties possible.

stages.name: Electorate response for voted awards
stages.description: Voters see counting statistics, team record and ranking, and highlights, and award ballots are collected at a fixed date before bowls; electorates differ by award (AP voters for conference awards, a committee for position awards), and positional constraints (receiver for Biletnikoff) filter candidates. Vote share is a multinomial contest with winner-take-all payoff and ties when shared.
stages.distribution: Multinomial vote shares with concentration; winner-take-all contest; ballot date fixes the information set.

stages.name: Coach and decision-maker outcomes
stages.description: Coach of the Year is awarded for exceeding expectation, ranking and conference outcomes; the draft declaration is the player's decision determined by draft projection, eligibility and alternatives, and revealed by a public announcement before a deadline. These are not outputs of a game model; they are decision processes with hazards and information timing.
stages.distribution: Logistic probabilities with strong dependence on a single latent score (surprise for coaches, draft grade for players).

stages.name: Settlement mechanics and procedural risk
stages.description: Ties pay 1/N, non-participation resolves No, finalist markets resolve No if finalists are not announced, and the draft market needs an unequivocal public announcement; the regular-season-only window for leader contracts excludes the conference championship game and the bowl, so postseason production is irrelevant.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping with discrete tie fractions; procedural risk is a small probability mass.

talent_strength.note: Team success and coach expectation drive votes; individual player talent enters through production and draft grade.

role_personnel.note: Usage determines volume; quarterback role limited to the passing-touchdown leader.

availability_news.note: Injury, benching and transfer hazard; no official feed exists.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach of the Year; scheme shifts to usage are not separately defined.

environment.note: Venue and weather affect individual game production but over a season-long cumulative stat these wash out except through the opponent-adjusted per-game rates; no separate environmental input is justified.

game_context_script.note: Score-state effects (trailing teams pass more, leading teams run and rotate) change cumulative leader totals but no input models the script effect on a candidate's usage; its size relative to injury hazard is unknown.

efficiency_conversion.note: Per-game production per opportunity for offensive leaders (inside leader_race_state) and sack, TFL and pressure rates per pass-rush snap for defensive awards and leaders; the offence-only WEAK inputs are removed.

officiating_rules.note: Officials do not affect award voting or season totals except through statistical corrections; the relevant rules clauses (tie, participation) are carried under settlement_contract, not as an officiating input.

settlement_contract.note: Tie-sharing, participation and announcement clauses read from rules; some series have no sampled rules.

cfb.leader_race_state.label: Statistical-leader race state (current leaderboard plus projected remaining production)
cfb.leader_race_state.mechanism: Cumulative stat as of the query week for each candidate plus a distribution over remaining production, from usage, efficiency, opponents and games left.
cfb.leader_race_state.rationale: Leader contracts (most rushing yards, passing TDs, receiving yards, sacks) resolve at the end of the regular season on cumulative totals, so the price is an order-statistic problem over several candidates with a current lead, a different number of games remaining and different injury exposure; ties pay $1/N. Note: this id bundles the leaderboard state (current total, gap to rivals, games remaining) with a projection; the state is the input and the overtaking probability is a model output built from it.
cfb.leader_race_state.measurement: For each candidate, mean per-game production over the last 6 games weighted 0.8 per game, shrunk toward prior-season rate with k = 4 games; adjust per remaining opponent by the opponent's allowed rate (opponent-adjusted), games remaining from the schedule, P(plays) from the hazard input; simulate remaining totals from negative binomial per game with candidate-specific dispersion, add to current total, and compute P(rank 1) with ties allocated 1/N. Update weekly; as-of the previous Sunday.
free_sources: CFBD player season and game stats (free key)
raw_data: player game logs with carries, targets, yards, TDs, sacks
cfb.leader_race_state.why: Turns the current leaderboard and projected remaining production into probabilities for the order-statistic contract.

cfb.player_participation_hazard.label: Player participation and season-ending injury hazard
cfb.player_participation_hazard.mechanism: Per-game probability that a candidate plays and the probability of a season-ending injury or benching, by position and usage.
cfb.player_participation_hazard.rationale: Contracts resolve to No if the player does not play in the season, and a candidate who misses games falls out of a counting-stat race; running backs and edge rushers have higher injury exposure than quarterbacks and are the main candidates of leader markets.
cfb.player_participation_hazard.measurement: Per candidate: P(miss a given game) = base rate by position (estimated from FBS history, to be measured; assume a few percent per game for backs) x workload multiplier (carries per game above the position median) x prior-injury indicator; P(season-ending) as a fraction of misses; combine across remaining games as a Bernoulli path. Redshirt and transfer eligibility flags enter as availability states. Weekly update with timestamped news capture.
cfb.player_participation_hazard.why: Controls how often a leader candidate drops out of the race or resolves No, directly shaping probabilities for later-season rungs.

cfb.award_vote_feature_model.label: Award-specific vote-share model features
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.mechanism: Candidate-level features that predict vote share for each award: counting stats, team record, ranking, position bias and highlight games.
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.rationale: Different awards have different electorates and different positional constraints: the Biletnikoff goes to a receiver, AP defensive player awards to defenders, and voters see box-score numbers and team results rather than efficiency grades; a position-agnostic Heisman narrative variable misses all of this.
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.measurement: For each award and year since 2010 fit a multinomial logit of vote share on: rank of the candidate's primary counting stat among the position pool (percentile), team win percentage and AP rank at ballot time, games played fraction, prior-year honours, and a position-group indicator; regularise with ridge (lambda chosen by leave-year-out); produce candidate probabilities with ties handled by 1/N rule where voters can share an award. Ballot date as-of cut.
raw_data: award winners and finalists by year
team record and rank at ballot time
cfb.award_vote_feature_model.why: Replaces the unmeasurable narrative input by features voters can observe, separately per award.

cfb.coach_overperformance_index.label: Coach overperformance index
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.mechanism: Wins above preseason expectation and rank change for a head coach's team, from non-market preseason ratings.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.rationale: Coach of the Year voting rewards teams that exceed expectations, not simply the best team; a coach who takes a team expected to win 5 to 11 wins is favoured over one at the top of the polls, but ranking and conference title also matter.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.measurement: Expected wins from non-market preseason rating and schedule (Poisson-binomial of game win probabilities) minus actual wins to date plus projected remaining wins; add change in AP rank from preseason to ballot date and a conference-title indicator; fit historical Coach of the Year winners 2005-2025 with a logit on the index, final record, final ranking, and first-year/turnaround flags. As-of ballot date.
cfb.coach_overperformance_index.why: Coach of the Year (KXNCAAFCOTY) is decided on surprise relative to expectation, which no other input measures.

cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.label: NFL draft declaration propensity
cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.mechanism: Probability that an eligible player announces entry to the NFL draft before the deadline given draft projection, eligibility and alternatives.
cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.rationale: The market KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE resolves on a public, unequivocal declaration before Feb 2, 2027; players with high projected picks declare at high rates, but eligibility (three years removed from high school), compensation in college (revenue sharing and NIL), injuries and coaching changes alter the decision, and a statement that a player will return does not count as an early No.
cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.measurement: Logistic hazard on: consensus draft rank (average of public big boards), draft-eligible indicator (years since high school graduation >= 3), draft stock change after the season, college compensation proxy, injury flag, coaching change; calibrate on 2015-2026 declarations using draft early-entry lists; as-of date-specific survival to the announcement window (typically before mid-January). Timestamped public statements are tracked separately.
cfb.draft_declaration_propensity.why: Directly models the decision process behind the draft-declaration series rather than treating it as an award.

cfb.defender_production_profile.label: Defender production and pass-rush usage profile
cfb.defender_production_profile.mechanism: For defensive voted awards (AP conference Defensive Player of the Year) and sack/tackle-for-loss leaders: the defender share of pass-rush snaps, pressures, sacks, TFL and havoc plays per game against the remaining schedule.
cfb.defender_production_profile.rationale: Defensive votes follow headline sacks and TFL plus team success, and a leader race in sacks depends on pass-rush snap volume, opponent pass-attempt volume and offensive-line quality rather than on rushing or passing efficiency; offence-centric inputs say nothing about it.
cfb.defender_production_profile.measurement: For each defender: sacks, TFL and pressures per pass-rush snap over the last 6 games with weight 0.8 per game, shrunk to a prior-season rate with k = 150 pass-rush snaps; expected snaps remaining = games remaining x snap share (last 4 games); opponent adjustment = opponent offence sacks-allowed rate relative to the FBS mean, with opponent pass attempts forecast from its pass rate; simulate remaining sacks per game as Poisson with a dispersion fit on 2014-2025 and add to the current total; for award votes include team rank and opponent-adjusted havoc rank. As-of the previous Sunday.
free_sources: CFBD player stats and PPA (free key)
raw_data: defender sacks, TFL and pressures by game
opponent sacks allowed and pass attempts
cfb.defender_production_profile.why: The four AP Defensive Player of the Year series and the sack/TFL leader series need defender production and pass-rush usage, which the offence-centric inputs do not carry.

cfb.award_narrative.reason: Narrative has no measurable definition as written and is Heisman-centric; the live series are stat leaders, AP defensive-player awards, Biletnikoff, coach of the year and draft declaration, none of which map onto one narrative score; it must be replaced by measurable vote-share features per award.

cfb.award_vote_distribution.reason: Historical vote-share distributions by award are the right base for voted contracts, but electorates differ by award (AP writers for conference DPOY, a foundation panel for Biletnikoff, a coaches or writers panel for coach awards), so it must be built per award and not pooled.

cfb.player_usage.reason: Carries, targets and pass-rush snaps are the volume that produces the counting stats which leader contracts settle on; the original secondary role understates it, since a leader is mostly a usage story with an efficiency multiplier.

cfb.pass_efficiency.reason: Of the live series only the ACC passing-touchdowns leader is a quarterback stat; efficiency per attempt is a weaker driver of a counting-stat race than attempts and team scoring, and it does not matter for defensive, receiver or coach awards.

cfb.qb.reason: Starting quarterback status and regime matter for the passing-touchdown leader and for team-success-based votes (coach awards), but are irrelevant to defensive and receiver awards; scope-limited.

cfb.qb_rushing.reason: Quarterback rushing adds to Heisman narratives but the live series count receiving yards, rushing yards (rarely led by a quarterback) and sacks; marginal relevance.

cfb.td_rates.reason: Touchdown rates by role translate usage into headline numbers for offensive voted awards, but none of the live series is an anytime touchdown market and the share of voter weight on touchdowns versus yards is not established.

cfb.standings.reason: Team record and ranking raise voters' support for individual awards and are the dominant input to coach of the year; use rank and wins above expectation rather than raw standing.

cfb.schedule_strength.reason: Voters discount production against weak schedules and the remaining schedule determines games left for a leader; two distinct uses that should be separated.

interactions.mechanism: A leader's probability is the product of being ahead and staying healthy: a candidate with a small lead and high workload faces a higher chance of falling behind because of injury, so the joint of current gap, workload and hazard shapes the probability more than the gap alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the race with and without the hazard and compare to realised outcomes of past leaders by workload tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Voters weight statistics by team success and discount production against weak schedules, so a candidate's effective support is production percentile times a team-rank factor times a schedule discount; the same stats on a ranked team and an unranked team yield very different vote shares.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit logit vote share with the product of stat percentile and team rank; compare with additive features.

interactions.mechanism: Hypothesis to test: a coach who beats expectation by many wins wins only if the team also finishes ranked or wins a title; above a threshold of wins above expectation the probability jumps, and below it conference rank decides.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate winner probability by bins of wins above expectation crossed with final rank across history.

interactions.mechanism: A strong season raises draft stock and the declaration probability, but an injury lowers both the award chance and the draft grade and can reverse the declaration decision; awards and declarations are correlated through the same season outcome.
interactions.how_to_test: Contrast declaration rates of award finalists versus non-finalists with similar pre-season grades, and with injury flag.

interactions.mechanism: Remaining schedule changes the leader's expected production, and for the passing touchdown leader it also depends on whether the quarterback keeps starting; a candidate with an easy remaining schedule overtakes only if his team continues to pass at the same rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised production in remaining games with projections split by remaining opponent rank and team pass rate.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in the gap: probability of overtaking falls rapidly once the lead exceeds about one game's production
nonlinearities.why: Remaining games contribute a bounded amount of production, so a lead above the remaining capacity is effectively decisive, making probabilities approach 0 and 1 faster than a linear lead model.

nonlinearities.shape: Winner-take-all concentration: vote share to winner probability is a steep softmax, not proportional
nonlinearities.why: A candidate with 40 percent share of expected votes wins far more than 40 percent of the time because winner-take-all amplifies leads.

nonlinearities.shape: Heavy-tailed: a small probability of immediate elimination with large impact, increasing in workload
nonlinearities.why: Season-ending injuries remove a candidate abruptly; the probability is small per game but compounds across the remaining games and concentrates in the highest-workload players.

contract.settlement_definition: These are event-by-date or categorical outcomes decided by people and institutions, not by a game: KXNCAAFCOACHLEAVE and COACHOUT settle YES if the named head coach is fired, resigns, otherwise leaves, or announces he will leave before the stated date (Dec 1, 2026 or Feb 1, 2027); KXNCAAFNEXTCOACH settles YES if the next permanent head coach officially announced is the named person (interim or acting coaches do not count) and resolves No if none is announced before Sep 1, 2027; KXNCAAFCFPEXPAND settles YES if the CFP has officially approved a fully adopted format with exactly 24 teams, confirmed by a Source Agency, after issuance and before Dec 2, 2026; CONFLEAVE and JOINCONF settle on an announcement, binding agreement, formal notice or settlement within the period even if the effective date is later; KXNCAAFTRANSFER is a multi-outcome market on a named player's destination.

rules_evidence.quote: must be fired, resign, or otherwise leave their position as head coach; or has announced that they will do so before Dec 1, 2026.
rules_evidence.establishes: An announcement of future departure counts, so retirement announcements and agreed exits resolve YES even if the departure takes effect later.

rules_evidence.quote: An interim or acting head coach does not count as the head coach for the purposes of this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Only a permanent head coach counts and the market resolves No if none is announced by Sep 1, 2027, adding a timing hazard.

rules_evidence.quote: a fully adopted CFP championship format with exactly 24 participating teams
rules_evidence.establishes: Approval must be binding and for exactly 24 teams, so intermediate announcements, studies or a different team count do not qualify.

rules_evidence.quote: LSU College Football team provides formal notice of withdrawal from the SEC during the stated time period.
rules_evidence.establishes: Several different formal steps qualify (announcement, binding agreement, notice, exit settlement), widening the event relative to an actual departure.

rules_evidence.quote: publicly announces or formally agrees to join the Big 12 during the specified time period
rules_evidence.establishes: A public announcement or formal agreement within the period qualifies regardless of the effective date.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolves Yes if Arch Manning officially withdraws his name from the NCAA Transfer Portal or announces withdrawal
rules_evidence.establishes: The market is a multi-outcome set; the staying outcome requires withdrawal or never entering, evaluated by the stated date.

variants_and_edge_cases: Coach-exit contracts differ only by named coach and window end (Dec 1 vs Feb 1), so the hazard must be integrated to the exact date; announcement of future departure counts, so a mid-season announced retirement resolves immediately.
NEXTCOACH resolves No for all candidates if no permanent coach is announced before Sep 1, 2027, and an interim hire does not count; candidates are mutually exclusive except through that No state.
CFPEXPAND needs a binding decision by an authorized governing body with exactly 24 teams confirmed by a Source Agency before Dec 2, 2026; the decision may take effect in a later season.

CONFLEAVE and JOINCONF are triggered by announcement, binding agreement, formal notice or settlement, not by effective membership change, and the sampled secondary text is truncated so additional triggers could exist.

TRANSFER outcomes are multi-way (stays, declares for the draft, commits elsewhere, possibly other); sum of probabilities must be one when all outcomes are listed, and the staying outcome is conditional on the portal behaviour.

KXNCAAFTRANSFER is a player decision filed with coach and governance events; its declare-for-the-draft leg is the same event as KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE in the awards archetype, so the two series should share one declaration model, and as listed the transfer model has no usable primary feature because compensation offers are unobservable.
contract.settlement_data_source: Source Agencies named in the rules (credible news reports, official school or conference announcements); the exact list of Source Agencies is not in the sampled text.

series_mapping_issues.issue: Named-player multi-outcome decision (stays at Texas / declares for the draft / commits elsewhere); the declare leg duplicates KXNCAAFDRAFTDECLARE in the awards archetype and the destination depends on unobservable NIL offers

mechanism.summary: These contracts depend on decisions by people and institutions made under constraints that can be written down: a head coach leaves when performance relative to expectation, contract cost, administration and outside opportunities combine to cross a decision threshold, concentrated at the end of the regular season and after bowls; a hire follows a vacancy through a candidate pool and a timing process; governance outcomes follow vote requirements and stakeholder positions on a meeting calendar; realignment follows contracts and procedures; a player's destination follows portal rules, need and compensation. Information arrives as dated reports, so the timing of information and the definition of which announcement counts are decisive.

stages.name: Triggering conditions relative to expectation
stages.description: Coach exits and some governance events are triggered when outcomes fall short of expectations: record against a preseason expectation, losing to a rival, missing a bowl. The trigger raises a decision-maker's willingness, but the realised decision is tempered by cost and calendar; expectation must be defined from ratings rather than from the final record alone.
stages.distribution: Hazard that increases with shortfall; concentrated in the last three weeks of the regular season and the first weeks after bowls.

stages.name: Constraints: cost, process and contracts
stages.description: A decision becomes feasible only if its cost is bearable: buyouts constrain firing, grant-of-rights and exit fees constrain conference moves, voting thresholds constrain CFP changes, and portal windows constrain transfers. These constraints are knowable from documents and calendars, and they change the date at which the event can first happen.
stages.distribution: Step functions in date: probability mass appears only after the feasibility date; before it the hazard is near zero.

stages.name: Candidate pool and destination choice
stages.description: When a vacancy opens or a player enters the portal, the outcome is categorical among a limited candidate set, determined by need, relationships, compensation and the competition among candidates; timing matters because a market can resolve No if no hire occurs before the date.
stages.distribution: Multinomial choice with a No-outcome mass for timing failure; sharp updating on credible reports.

stages.name: Information flow and credibility of reports
stages.description: Because decisions are private until announced, outcomes are forecast from reports of varying reliability; the timing of leaks (an AD meeting, a plane tracked, a source quoted) determines when probabilities should change. The rules define which announcements count, so a statement that does not meet the definition leaves the market open.
stages.distribution: Jump process in beliefs triggered by reports; reliability of sources varies by reporter; the event itself is a point-in-time announcement.

stages.name: Settlement definition and window
stages.description: Each rule picks a specific definition: announcement of future departure counts for coaches, binding adoption of exactly 24 teams for the CFP, announcement or formal notice for conferences, and the staying outcome for a transfer; windows end on specific dates (Dec 1, Dec 2, Jan 1, Feb 1, Feb 2, Sep 1), so the same underlying decision can resolve YES or NO depending on its timing.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the event time and type to the contract outcome.

talent_strength.note: Team strength matters only through performance relative to preseason expectation for coach exits; no player or team strength input applies to governance or realignment series.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent or unit interaction in a personnel, governance or realignment decision; matchup structure is irrelevant to when a coach is fired or a conference votes.

role_personnel.note: Candidate and destination pools by role and need.

availability_news.note: Dated reports and statements fix the information set; source reliability weights are part of the candidate and governance models.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach tenure and results; scheme and tempo content of cfb.coaching is irrelevant here.

environment.note: Venue, weather and altitude play no role in whether a coach leaves, a conference realigns or the CFP changes its format; the only environment is institutional (market and media-rights context), which is handled by the governance state.

game_context_script.note: In-game flow does not apply; the only game-linked effect is that a single result (a rivalry loss or a lost bowl-eligibility game) can trigger a decision, which is carried by the expectation-shortfall and rivalry features.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities or possessions; these are binary or categorical decisions with a time window, so pace and volume do not describe the outcome process.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-play rate exists; the closest analogue is the hit rate of reporters' leaks, which sits in the information-flow stage rather than in a performance conversion input.

distribution_variance.note: Calendar-aware base rates and hazards with uncertainty from small samples (15-25 FBS coach changes per year).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Stakes, contract incentives and expectation shortfall.

officiating_rules.note: Governance rules: voting thresholds, grant-of-rights and CFP format procedure sit in the vote-count and feasibility states; cfb.playoff_format is only a format table (KEEP_CONTEXT) and is not credited as the governance layer, since expansion is a governing-body vote.

settlement_contract.note: Qualifying announcement definitions and window end dates read from the sampled rules text.

cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.label: Head-coach exit hazard features
cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.mechanism: Covariates of the weekly probability that a head coach is fired, resigns or announces departure: record versus expectation, contract and buyout, losing streaks, rivalry results, age and administration stability.
cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.rationale: Both COACHLEAVE and COACHOUT resolve on leaving or announcing departure within a window, and the hazard is concentrated at the end of the regular season and after bowls; the cost of firing (buyout) restrains exits, while a deep disappointment relative to expectation, athletic director turnover or an attractive outside job raises them.
cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.measurement: Cox proportional hazard by week with features: wins minus preseason expected wins from non-market ratings (to date), consecutive losses, losses to rivals, remaining contractually-secured buyout in dollars relative to athletic department revenue, tenure and age (retirement), athletic director tenure (first-year AD indicator), outside-job interest flag; fit on FBS head-coach changes 2005-2025 (about 15-25 per year); output cumulative probability for each specific window end (Dec 1, Feb 1) given as-of date. Competing risks: fit cause-specific hazards for (a) fired, (b) resigns or retires (age, health, announced future departure counts under COACHLEAVE/COACHOUT), (c) leaves for another program or the NFL (poached; outside-job interest flag, assistant-coach and peer-vacancy market) while an interim appointment is non-qualifying for NEXTCOACH. Prior-only fallback: until the covariate model validates on held-out years (it cannot be validated with 15-25 changes a year and a dozen features), the default forecast is the calendar-window base rate from cfb.offfield_base_rate adjusted only by wins minus expectation; covariates enter only if they improve out-of-sample log loss.
cfb.coach_exit_hazard_features.why: Supplies the hazard process behind two series where the window end date is the main difference.

cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.label: Buyout exposure and contract state
cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.mechanism: Remaining contractually-secured pay and buyout owed by the school, expressed relative to athletic department finances, as a function of date.
cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.rationale: The firing decision is partly financial: a school owing 30 to 80 million dollars is far less likely to fire before a contractual step-down; buyouts often fall after December 31 or at the start of a contract year, so timing within the window matters.
cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.measurement: For each head coach: buyout amount B(t) as a function of date from contract terms (stepdowns on dates such as Jan 1 or Jun 30), mitigated by offset clauses; ratio = B(t) / (annual athletic revenue + booster fund proxy); record the ratio at the as-of date and at the window end. Missing contracts imputed with the 3-year median for the conference tier.
cfb.coach_buyout_exposure.why: Separates ability to pay from desire to fire; a key friction missing from base rates.

cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.label: Next-head-coach candidate and timing model
cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.mechanism: Probability that each named person becomes the next permanent head coach, and the timing of the announcement, conditional on a vacancy.
cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.rationale: KXNCAAFNEXTCOACH settles on the next permanent head coach officially announced by a date; interim coaches do not count, and the school's tier, athletic director history, available coordinators and head coaches, and leaks determine the distribution. A candidate who is also a candidate elsewhere reduces probability.
cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.measurement: Multinomial logit over the candidate pool with features: current job tier, win rate, school-coach history (alumnus, prior staff), AD's hiring pattern (coordinator vs head coach, G5 head coach), reported interest and visits from timestamped credible reporting (weight by source reliability from past hits), buyout of the candidate's current school; hiring time hazard: P(announce by Sep 1, 2027) from historical time from vacancy to announcement (median weeks). Updated daily.
free_sources: Beat reporters and coaching carousel trackers (own capture)
cfb.next_coach_candidate_model.why: Outcome is a categorical hire among named people with leakage through reporting; needs a candidate-level model.

cfb.governance_vote_count_state.label: Governance vote count and stakeholder positions
cfb.governance_vote_count_state.mechanism: Count of declared positions of the decision makers (commissioners, presidents, media partners) against the approval threshold, dated.
cfb.governance_vote_count_state.rationale: CFP expansion to exactly 24 teams (KXNCAAFCFPEXPAND) requires binding approval by the CFP management committee, a body with explicit voting requirements and divided stakeholder positions; the probability of passage depends on how many needed votes are publicly aligned and whether the decision calendar allows approval before the deadline.
cfb.governance_vote_count_state.measurement: Table of stakeholders with stated position (support, oppose, neutral, undecided) coded from dated public statements, weight by vote power in the governing documents; compute votes in favour needed vs declared; P(approval by deadline) = logistic over (declared share - threshold) and (days left x meeting calendar density); update on each meeting and report; as-of date. Coded manually with source and timestamp.
cfb.governance_vote_count_state.why: Creates a structured state variable out of otherwise qualitative news for governance contracts.

cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.label: Transfer destination candidate model
cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.mechanism: Probability over destinations for a named player: stays, declares for the draft, or commits to a specific school, from portal status and reported interest.
cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.rationale: KXNCAAFTRANSFER offers multi-outcome markets (stays, declares for the draft, commits elsewhere); resolution depends on the portal window, whether the player enters, and which programs have need and compensation capacity; staying resolves YES if the player withdraws from the portal.
cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.measurement: State machine: P(enters portal) from player class, role, coach change, depth chart competitor and reported interest; conditional destination multinomial with features (position need, revenue-sharing capacity estimate, coach relationship, region, visits) from timestamped credible reports; window dates from NCAA rules; as-of date. Missing compensation data imputed from conference tier.
cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model.why: The existing team-level transfer input is too aggregate for a named-player market.

cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.label: Realignment feasibility state (grant of rights, exit terms, membership process)
cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.mechanism: Contractual and procedural constraints on a conference move: grant-of-rights, exit fees, notice periods, membership votes, litigation status.
cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.rationale: Conference leave or join markets (LSU leaving the SEC, Washington State joining the Big 12) resolve on public announcement, binding agreement, formal notice or exit settlement within a window; the feasibility of the move and the steps needed to complete it are much more informative than historical frequencies of realignment.
cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.measurement: Table by team and conference: grant-of-rights end date, exit fee schedule, notice requirement, membership approval threshold and who votes, litigation status; compute minimal feasible announcement date under current constraints; combine with reported talks (credible reporting count weighted by reliability) in a logistic hazard for announcement in the window; as-of date. Missing terms flagged unknown.
cfb.realignment_feasibility_state.why: Converts qualitative realignment talk into feasibility and timing constraints.

cfb.offfield_base_rate.reason: Reference-class base rates by calendar window are the right prior for every series here, but the label lumps coaching, conference and facility events; it needs separate classes (head-coach exits by week, hires after a vacancy, realignment announcements per year, CFP format changes) with calendar-aware hazards.

cfb.coaching.reason: Coach tenure and record are relevant to exits, but the label also covers scheme and tempo, which are irrelevant to personnel decisions; replace with hazard features such as record versus expectation, contract and buyout.

cfb.standings.reason: Season outcome matters for coach exits only relative to preseason expectation, which this input does not define; the surprise component is the missing structure.

cfb.motivation.reason: Rivalry losses and bowl eligibility are plausible triggers of firings, but the claim that rivalry losses raise exit risk beyond record is a hypothesis with no measure here.

cfb.transfer_roster.reason: Team-level roster churn is too aggregate for a named-player destination market (KXNCAAFTRANSFER); useful only as context about portal activity, with the player-level decision model missing.

cfb.opt_out_departures.reason: Bowl opt-outs and redshirt decisions concern playing time, not a player's destination or a coaching or governance decision; little predictive value for these series.

cfb.suspension_eligibility.reason: Suspensions and targeting ejections do not drive coach exits, conference moves or CFP governance; at best they matter for a transfer's eligibility, which is a tiny fraction of the archetype.

cfb.roster_continuity.reason: Returning production signals retention pressure in the abstract but has no demonstrated link to coach exits or transfers of a specific star; the hypothesis is untested here.

cfb.playoff_format.reason: Current format rules define what a 24-team expansion would change, but the expansion decision is a governance vote driven by commissioners, presidents and media partners rather than by the present format.

interactions.mechanism: A poor season raises the firing hazard but a large buyout multiplies it down, so the hazard is the product of performance shortfall and affordability; a coach with a 10 win shortfall and a 40 million dollar buyout is about as likely to survive as one with a smaller shortfall and no buyout.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the hazard with an interaction of shortfall and buyout ratio; test in a historical sample of coaches with deep shortfalls.

interactions.mechanism: The hazard changes regime at the end of the regular season: before rivalry week exits are rare, after the final regular-season game and after bowls they cluster, so the cumulative probability to Dec 1 is dominated by the last two weeks while to Feb 1 it includes the post-bowl wave.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate weekly hazard from the historical timing of FBS firings and test whether a regime break occurs around rivalry week.

interactions.mechanism: CFP approval jumps when declared support crosses the voting threshold and the calendar allows a meeting; until then the probability is low regardless of rhetoric, so the key variable is votes relative to the threshold, not general support.
interactions.how_to_test: Code stakeholder positions in past governance decisions and estimate approval probability against votes minus threshold.

interactions.mechanism: A candidate's hire probability depends on his own school's buyout and whether his current team is still playing, since coaches in the playoff or bowl cannot be hired until the season ends; the timing hazard and the candidate identity are interdependent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare hire timing and identity for candidates at schools still playing versus eliminated, from past carousels.

interactions.mechanism: A conference move has zero probability before the grant-of-rights, notice and membership-vote constraints allow it and a small positive hazard afterwards, so the response to reported talks is piecewise in the date and in the constraint state; the same rumor means very different things before and after the feasibility date.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate historical realignments by whether constraints had lapsed at announcement; estimate hazards before and after the feasibility date.

nonlinearities.shape: Hazard convex in season shortfall and strongly time-clustered at the end of the regular season
nonlinearities.why: Mild underperformance rarely leads to a firing but large shortfalls with a poor finish carry steeply higher hazard, concentrated in a handful of days, so linear time-in-window accumulation is wrong.

nonlinearities.shape: Step at the approval threshold with a long flat region below it
nonlinearities.why: Governance outcomes do not move continuously with support: at 60 percent of required votes the probability is near zero and at 100 percent near one once a meeting occurs.

nonlinearities.shape: Winner-take-all softmax over candidates with rapid sharpening as credible reports accumulate
nonlinearities.why: Candidate probabilities start diffuse and collapse toward one name after a credible report, a non-linear update that a linear aggregation of rumors would miss.

contract.settlement_definition: Poll contracts settle on a specific labelled ranking release: KXNCAAFTOPAPRANK on whether the team is ranked in the AP top 25 at a given week (for example Week 5), KXNCAAFAPRANK on the exact rank in the AP Final Rankings (expected Jan 26, 2027), KXNCAAFAPANY on being ranked number one in any eligible AP poll of the season starting with the Preseason poll, KXNCAAFAPCHURN on at least N distinct teams ranked number one in any poll including Preseason and Final, and KXNCAAFCFPPOLL and TOPCFPPOLL on exact or top-N rank in the CFP rankings of a labelled date (for example Nov 24), falling to the next published CFP rankings after that date if none is labelled then. Resolution is determined solely by the official AP website or the CFP rankings.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution is determined solely by the AP Top 25 College Football Polls on the official Associated Press website.
rules_evidence.establishes: The AP website is the only source of truth; other displays with different week labels do not count.

rules_evidence.quote: If the same team holds rank #1 in multiple polls throughout the season, it is counted only once.
rules_evidence.establishes: The churn contract counts distinct teams across all polls including Preseason and Final, so a single team repeating does not add to the count.

rules_evidence.quote: If no rankings are published that are labeled for Nov 24 in the 2026-27 college football season, then the market resolves based on the next published College Football Playoff rankings after Nov 24.
rules_evidence.establishes: A missing release for the named date falls back to the next published CFP rankings, so a date shift moves the evaluated ranking.

rules_evidence.quote: Resolution is determined solely by the AP Top 25 Poll Week 5 Rankings for the 2026-27 season on the official Associated Press website.
rules_evidence.establishes: The week label is the AP's official designation, and Week 5 is not a calendar week but the fifth numbered poll.

rules_evidence.quote: If West Virginia is ranked #1 on the College Football AP Poll Final Rankings (expected to be released on Jan 26, 2027)
rules_evidence.establishes: The final AP poll is released after the national championship game, so bowl and CFP results are part of the information set.

variants_and_edge_cases: Two bodies with different processes share the archetype: the AP poll of about 60 voters each week and the 13-member CFP committee, which begins weekly rankings late in the season, so the number of releases before a date differs.
The KXNCAAFCFPPOLL sampled rules text contains an unfilled template token (|| Time Period ||) in place of the season, a text defect that suggests template variables may not always be filled in.
KXNCAAFAPCHURN counts all polls including Preseason and Final; APANY covers any poll starting with the Preseason poll; both depend on the number of polls and on AP's label conventions.
Exactly #25 on a CFP release is a boundary event; the top 4 market depends on the committee's top four, and seeding rules do not change the ranking list.
Statuses vary: TOPAPRANK sample is finalized, CFPPOLL inactive; markets can be closed or settled before the contract is read, so state matters.

KXNCAAFAPRANK resolves on the AP Final Rankings expected Jan 26, 2027, after the CFP championship game, so bowl and CFP results are part of the information set and the final #1 is tied to the national champion.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official AP Top 25 poll as published on the Associated Press website and official CFP rankings; Kalshi text names these sources explicitly.

mechanism.summary: A rank is the output of a voting body reacting to results and perception, not of team strength directly. AP voters begin from last week's ballot and move teams by asymmetric amounts: a loss by a highly ranked team costs more than the same loss by a lower-ranked team, an upset win by an unranked team earns entry only if it clears the boundary, and the preseason ballot is built from last season and returning production. The CFP committee builds a resume ranking with explicit factors (strength of record, wins over ranked teams, conference title, head-to-head and injuries) but also moves slowly. Distinct number-one counts are governed by upsets of the few top teams and the succession rule, while boundary contracts (top 25, exactly #25) depend on the density of similar teams near the cut line.

stages.name: Results of the games that move the ballots
stages.description: Rank changes follow the outcomes of weekend games, so the first stage is the win probability of each ranked or near-ranked team in each game, with margin and venue; unlikely wins by lower-rated teams create the large changes, and top teams' head-to-head games guarantee a swap.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli outcomes with game win probabilities between 50 and 99 percent for top teams; correlated through shared rating uncertainty.

stages.name: Voter response: inertia and asymmetric movement
stages.description: Given results, voters adjust the previous ballot: top teams that win usually stay, losses drop a team by an amount that depends on its rank, the opponent's rank and the timing in the season, and unranked teams enter only after wins over ranked or similar teams. Preseason polls reflect hype and returning production, and the final poll reflects bowl and playoff results.
stages.distribution: Ordered-response with strong persistence; asymmetric (drop larger than rise) and convex in rank.

stages.name: Succession at number one and ballot state
stages.description: When the number one loses, the successor depends on how first-place votes and points are distributed among the next teams; the count of distinct number-ones is a counting process over losses by the leader and successors, and head-to-head games and the preseason order set the starting state.
stages.distribution: Markov chain over a small set of contenders; counting process with rare events (3-8 per season).

stages.name: Committee resume ranking
stages.description: The CFP committee ranks teams from resume and results, with explicit weights on strength of record, quality wins, losses, conference championship and head-to-head; rankings start in early November and change weekly with strong inertia. Exact rank markets need the whole ordering around the target position, particularly where teams have similar resumes.
stages.distribution: Ordinal with inertia and local reshuffling; uncertainty greatest in the middle and at rank 25.

stages.name: Boundary density and release mapping
stages.description: Entry into the top 25 and exact-rank contracts are decided near the cut line where vote points differ by small amounts; the evaluated release is determined by a calendar and a label map, with a fallback to the next published release if none carries the date.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like vote-point noise around a threshold; deterministic label mapping.

stages.name: Postseason results and the Final AP #1
stages.description: The Final AP poll is released after the CFP championship game, so KXNCAAFAPRANK on the Final #1 is driven by bowl and CFP results: who wins the national title, with a small tail where voters rank another team first; the same bracket results feed the late-season number-one handovers that APANY and APCHURN count.
stages.distribution: Single-elimination bracket survival then a near-deterministic link from champion to AP #1 with a small split-ballot tail.

cfb.poll_transition_model.label: AP poll transition model (rank next week given rank, result and opponent)
cfb.poll_transition_model.mechanism: Fitted mapping from the previous AP rank, the weekend result and the opponent to the next AP rank or vote share.
cfb.poll_transition_model.rationale: AP voters start from last week's ballot and move teams for results: a loss by a highly ranked team drops it several places, a win moves it up only if teams above it lose, and unranked teams enter only after notable wins; the preseason poll is built from last year and returning production. Rank is persistent with asymmetric shocks.
cfb.poll_transition_model.measurement: Using AP polls since 1990 (rank, points, first-place votes, week) and game results: for each team-week fit an ordered response model of next rank on previous rank, result (win/loss), margin, opponent's AP rank at the time, home/away, and week of season, with team-level random effects for conference bias; evaluate by rank error. Output distribution over next rank for each team given the simulated weekend. As-of Sunday release.
free_sources: CFBD rankings and games endpoints (free key)
raw_data: weekly AP rank, points, first-place votes
cfb.poll_transition_model.why: Models the voter response layer that turns results into ranks for every AP contract in this archetype.

cfb.ballot_points_gap.label: Ballot points and first-place vote state
cfb.ballot_points_gap.mechanism: Points and first-place votes of the top teams as published, giving the margin by which the leader leads the next team.
cfb.ballot_points_gap.rationale: If the number-one team loses, the successor is the team with the next-most points unless voters coalesce around a winner; a large first-place vote share for the number two team means a quick handover, and a small gap leads to a split and possibly a different team ascending, which controls the count of distinct number-one teams.
cfb.ballot_points_gap.measurement: From each weekly AP release record points and first-place votes for ranks 1 to 5; compute share = points_i / (62 x 25 +... ) using ballot count n of that week; gap = (points_1 - points_2) / total points possible; successor probability = softmax over ranks 2-5 with temperature fitted on historical handovers (n about 50 events). As-of the latest published poll.
free_sources: CFBD rankings endpoint (free key; points and first-place votes field availability SOURCE_UNVERIFIED)
raw_data: weekly AP points and first-place votes
cfb.ballot_points_gap.why: Needed for successor-given-loss in churn and any-week-number-one contracts.

cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.label: Top-team loss hazard and number-one succession simulation
cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.mechanism: Probability that the current number one (and the next few teams) lose in each remaining week, combined into a succession process.
cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.rationale: Distinct-number-one and any-week-number-one markets are driven by upsets of the few top teams: each week the number one has a 5-20 percent chance to lose depending on opponent and venue, and the count of distinct number-ones grows by one per succession; head-to-head games between top teams guarantee a loser.
cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.measurement: For each top-8 team compute weekly P(loss) from non-market ratings and game site; simulate the AP number-one chain: leader loses -> successor by ballot_points_gap softmax; leader wins -> stays unless voters swap (historical swap rate to be estimated); produce P(distinct number-ones >= k) and P(team i ever #1). Correlation via shared rating draws and head-to-head constraints. As-of latest week, including preseason poll.
cfb.top_team_loss_hazard.why: Structural model for the two number-one contracts (APANY and APCHURN) where history is too thin for frequencies alone.

cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.label: CFP committee ranking features and protocol
cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.mechanism: Resume features the committee emphasises: strength of record, strength of schedule, wins over ranked teams, conference championship, head-to-head, common opponents and key injuries.
cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.rationale: CFP exact-rank contracts (top 4, exactly #25 on a given Tuesday) depend on a committee that claims to rank afresh each week but moves slowly, weights wins over ranked teams and conference championships, and considers injuries; a rating-only model misses protocol-specific weights.
cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.measurement: Fit a rank model on the 2014 to latest committee releases: rank_t ~ rank_(t-1), ESPN SOR or own resume metric, number of wins over top-25 and top-50 teams, losses (count, margin, quality), conference champion flag (post-title game), head-to-head vs adjacent teams, injury flag for starting quarterback; output the rank distribution at the release date (Nov 24). Calibrate by pairwise ordering accuracy for adjacent ranks.
free_sources: CFBD rankings endpoint (Playoff Committee Rankings; free key)
cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features.why: Provides the committee-specific mapping that differs from AP voting and from ratings.

cfb.bubble_proximity_state.label: Top-25 bubble proximity (others receiving votes and ranks 20-30)
cfb.bubble_proximity_state.mechanism: Points of unranked teams receiving votes and the gap among teams ranked 20 to 30, for entry and exact-rank markets near the cut line.
cfb.bubble_proximity_state.rationale: Contracts such as top 25 in AP Week 5 or exactly #25 in the CFP rankings sit on the boundary where many teams have similar resumes and tiny vote differences decide placement; probabilities depend on the density of teams around the cut line rather than on the strength of the team in question alone.
cfb.bubble_proximity_state.measurement: At each release collect points for ranks 15-25 and the unranked others receiving votes list (typically 10-20 teams with points); for each team compute z = (team points - points at rank 25) / SD of week-to-week points change (fitted); P(ranked next week) = Phi(z + expected effect of the coming game from the transition model). For CFP exact-rank: density of resume-metric gaps around ranks 22-28. As-of latest release.
raw_data: weekly AP points for ranks 1-25 and others
cfb.bubble_proximity_state.why: Handles boundary markets where individual strength is not the main driver.

cfb.poll_release_calendar.label: Poll release calendar and week-label map
cfb.poll_release_calendar.mechanism: Dates, labels and numbering of AP and CFP releases, including preseason, weekly and final polls.
cfb.poll_release_calendar.rationale: Contracts refer to labelled releases (AP Week 5, Final Rankings expected Jan 26, 2027, CFP rankings of Nov 24, next published after if none is labeled that date); mismatched label dates or an AP week renumbering can resolve a market differently than a naive date match.
cfb.poll_release_calendar.measurement: Table by season: release timestamp, official AP label (Preseason, Week 1..., Final), CFP release Tuesday dates and committee start date; mapping function from contract strings (for example Nov 24, Week 5, Final) to the release that settles it, with the fallback rule next published release after the date; update on announcements; verify against past years. Include the season-by-season AP label table (Preseason, Week 1 ... Week N, Final) because AP Week numbering is AP own label and Preseason is unnumbered, so Week 5 is the fifth numbered release after the Preseason poll; CFP releases are on Tuesdays (Nov 24, 2026 is a Tuesday) with the fallback to the next published release when no release carries the labelled date.
raw_data: release dates and labels by season
cfb.poll_release_calendar.why: A settlement-mapping input that determines which ranking is evaluated.

cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.label: National-title path probability and AP final-ranking link
cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.mechanism: KXNCAAFAPRANK (Final AP #1, released after the title game) and the late-season paths of KXNCAAFAPANY and KXNCAAFAPCHURN depend on bowl and CFP results through the national championship; the input is a bracket simulation from non-market ratings plus the historical link between the CFP champion and the AP final #1.
cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.rationale: The Final AP poll is released after the championship game (rules text: Final Rankings expected Jan 26, 2027), so the leading candidate for #1 is the CFP champion; AP voters have ranked the champion first in the CFP era (2014-2024, to be verified), which turns the Final-#1 market into a title-probability market with a small split-vote tail, and the number of distinct #1 teams depends on regular-season losses of the top-ranked team before the bracket.
cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.measurement: Simulate the bracket 20,000 times from cfb.sp_plus-type non-market ratings with posterior SD (as in the season_futures simulation): seeding from a projected committee ranking (cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features), bracket paths under the 2026 format, neutral-site games without home edge; output P(national champion) per team. Then P(AP final #1 = team) = P(champion) x P(AP #1 | champion; empirical rate from CFP-era seasons with Beta(9, 1) prior) + P(non-champion #1 | split cases, small mass from the same history). As-of the latest week; update after each bracket round.
raw_data: historical AP final rank vs CFP champion
cfb.title_path_to_final_ap.why: KXNCAAFAPRANK (Final AP #1) and late-season KXNCAAFAPANY/APCHURN paths cannot be priced without a title-probability input; the machinery otherwise lives only in season_futures.

cfb.poll_voter_behavior.reason: Umbrella label for two different electorates; superseded for the AP by cfb.poll_transition_model and for the CFP committee by cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features, which carry the measurable definitions, so it is kept only as context and not as a separate primary input.

cfb.sp_plus.reason: Ratings predict game results that later move ranks, but rank is a function of results and perception, not of the rating; used for game win probabilities in the simulation, with the poll response as a separate layer.

cfb.standings.reason: Conference standing matters for CFP committee ranking (champions) and for who plays whom; for AP weekly rank it is mostly a proxy for team wins already captured in results.

cfb.schedule_strength.reason: Past and remaining strength of schedule feeds the committee's resume; AP voters respond more to the quality of the win just played, so scalar strength of schedule is a coarse stand-in for opponent rank at game time.

cfb.off_ppa.reason: Offensive efficiency enters rank only through the game win probabilities of future games, which a composite rating already provides; keeping it separately duplicates the same pathway.

cfb.def_ppa.reason: Defensive efficiency enters rank only through game win probabilities, duplicating the composite rating; adding it would double-count team strength in the simulation.

cfb.cross_conf_calibration.reason: Voters rate wins in some conferences above others and the committee compares across conferences with sparse connectivity; the calibration affects how a given win moves a team and is a voter-bias term as well as a strength term.

cfb.motivation.reason: Rivalry and bowl stakes change upset risk in specific games, a small second-order effect on win probability; no demonstrated link to the poll response itself.

cfb.qb_status_pit.reason: A quarterback injury affects win probability in top games and voter expectations (voters rank injured teams lower, and the committee explicitly considers injuries); knowable timing matters for the weekly ballot.

cfb.playoff_format.reason: CFP rankings always list 25 teams, so the format matters mostly for how much the committee cares about the top four or twelve positions and for conference-champion treatment; weak for the AP-based series.

interactions.mechanism: The rank penalty of a loss is larger for a higher-ranked team and smaller when the loss came against a highly ranked opponent or a hard schedule, so the drop is the product of rank, opponent rank and timing; the same loss moves a number-three team five places and a number-fifteen team only two.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate drop size by previous rank, opponent rank and week; check multiplicative structure against additive in a held-out set of seasons. Test it as terms on rank, opponent rank and week in a model, not on the transition model own coefficients.

interactions.mechanism: When the leader loses, the successor probability depends on first-place vote distribution and on whether the number two team also won; a split ballot raises the chance that a third team becomes number one, which adds to the distinct count.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate handovers by first-place-vote gap and by number two's result in past seasons.

interactions.mechanism: Committee rankings before conference championships treat unbeaten and one-loss teams one way, and after champions are decided the champion status resets the order; so the same resume yields different ranks before and after the title games, and the Nov 24 release comes before the championships.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit rank models separately before and after championship week; compare weights on the champion indicator.

interactions.mechanism: Entry to the AP top 25 saturates quickly in vote points: once a team has votes comparable to rank 25 a single win moves it in, but far below the line even a big upset win leaves it out; the effect of a win is concentrated in teams near the line and depends on conference credit.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate P(enter) by distance from the line in points and by conference, for teams that won as underdogs.

interactions.mechanism: Head-to-head games between top teams make losses perfectly negatively correlated and guarantee that at least one of the top teams loses, so the count of distinct number-ones is not a sum of independent losses; the schedule structure of the top eight teams matters.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate churn with and without head-to-head constraints and compare to observed distinct counts.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in previous rank for loss penalties and asymmetric: losses cost more than wins gain
nonlinearities.why: A loss by the top team can drop it several places while an equivalent win moves it up only if teams above lose, making rank changes skewed and dependent on the starting rank.

nonlinearities.shape: Bounded per-week hazard (about 5-20 percent) compounding over 13 weeks into a high-probability of at least one change
nonlinearities.why: Weekly upsets of the number one are rare but accumulate, so the distinct count distribution is Poisson-like with mean around 3 to 5 across the season, not a linear function of rating.

nonlinearities.shape: Probit-like in the vote-point gap to rank 25
nonlinearities.why: Probability of being ranked changes quickly only within a narrow band around the cut line; far from the line the probability is nearly 0 or 1.

contract.settlement_definition: Eight team or game count series, each read from its own rules: KXNCAAFTEAMYDS (total offense = rushing plus receiving yards, sacks and quarterback kneels negative rushing yards, overtime periods one and two count, 2-point conversions excluded), TEAMINT, TEAMSACK and TEAMTO (defensive interceptions, sacks and turnovers gained by the named team, overtime periods one and two count, statistics during 2-point attempts excluded; a turnover on downs is not a turnover), TEAMFG and TOTALFG (made field goals by one team or both, overtime counts), KXNCAAF2PT (at least one successful 2-point conversion in regulation; overtime conversions do not count), and KXNCAAFDELAY (any official weather delay, including a delayed start or a stoppage after kickoff). Postponement under 48 hours stays open, longer resolves to a fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: Any 2-point conversions recorded in overtime do not count towards this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: The two-point series is regulation only, unlike the yardage, sack and field-goal series that count overtime.

rules_evidence.quote: A team's total yards of offense equals its total rushing yards plus total receiving yards. Sacks and quarterback kneels count as negative rushing yards for the team on offense.
rules_evidence.establishes: Total yards are net of sack and kneel yardage, which lowers the mean relative to gross yardage.

rules_evidence.quote: A turnover on downs is not considered a team turnover.
rules_evidence.establishes: Forced turnovers are interceptions and fumble recoveries only, excluding turnovers on downs and possession changes after scores.

rules_evidence.quote: Statistics recorded during a 2-point conversion attempt do not count, including those in overtime.
rules_evidence.establishes: A sack on a 2-point try is not counted, so only regular snaps contribute to the team sack total.

rules_evidence.quote: This includes a delayed start time as well as any suspension or stoppage of play after the event has begun due to weather.
rules_evidence.establishes: Any official weather delay qualifies with no minimum duration, so a short lightning hold resolves YES.

rules_evidence.quote: Any made field goals recorded in overtime count toward a team's total.
rules_evidence.establishes: Field-goal counts include overtime, so overtime possessions add to the count.

variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime scope differs by series: yards, sacks, interceptions and turnovers count only overtime periods one and two, field-goal series count overtime without that limit (only periods one and two can produce field goals anyway), and the two-point series is regulation only.

TEAMYDS is net total offense (rushing plus receiving yards with sacks and kneels as negative rushing yards), so a team that kneels in victory formation loses yards and heavy sack games lower the total.

TEAMTO counts turnovers gained (interceptions and fumble recoveries) and excludes turnovers on downs and possession changes after scores; the sampled secondary text is truncated, so fumbles lost on punts and kickoffs may be included or not and this is unconfirmed.

DELAY resolves YES for any official weather delay, including a delayed start, with no minimum duration and no source named in the sample for what counts as official; delays caused solely by other reasons resolve No.
Team-level counts (TEAMSACK, TEAMINT, TEAMTO, TEAMFG) are for the named team while TOTALFG and 2PT are for both teams; each series ladders thresholds as half-point strikes (3.5, 1.5, 2.5).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official game statistics (the number recorded by the team in the game) and, for DELAY, an official delay; the sampled text names no stats provider and no source for the delay declaration.

mechanism.summary: Each series is a count of a discrete event over a team's or the game's opportunities: sacks and interceptions are rates times the opponent's dropbacks, with the rate set by the pass rush against the quarterback's sack and interception propensity; forced turnovers add fumble recoveries, which are roughly even odds and regress; field goals are attempts (drives that stall inside range and the coach's decision to kick) times make probability by distance and conditions; two-point conversions are touchdowns times a decision rate times success; total yards are plays times net yards per play. Weather delay is a different kind of event: a thunderstorm and lightning hazard at the venue during the game window. Counts are small and overdispersed, and settlement definitions are unknown.

stages.name: Opportunity counts for the event
stages.description: Each count has its own opportunity base: the opponent's dropbacks for sacks and interceptions, the team's drives that reach field-goal range for kicks, the touchdowns scored for two-point tries, and plays for yards. The base depends on tempo, run-pass mix and expected score state, and varies by 10 to 20 percent between games, giving the first source of variance.
stages.distribution: Counts with negative-binomial variation around a state-dependent mean; opportunity counts differ across series.

stages.name: Event rate per opportunity
stages.description: The rate per opportunity depends on matchup: the opposing pass rush against the protection and the quarterback's sack proneness, the quarterback's interception propensity against ball skills, the kicker's range and conditions for field goals, the offence and defence for two-point success and yards per play. Fumble recoveries are close to a coin flip and so forced-turnover rate regresses strongly.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per opportunity with small probabilities (a few percent for sacks and interceptions); heavily regressed for lucky components.

stages.name: Decisions that create or remove opportunities
stages.description: Field-goal counts depend on the coach's choice to kick, go for it or punt on fourth down; two-point counts depend on the score chart and coach tendency; yards depend on play-calling balance. These choices are not random draws from an ability rate but strategy, and they change count distributions even at equal ability.
stages.distribution: Discrete decisions with coach-specific policy; conditional on score, time and field position.

stages.name: Environment and rare weather events
stages.description: Wind, temperature and rain change field-goal accuracy, passing and sacks; thunderstorms and lightning within the venue protocol radius cause delays, a binary event driven by convective weather, time of day and stadium type, where the series counts any official stoppage or delayed start for weather with no minimum duration.
stages.distribution: Continuous weather effects on rates; rare binary delay event with seasonal and diurnal pattern.

stages.name: Count distribution and settlement ambiguity
stages.description: The distribution of a small count is overdispersed and lumpy, and the rules set series-specific definitions that must be applied exactly: net yardage with sacks and kneels negative, turnovers gained without turnovers on downs, overtime scope that differs by series, regulation-only two-point conversions and any weather delay for the delay series.
stages.distribution: Negative binomial or Poisson-gamma counts with series-specific definitions; definition errors shift rung probabilities by amounts comparable to model edges.
