cfb.opp_dropback_volume.label: Opposing dropback volume under expected script
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.mechanism: Expected number of pass dropbacks by the opponent (the opportunity count for sacks and interceptions) given its pass rate and the expected game state.
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.rationale: Sack and interception counts are rates times the opponent's dropbacks, and the opponent's dropbacks swing by 10 to 15 depending on whether it trails or leads; using season averages misprices games with large expected margins. Note: this measures the same quantity as cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts plus cfb.state_dependent_pace in the game_stat_props record (dropbacks under the expected script) and should be aliased to one catalog input.
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.measurement: Opponent neutral-situation pass rate (first and second down, score within 7, first three quarters) over last 10 games with 0.8 decay, expected plays from state-dependent tempo, and expected score state from non-market ratings (leading by 14+ lowers pass rate by about 10 points; trailing raises it by a similar amount); output expected dropbacks and negative-binomial dispersion. As-of last completed game.
raw_data: plays with down, distance, score, play type, offense
cfb.opp_dropback_volume.why: Sets the number of opportunities for the defensive count series (sacks, interceptions, forced turnovers).

cfb.qb_sack_proneness.label: Quarterback sack proneness independent of line
cfb.qb_sack_proneness.mechanism: Quarterback-specific tendency to take sacks: time to throw, scrambling, holding the ball and sack share of pressures.
cfb.qb_sack_proneness.rationale: Two offences with identical pressure rates can differ in sack rate depending on the quarterback; a mobile quarterback with quick release avoids sacks, a slow decision-maker takes them; for a team sack total the opposing quarterback's contribution is as large as the pass rush.
cfb.qb_sack_proneness.measurement: Per starting QB: sacks per dropback over the last 2 seasons with 0.6 decay, adjusted for opposing pass-rush strength and for pass-block efficiency of his line; decompose into pressure rate x sack-given-pressure; shrinkage k = 150 dropbacks to conference mean; backup quarterback replaced with a recruiting-class prior. As-of pregame QB status vintage.
free_sources: PFF College pressure and time to throw (paid)
cfb.qb_sack_proneness.why: Separates the quarterback component from the opposing rush in the team sack total.

cfb.qb_interception_propensity.label: Quarterback interception propensity (turnover-worthy plays)
cfb.qb_interception_propensity.mechanism: Expected interceptions per attempt from turnover-worthy throws and depth of target, regressed away from realised interception rate.
cfb.qb_interception_propensity.rationale: Interception rates are noisy: a quarterback with a high realised rate over 150 attempts regresses by about half; turnover-worthy plays and depth of target are more predictive of next-game interceptions than past interceptions, and the defence's ball-hawking skill adds only a small increment.
cfb.qb_interception_propensity.measurement: Per QB: expected INT rate = 0.5 x realised INT per attempt (2 seasons, 0.6 decay) + 0.5 x charting-based turnover-worthy rate x conversion factor; if charting unavailable use depth-of-target and completion rate proxy with shrinkage k = 200 attempts; opposing defence adjustment by its INT rate over expected (k = 300 opponent attempts). Multiply by opponent dropbacks (cfb.opp_dropback_volume).
cfb.qb_interception_propensity.why: Gives a regressed intensity for the interception and turnover series instead of extrapolating noisy interception counts.

cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.label: Field-goal attempt and make model by distance
cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.mechanism: Expected number of field-goal attempts per team from drives reaching the 35, decisions to kick, go for it or punt, and probability of making each by distance and weather.
cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.rationale: Field-goal counts are attempts times make probability: attempts depend on how many drives stall within range and the coach's 4th-down policy; the make rate depends on distance and conditions; both teams contribute for the total series.
cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.measurement: Per team: drives crossing the opponent 35 without scoring a touchdown (count per game, last 10 games with 0.85 decay) x P(kick | 4th down inside 35, distance, score, time) from the coach's historical rates; make probability = logistic(kicker career accuracy by distance bucket with shrinkage k = 20 kicks, wind and temperature adjustment); expected FG made = sum over attempts; add overtime possessions if the contract counts them. As-of pregame kicker and weather vintages.
cfb.fg_attempt_make_model.why: Directly produces the mean and dispersion for TEAMFG and TOTALFG.

cfb.two_point_attempt_model.label: Two-point attempt decision and success model
cfb.two_point_attempt_model.mechanism: Number of touchdowns times the probability of going for two (by score chart and coach) times success rate from the 3-yard line.
cfb.two_point_attempt_model.rationale: Two-point conversions are a small count: 0 to 3 per game, and under KXNCAAF2PT only successful conversions in regulation count. Attempts follow the touchdown count, the score differential (chart situations such as down 8 or up 17 invite a try) and the coach's tendency; success rate is near one half but depends on the offence and defence.
cfb.two_point_attempt_model.measurement: Per coach: P(go for 2 | TD, score diff, period) from a logistic fit on 2014-2025 plays, with shrinkage k = 20 touchdowns to the conference mean; success rate by team offence and opposing defence, beta prior at league mean (to be estimated) with strength 25; expected successful regulation conversions = expected touchdowns x decision probability x success rate (overtime excluded by the contract); output P(at least one successful) and the count pmf. As-of pregame.
raw_data: touchdowns and extra-point/2-point attempts with score state
cfb.two_point_attempt_model.why: Provides P(at least one successful conversion in regulation), the strike of KXNCAAF2PT, from a small-count model.

cfb.weather_delay_hazard.label: Weather delay hazard from thunderstorm and lightning forecast
cfb.weather_delay_hazard.mechanism: Probability of a stoppage from lightning or severe weather during a window around kickoff given forecast thunderstorm probability, lightning proximity and venue protocol.
cfb.weather_delay_hazard.rationale: A weather delay is a binary event driven by lightning within a protocol radius (about 8 miles under common policy) and the 30-minute clock that restarts with each strike; early-season Southern and Midwestern afternoon games are most exposed, and domes and closed stadiums remove the risk.
cfb.weather_delay_hazard.measurement: P(delay) = logistic of forecast probability of thunderstorms in the 4-hour window, convective available potential energy index, local time (afternoon peak), month, roof status, and prior delay frequency at the stadium; calibrated on historical games with documented delays since 2010. Forecast vintage within 6 hours of kickoff; update with live radar if allowed. Event definition per the series rules: any official weather delay, including a delayed start or any suspension or stoppage after kickoff, with no minimum duration.
free_sources: NOAA GOES-R GLM lightning data (free, SOURCE_UNVERIFIED archive convenience)
cfb.weather_delay_hazard.why: Replaces a wind-focused weather input with the hazard that actually determines the delay series.

cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.label: Net yards per play expectation (rush plus pass, sacks included)
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.mechanism: Expected team total yards from plays times net yards per play, built from rushing and passing components under NCAA accounting.
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.rationale: Total yards is plays times yards per play, and under NCAA conventions sack yardage lost is charged to rushing, so net yards per play depends on the sack rate; explosive plays create heavy right tails and yards correlate strongly with pace and script.
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.measurement: Per team: opponent-adjusted rush yards per attempt with sack and kneel yardage charged to rushing yards (the KXNCAAFTEAMYDS note confirms only this yardage accounting; it does not say sacks count as rush attempts, which does not change total yards), pass yards per attempt, run share expected from script; expected total yards = expected plays x [run share x rush ypc + pass share x (net pass ypa)]; opponent adjustments by opposing allowed values with 10-game window, 0.8 decay, k = 6 games shrinkage; dispersion from historical residuals by bucket. As-of last game.
free_sources: CFBD plays and team stats (free key)
cfb.net_yards_per_play_model.why: Gives the mean and spread of KXNCAAFTEAMYDS, which defines team yards as rushing plus receiving yards with sacks and kneels as negative rushing yards.

cfb.pace.reason: Plays bound yards, dropbacks and drives, but different counts depend on different parts of tempo (dropbacks for sacks and interceptions, drives for field goals); the single average plays per game should be split into dropbacks and drives for each series.

cfb.drives.reason: Drives are the opportunity unit for field goals and for some turnovers; needed for TOTALFG and TEAMFG, but incomplete without the drive-end distribution (reaching the 35, kicking, going for it).

cfb.pass_rush.reason: Pressure and sack rates for and against are the core of the sack series, but a quarterback's own sack proneness (holding the ball, scrambling) and the blitz rate are separate parts that the combined label hides.

cfb.turnover_luck.reason: Fumble recovery is about even odds, so recovered fumbles regress to expectation; essential for forced-turnover counts but meaningless for sacks or field goals, so its use is series-specific.

cfb.havoc.reason: Havoc combines tackles for loss, forced fumbles and pass breakups and is a stable defensive trait, useful for sacks and takeaways as a pooled measure; it is a derived blend of the components that individual series need separately.

cfb.kicker.reason: Kicker range and accuracy by distance are the make-probability half of the field-goal counts; the attempt half (how many drives end in kicks) is not covered by this input.

cfb.redzone.reason: Red-zone touchdown versus field-goal rate shifts attempts for FG counts and TD to FG conversion, but regresses heavily; it also affects two-point attempts only through the number of touchdowns.

cfb.script.reason: Score state drives pass volume (more sacks and interceptions when trailing) and two-point decisions; defined as rebuilt from own forecast, which avoids market circularity, but needs expected margin from ratings, not from quotes.

cfb.weather_pit.reason: Wind and temperature forecasts affect field-goal range and passing, but the weather-delay series needs lightning and thunderstorm probability specifically, which a wind-and-rain forecast vintage does not supply.

cfb.officials.reason: Crew tendencies add penalties and replay stoppages, with small effects on counts of sacks or field goals; a context variable only.

cfb.ot_model.reason: Overtime periods one and two count for yards, sacks, interceptions and turnovers and all overtime counts for made field goals, while two-point conversions in overtime are excluded; so it matters for most series and not for KXNCAAF2PT, which the existing label does not distinguish.

cfb.clock_rules.reason: The clock rule regime shifts plays per game for yards and counts by season, but is constant within a season; it is a stratifier for training data, not a game-level driver.

interactions.mechanism: Expected sacks equal dropbacks times pressure rate times sack-given-pressure, and a mobile quick-release quarterback cuts the third factor, so the pass rush's advantage is large only against a quarterback who holds the ball; the effect is multiplicative in the volume.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit sacks per game on dropbacks x pressure x QB sack-given-pressure terms; compare additive and multiplicative forms by held-out deviance.

interactions.mechanism: A field goal beyond about 40 yards is sharply less likely in a headwind of 15 mph or more, so wind turns long attempts into punts or fourth-down tries and both lowers makes and shifts attempts, which a make-rate adjustment alone misses.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare attempts and makes by distance bucket in windy versus calm games, split by kicker long-range accuracy.

interactions.mechanism: Two-point attempts occur after touchdowns and are concentrated in specific score-differential states (down 8, up 17, trailing late), so the count depends on touchdowns and on the state at the time; a team that scores often when trailing is likely to try more.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate attempt probability by score-differential state and period and compare with the predicted count for teams with different scoring and trailing profiles.

interactions.mechanism: A quarterback's observed interceptions carry little additional information beyond about 150 attempts once turnover-worthy play rate is known, and defensive havoc adds little to the interception rate beyond regression; forced-turnover counts are dominated by regression to the mean after the first handful of observations.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the regression coefficient of past INT rate by attempts played; test the incremental contribution of havoc to next-game interceptions.

interactions.mechanism: Delays cluster in afternoon and evening games in warm months at open stadiums; the hazard is near zero in domes and cold weather, and the regime depends on the season month and stadium type, so a single weather forecast variable is not enough.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute delay frequency by month, local time and roof status over past seasons; confirm the regime separation.

nonlinearities.shape: Rare-event logistic in forecast thunderstorm probability with an afternoon peak and a floor at zero for domes
nonlinearities.why: Delay probability stays under a few percent until thunderstorm probability is high, then rises quickly; domes break the relationship, so the response is not linear in forecast probability.

nonlinearities.shape: Make probability decreasing in distance with steeper fall beyond 45 yards and an interaction with wind
nonlinearities.why: A kicker's accuracy is high inside 35 yards and drops steeply beyond 45, so the count of made field goals depends on the distribution of distances, not only the number of attempts.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise in lead size: dropbacks rise when trailing by two scores and fall when leading
nonlinearities.why: Opportunity counts for sacks and interceptions respond non-linearly to the expected margin, so the same team gets very different counts in a blowout and a close game.
